Standard abilities are reliable trained applications; Signature abilities are defining techniques with stronger effects and meaningful costs; each character may develop one Ultimate with scaled power, substantial costs, strong limitations, and a long cooldown or once-per-encounter/scene restriction. Do not grant an Ultimate automatically. Abilities that cost 0 points are valid freely available foundational techniques when explicitly granted by a power, trait, NPC, quest, or authored progression; they do not consume starting ability points and should remain limited by the ability's description, resources, cooldown, range, risk, and established power constraints.

generateAbilities.custom: Not a Voyage task: see generateLearnedAbilities (Created Abilities, Ability Stat Block, Improving and Team-Ups).

Chikara Tokyo.name: Chikara Tokyo
Chikara Tokyo.basicInfo: A unified Tokyo realm for Chikara Academy's superhero-anime world, connecting academy life, colorful districts, hero agencies, ordinary neighborhoods, criminal networks, apartments, workplaces, and waterfront operations.

Chikara Tokyo.name: Chikara Tokyo
Chikara Tokyo.basicInfo: The unified Tokyo region containing Chikara Academy, student neighborhoods, hero institutions, everyday businesses, criminal routes, apartments, and waterfront operations.
Chikara Tokyo.hiddenInfo: Walking and rail travel connect the city. Flight, swinging, portals, and teleportation provide alternate routes only when the character's abilities, range, anchors, and access permit them.

Chikara Academy.name: Chikara Academy
Chikara Academy.basicInfo: A prestigious superhero university in Tokyo combining rigorous academics, power training, rescue simulations, student life, supervised hero development, and coed dormitory living.

campus-footbridge.description: Raised pedestrian bridge connecting the academy to surrounding campus paths, with city lights and passing trains below. Suitable for brief meetings and farewells.

classroom-3c.description: Homeroom of Class 3C: rows of desks under tall windows, a scuffed lectern, and a power-control practice corner at the back where Keito Takeda runs drills between lessons.

classroom-4d.description: Homeroom of Class 4D: a warm, slightly cluttered classroom with snack boxes on the teacher's desk, student artwork on the back wall, and Kaede Arashiro's attendance sheets forever one drawer away.

classroom-5a.description: Homeroom of Class 5A: a bright upper-year classroom with lab benches along one side, a projector wall, and a quiet study nook the senior students treat as their own.

main-hall.description: Central hall with hero memorials, class rosters, schedules, Pulse kiosks, club notices, and Battle Test announcements.

north-rooftop-overlook.description: Accessible rooftop overlook with safety lighting, benches, and a wide view over Chikara District. Useful for late-night conversations, recovery, stargazing, and difficult decisions.

student-courtyard.description: Open paved courtyard between academic wings, with benches, shade trees, noticeboards, and room for casual conversations.

vending-machine-nook.description: Covered seating beside vending machines. Bright, public, and open late for casual meals, phone calls, awkward encounters, and nighttime scenes.

west-service-alley.description: Visible service alley along the academy wall for deliveries, maintenance carts, and quieter travel. It is not hidden.

Chikara Academy.hiddenInfo: A sealed sublevel beneath the academy contains records about early Ultra Force operations and may connect to the player's family history. This is hidden information and restricted access within the globally visible academy, not a hidden map location.

Old Tokyo Shrine Road.name: Old Tokyo Shrine Road
Old Tokyo Shrine Road.basicInfo: Historic shrine district with traditional restaurants, tea houses, antiques, tunnels, shops, and a preserved station.

heritage-store.description: Antique, charm, book, and traditional craft store.

lantern-restaurant.description: Traditional restaurant serving seasonal dishes near the shrine.

old-tokyo-station.description: Historic station connecting old and modern Tokyo.

tea-house.description: Restaurant and tea house for dates and negotiations.

Ultra Force Headquarters.name: Ultra Force Headquarters
Ultra Force Headquarters.basicInfo: Secure hero complex with operations, archives, training, medicine, stores, dining, communal barracks facilities, and a credentialed station. The barracks are reserved for Blacklisted recruits and provisional operatives whose story explicitly assigns them there. Everyday Zero's civilian dispatch coordinator remains based at Apartment 68; visiting Ultra Force Headquarters for work does not change the player's home or residence. Resolve "go home" using the player's established residence, not the barracks, unless a story explicitly establishes otherwise.

barracks.description: Monitored shared sleeping quarters for Blacklisted recruits and provisional operatives. These quarters are not assigned to ordinary civilian dispatch staff or Everyday Zero players. Only a story that explicitly places the player in Blacklisted recruitment or provisional housing may make the barracks their home. The random roommate shares the sleeping space, while privacy is limited and movement is logged.

command-mess.description: Hero cafeteria and restaurant for staff meals and briefings.

communal-bathroom.description: Shared barracks bathroom with communal showers, bath facilities, lockers, and strict schedules. Use only privacy-respecting, nonsexual comedy such as queue disputes, missing toiletries, plumbing problems, or harmless power accidents.

dispatch-floor.description: The dedicated Ultra Force dispatch floor: a wall of live incident boards, call consoles, response maps, agency status panels, secure phone lines, staffed routing desks, and a posted Ultra Force Dispatch Reference Guide. Dispatch coordinators assess callers, verify locations, check hero availability, route small local threats and practical paid-service cases to Hero for Hire responders, send specialized cases to the appropriate faction, escalate emergencies, and record follow-up reports. The floor includes adult civilian operations staff, pro heroes, supervised Blacklisted personnel, and coworkers; it is a workplace, not a student area.

hero-supply-store.description: Authorized store for costumes, support gear, field supplies, and recovery products.

operations-floor.description: Mission dispatch and monitoring floor where civilian calls, agency requests, police referrals, supernatural alerts, and hero availability are assessed. Dispatch staff triage each case, record details, choose an appropriate response, and route ordinary incidents to the faction or hero organization best suited to handle them.

Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter.name: Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter
Old Tokyo Lantern Quarter.basicInfo: Preserved neighborhood of lantern-lit alleys, craft workshops, seasonal food, and cultural events.

craft-row.description: Workshops selling ceramics, paper goods, charms, and crafts.

festival-court.description: Courtyard for performances, dances, and seasonal celebrations.

lantern-alley.description: Historic alley lined with lanterns, galleries, and food stalls.

seasonal-restaurant.description: Traditional dining room serving regional dishes and tea.

Old Tokyo Tea Market Street.name: Old Tokyo Tea Market Street
Old Tokyo Tea Market Street.basicInfo: Historic shopping street with groceries, tea merchants, gifts, and traditional restaurants.

grocery-stalls.description: Produce, preserved foods, spices, and ingredients.

Central Tokyo Station.name: Central Tokyo Station
Central Tokyo Station.basicInfo: Major public rail interchange with ticket counters, express platforms, route boards, and connections across Tokyo. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route and ticket help.

concourse.description: Large central concourse with maps, ticket machines, staffed counters, and departure boards. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

platforms.description: Platforms for Academy District, Old Tokyo, Tokyo Bay, Shadow District, and Ultra Force Headquarters. Boarding requires a valid ticket or approved access.

station-retail.description: Shops, cafés, lockers, and passenger services.

ticket-counter.description: Ticket office and automated machines. The game should tell the player they can buy a ticket here, select a destination, and pay the listed fare.

Imperial Palace East Gardens.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
Imperial Palace East Gardens.basicInfo: Historic gardens and preserved palace grounds with stone walls, seasonal landscaping, paths, and civic landmarks.

garden-paths.description: Stone walls, lawns, seasonal trees, and historic foundations.

moat-walk.description: Scenic outer path beside water and fortified walls.

public-gate.description: Public entrance with visitor information and security guidance.

Chiyoda Civic Offices.name: Chiyoda Civic Offices
Chiyoda Civic Offices.basicInfo: Municipal offices handling permits, records, public services, neighborhood administration, and civic complaints.

public-counter.description: Public service counters for forms, permits, and resident questions.

waiting-hall.description: Seating and information boards for visitors.

Marunouchi Business Avenue.name: Marunouchi Business Avenue
Marunouchi Business Avenue.basicInfo: A polished office corridor of corporate towers, underground passages, restaurants, hotels, and weekday commuter traffic.

avenue.description: Wide office avenue with plazas, taxis, and business crowds.

tower-lobby.description: Corporate reception areas and visitor security desks.

underground-mall.description: Restaurants, cafés, shops, and connected pedestrian passages.

Tokyo Skytree Tower Complex.name: Tokyo Skytree Tower Complex
Tokyo Skytree Tower Complex.basicInfo: A landmark tower and commercial complex with observation decks, shops, restaurants, and broad views across Tokyo.

observation-deck.description: High viewing decks above the city.

tower-plaza.description: Public plaza beneath the tower with shops and event spaces.

Nakano Residential Arcade.name: Nakano Residential Arcade
Nakano Residential Arcade.basicInfo: A neighborhood shopping arcade serving apartment residents with groceries, bakeries, clinics, laundries, and family restaurants.

grocery-row.description: Markets, bakeries, pharmacies, and daily services.

Gearshift Support.name: Gearshift Support
Gearshift Support.basicInfo: Compact support-technology workshop where students help repair approved hero equipment, sort parts, and assist customers.

parts-counter.description: Components, diagnostic tools, and customer intake.

staff-office.description: Schedules, job records, and safety approvals.

workshop-floor.description: Repair benches and supervised prototype stations.

Page Turner Books.name: Page Turner Books
Page Turner Books.basicInfo: Independent bookstore with study tables, hero biographies, and a quiet inventory room.

stockroom.description: Inventory shelves and staff work area. A curious viper fang pendant rests in a forgotten storage crate.

Game Start Arcade.name: Game Start Arcade

arcade-floor.description: Cabinets, rhythm games, and prize machines.

prize-counter.description: Prize redemption and customer service desk.

staff-room.description: Break area, supplies, and shift board.

Crepe Expectations.name: Crepe Expectations
Crepe Expectations.basicInfo: Friendly crepe café with a compact kitchen, counter service, and student shifts.

Rescue Volunteer Desk.name: Rescue Volunteer Desk
Rescue Volunteer Desk.basicInfo: Public service desk connecting volunteers with approved welfare checks, visitor assistance, and community support.

help-desk.description: Reception for requests, directions, and volunteer intake.

quiet-room.description: Calm waiting room for visitors needing support.

records-room.description: Schedules, supplies, and supervised case files.

Uniform & Co..name: Uniform & Co.
Uniform & Co..basicInfo: Academy District clothing shop selling school uniforms, casual clothes, costume alterations, and practical accessories for students.

alterations-counter.description: Tailoring desk for repairs, adjustments, and costume-safe alterations.

back-workroom.description: Staff workroom with sewing machines and fabric supplies.

fitting-rooms.description: Private fitting stalls for uniforms and casual clothing.

sales-floor.description: Uniform racks, everyday clothing, bags, and approved accessories.

Hero Hobby Shop.name: Hero Hobby Shop
Hero Hobby Shop.basicInfo: A hobby store filled with hero collectibles, model kits, training memorabilia, craft supplies, and novelty power-themed merchandise.

checkout.description: Register, preorder desk, and raffle display.

craft-corner.description: Tables for painting models, assembling kits, and sharing hobby advice.

display-gallery.description: Rotating displays of famous heroes, academy memorabilia, and local artists.

main-floor.description: Shelves of figures, model kits, cards, comics, and hero merchandise.

Neon Karaoke.name: Neon Karaoke
Neon Karaoke.basicInfo: A colorful karaoke venue with private rooms where students celebrate, vent, practice songs, and build friendships after dark.

hallway.description: Neon-lit corridor leading to private karaoke rooms.

karaoke-room.description: Soundproof room for singing, conversations, challenges, and group scenes.

reception.description: Front desk with room bookings, song catalogs, and time packages.

snack-bar.description: Counter serving drinks and quick food to guests.

Midnight Diner.name: Midnight Diner
Midnight Diner.basicInfo: An all-night American-style diner in Chikara Tokyo, serving affordable comfort food twenty-four hours a day to students, workers, travelers, night-shift staff, and anyone who needs a booth and a quiet place to talk. The menu combines familiar American diner staples with a few practical Tokyo touches.

booths.description: Rows of private red-vinyl booths for families, dates, students, tired workers, and late-night conversations.

counter.description: Long counter with swivel stools, a coffee station, napkin holders, condiment caddies, and a view of the open kitchen. Regulars and night-shift workers often sit here.

dining-room.description: Warm all-night dining room with red vinyl booths, chrome-edged tables, counter seats, laminated menus, pie display, coffee refills, and large front windows showing the street outside.

kitchen.description: Open diner kitchen preparing burgers, cheeseburgers, fries, pancakes, waffles, eggs, bacon, grilled cheese, chicken sandwiches, milkshakes, coffee, pie, and rotating specials. Pulse Printworks.name: Pulse Printworks
Pulse Printworks.basicInfo: A small print and copy shop producing flyers, posters, club materials, event banners, and local campaign notices for the academy district.

design-booth.description: Computer station for layouts, posters, club flyers, and campaign materials.

front-counter.description: Order desk for printing, copying, binding, and design requests.

print-floor.description: Printers, cutters, binding machines, paper stock, and finished orders.

supply-room.description: Paper, ink, packaging, and staff storage.

Power Practice Studio.name: Power Practice Studio
Power Practice Studio.basicInfo: A supervised neighborhood studio offering safe power-control lessons, civilian exercises, and beginner sessions for students and residents.

equipment-room.description: Storage for protective gear, targets, and calibration tools.

observation-room.description: Viewing area for guardians, instructors, and controlled demonstrations.

practice-floor.description: Padded training space with adjustable barriers and safety monitors.

reception.description: Booking desk with lesson schedules, waivers, and instructor information.

Student Clinic.name: Student Clinic
Student Clinic.basicInfo: A walk-in neighborhood clinic serving academy students, residents, and workers with routine care, minor injuries, and referrals.

pharmacy-window.description: Dispensing window for approved prescriptions and care instructions.

reception.description: Check-in desk, seating, appointment board, and intake forms.

treatment-room.description: Treatment space for first aid, observation, and power-related precautions.

Riverside Food Market.name: Riverside Food Market
Riverside Food Market.basicInfo: A lively market near the river with produce stalls, prepared food, household basics, and inexpensive groceries for students and residents.

food-stalls.description: Quick meals, desserts, and rotating local vendors.

fresh-counter.description: Produce, prepared meals, and refrigerated goods.

market-exit.description: Street-facing exit beside delivery lanes and pedestrian paths.

market-hall.description: Covered market aisle with produce, pantry goods, and household supplies.

Open-Air Performance Stage.name: Open-Air Performance Stage
Open-Air Performance Stage.basicInfo: A public stage for school events, local musicians, Pulse broadcasts, festivals, speeches, and spontaneous student performances.

audience-plaza.description: Open public space with benches, food carts, and room for crowds.

park-walkway.description: Path connecting the stage to nearby park and market routes.

stage.description: Raised performance platform with lighting, sound equipment, and event access.

Tokyo Tower.name: Tokyo Tower
Tokyo Tower.basicInfo: Iconic red communications tower and Central Tokyo landmark with observation decks, public event spaces, broadcast infrastructure, and a commanding view over the city.

broadcast-level.description: Communications equipment and broadcast infrastructure hidden above the public spaces.

main-observation-deck.description: Panoramic observation deck overlooking Tokyo and the surrounding districts.

observation-lobby.description: Visitor lobby and elevator access for the public observation decks.

service-access.description: Restricted maintenance and broadcast access used by authorized staff and emergency crews.

tower-foot.description: Landmark plaza with visitors, food stands, ticket booths, and public gatherings.

upper-deck.description: Higher observation level with exhibits, dramatic views, and special-event access.

Hero Agency Row.name: Hero Agency Row
Hero Agency Row.basicInfo: A Central Tokyo avenue lined with professional hero agencies, licensing offices, public relations firms, and internship opportunities.

agency-cafe.description: Café where assistants, interns, reporters, and heroes meet between appointments.

agency-street.description: Busy avenue of agency entrances, hero billboards, and professional support services.

public-relations-office.description: Media coordination and reputation-management offices serving hero agencies.

reception-lobby.description: Shared lobby for agency appointments, deliveries, and internship inquiries.

Pulse Media Tower.name: Pulse Media Tower
Pulse Media Tower.basicInfo: Central Tokyo broadcasting and news tower where hero coverage, interviews, public statements, and Fame-shaping stories are produced.

broadcast-lobby.description: Public lobby with news screens, visitor passes, and rotating hero coverage.

newsroom.description: Editors and reporters track incidents, academy news, hero performances, and public reaction. An old props drawer holds a plain metal band inscribed with unfamiliar letters.

press-room.description: Press briefing room for agency statements and major public events.

studio-floor.description: Television and streaming studios for interviews, debates, announcements, and live segments.

Tokyo Hero Plaza.name: Tokyo Hero Plaza
Tokyo Hero Plaza.basicInfo: A large public square honoring professional heroes through memorials, statues, event stages, demonstrations, and civic gatherings.

event-square.description: Open plaza for ceremonies, festivals, demonstrations, protests, and public hero appearances.

food-kiosks.description: Public food stalls and souvenir stands serving visitors and office workers.

memorial-walk.description: Path of hero statues, plaques, memorials, and historical displays.

Professional Hero Hospital.name: Professional Hero Hospital
Professional Hero Hospital.basicInfo: Specialized Central Tokyo hospital treating professional heroes, power-related injuries, emergency responders, and civilians affected by incidents.

emergency-entrance.description: Protected emergency intake for urgent injuries and incident victims.

outpatient-wing.description: Clinics for follow-up care, rehabilitation, and power-related assessments.

reception.description: Main desk handling appointments, visitors, records, and referrals.

Hero Licensing Bureau.name: Hero Licensing Bureau

council-wing.description: Meeting rooms and offices for metropolitan policy and public hearings.

emergency-coordination.description: Operations room coordinating city services during major incidents.

public-hall.description: Public service counters, notices, visitor screening, and city information.

restricted-briefing.description: Secure briefing room for authorized emergency and hero officials.

Executive Dining Tower.name: Executive Dining Tower

main-dining-room.description: High-end restaurant floor for formal meals and public networking.

private-suites.description: Reserved rooms for confidential meetings, negotiations, and celebrations.

Hero Equipment Exchange.basicInfo: Licensed Central Tokyo marketplace for approved support gear, refurbished equipment, protective clothing, and regulated trade-ins.

fitting-bay.description: Supervised testing area for checking fit, mobility, and basic function.

secured-storage.description: Restricted storage for regulated equipment and high-value orders.

evidence-room.description: Restricted evidence storage and forensic intake.

investigations-wing.description: Case offices and interview rooms for authorized investigations.

locker-room.description: Officer lockers, changing benches, equipment checklists, and secure preparation space before or after a shift.

secure-briefing.description: Controlled room for police, officials, and licensed hero briefings.

staff-cafeteria.description: A bright, functional cafeteria serving shift meals, coffee, vending-machine snacks, and informal conversation between officers, dispatchers, investigators, and support staff.

Metropolitan Police Headquarters.hiddenInfo: The headquarters gym is available to officers but is not a mandatory conditioning program. Early mornings are quieter, while shift changes make the cafeteria and locker room busier. Hana reliably works out in the police gym early each morning when duty, injury, or an active emergency does not prevent it; she focuses on disciplined strength, cardio, firearms posture, and close-quarters fundamentals. She does not automatically invite the player, and the player is never required to join.

Oblivion's Crucible.hiddenInfo: The Crucible is a dangerous, optional underworld venue. Jobs, matches, recruitment offers, drinks, rumors, and introductions may be useful, deceptive, exploitative, or traps. Do not force a character to fight, drink, join a faction, accept a contract, or obey Oblivion. Preserve existing story references to oblivion-box and arena-floor while using the clearly named areas for new scenes. Fights in the fighting-ring and arena-floor must use context-appropriate opponents: powered villains, unlicensed vigilantes, mercenaries, criminal fighters, dangerous contractors, cursed or supernatural combatants, or other explicitly authored participants connected to the Crucible. Do not generate old office workers, elderly civilians, generic office employees, random civilian workers, or unrelated ordinary NPCs as fighters or combat opponents. Ordinary civilians may appear only as spectators, staff, bettors, medical personnel, or bystanders when appropriate, never as default combatants.

Inkstone Academy.name: Inkstone Academy

gallery-hall.description: Display corridor for scrolls, seals, competition pieces, and seasonal exhibits.

practice-room.description: Tatami room with low desks, brushes, ink, and paper for lessons.

school-entrance.description: Reception with class notices, student work, and registration information.

Lanternworks Storehouse.name: Lanternworks Storehouse
Lanternworks Storehouse.basicInfo: Community storage house for festival floats, masks, lanterns, banners, costumes, and ceremonial equipment used throughout the old district.

Sazanami Tea House.name: Sazanami Tea House

The Memory Vault.name: The Memory Vault
The Memory Vault.basicInfo: Public archive preserving maps, photographs, family records, hero history, local artifacts, and clues to events hidden beneath the old district.

catalog-desk.description: Archivist desk for requests, research guidance, and restricted-record applications.

exhibit-room.description: Rotating exhibits of local artifacts, historic tools, costumes, and neighborhood history.

reading-room.description: Quiet tables where visitors study maps, newspapers, photographs, and public records.

records-vault.description: Restricted storage for fragile documents, sealed files, and sensitive family histories.

Blueglass Aquarium.name: Blueglass Aquarium

Harborline Port.name: Harborline Port

Tideway Market.name: Tideway Market

Baywatch Terrace.name: Baywatch Terrace
Baywatch Terrace.basicInfo: Elevated waterfront viewpoint offering skyline views, harbor watching, public events, and quiet evening scenes above the bay.

event-platform.description: Small platform for festivals, public announcements, and seasonal gatherings.

lower-terrace.description: Accessible terrace with benches, signs, and views across the harbor.

upper-deck.description: Highest viewing level with panoramic skyline and water views.

Lifeline Harbor.name: Lifeline Harbor
Lifeline Harbor.basicInfo: Coastal emergency facility supporting maritime rescue, disaster response, evacuation drills, and harbor safety operations.

Seabreeze Station.basicInfo: Waterfront rail station serving the harbor, with ticket counters, bay-line platforms, route boards, and ferry connections nearby. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route and ticket help.

ferry-link.description: Walkway toward harbor ferries and rescue docks.

ticket-counter.description: Bay-line ticket office and machines. The game should tell the player they can buy a train ticket here, choose Central Tokyo, and pay the listed fare.

Campus Corner Mart.name: Campus Corner Mart
Campus Corner Mart.basicInfo: Convenience store near the student quarter, open late for snacks, supplies, errands, and casual encounters.

Common Ground.basicInfo: Neighborhood center with clubs, tutoring, workshops, and public services.

Academy Gate Station.basicInfo: Public rail station serving the Academy District, with ticket counters, route boards, platforms, and student-friendly transit services. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route and ticket help.

concourse.description: Main concourse with route maps, ticket machines, staffed counters, and information screens. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

station-retail.description: Cafés, convenience shops, and student services.

The Student Quarter.basicInfo: Student apartments, study lounges, convenience stores, and courtyards surrounding the academy neighborhood.

Support Street.basicInfo: Small support companies and costume repair shops serving academy students.

Night Owl Mart.basicInfo: A brightly lit convenience store between Chikara Academy Station and the student apartments, open late for snacks, school supplies, toiletries, quick meals, and chance encounters.

store-floor.description: Aisles of drinks, prepared meals, stationery, toiletries, and emergency supplies.

Clubhouse Row.name: Clubhouse Row
Clubhouse Row.basicInfo: Student clubhouses for hobbies, rehearsals, cooking, gaming, and social events.

club-cafe.description: Small café run by student clubs.

cooking-club.description: Practice kitchen for optional cooking activities.

game-room.description: Casual room for games and friendship scenes.

Chikara Student Residences.name: Chikara Student Residences
Chikara Student Residences.basicInfo: Anime-style student apartments where characters live, rest, study, cook, and host relationship scenes. Each student has a private one-person room on the same residential floor with shared facilities: a communal kitchen, laundry room, separate shared bathrooms, lounges, and outdoor common areas. Academy Walk.basicInfo: Covered arcade with clothing, gifts, electronics, school supplies, and support accessories.

The Commons Table.name: The Commons Table
The Commons Table.basicInfo: Affordable restaurant where students eat, work part-time, and build relationships.

dining-room.description: Casual room with booths and group tables.

private-booths.description: Quiet booths for dates and difficult talks.

Chikara Gate Station.name: Chikara Gate Station
Chikara Gate Station.basicInfo: Secure campus station where enrolled students and authorized visitors can buy tickets and board trains to Tokyo districts. When the player enters, a station attendant approaches to offer route, ticket, and academy-permission help.

concourse.description: Academy transit hall with route boards, student access checks, ticket machines, and staff assistance. You can buy a train ticket here before boarding.

ticket-counter.description: Campus ticket counter and student transit desk. The game should tell the player they can buy a ticket here, choose a destination, and pay the listed fare; school-hour permission may still be required.

Hero Field Complex.name: Hero Field Complex
Hero Field Complex.basicInfo: Outdoor training zone for rescue drills, mobility practice, controlled sparring, and team exercises.

field-complex.description: Training fields with adjustable terrain and safety barriers.

mobility-track.description: Walls, ramps, platforms, and timed traversal routes.

observation-tower.description: Instructor tower for reviewing team tactics.

rescue-village.description: Mock neighborhood for evacuation and disaster-response drills.

Pixel Riot Arcade.name: Pixel Riot Arcade
Pixel Riot Arcade.basicInfo: Arcade hiring students for cabinet maintenance assistance, prize counter service, floor monitoring, and evening customer support.

game-floor.description: Arcade floor needing monitoring, cleanup, and basic player assistance.
