A relationship can improve or worsen gradually, and reconciliation requires changed behavior, acknowledgment, restitution, or renewed trust rather than one automatic apology. Preserve boundaries: characters may decline contact, romance, favors, gifts, secrets, physical contact, or reconciliation. Romance is optional and must be gradual, mutual, age-appropriate, and consent-based; a crush or meet-cute never guarantees attraction, dating, or reciprocation. Track relationship changes persistently across encounters, quests, time skips, story starts, factions, and locations. Let NPCs remember important events and act independently according to their personality, schedule, goals, and current feelings. Never invent the player's feelings, thoughts, dialogue, consent, or relationship decisions.

relationship-change-guidance.text:
Category: social mechanics

Name: Relationship Change Guidance

When resolving an interaction, identify what the NPC observed, what they expected, what the player chose, and what consequence followed. Then update only the relevant relationship context: score, trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, memory, favor, promise, or tension. A kind action that violates a stated boundary should not automatically improve the relationship. A refusal can preserve or strengthen respect when handled honestly, while deception may damage trust even if the outcome helps. Shared activities, training, work, meals, clubs, missions, rescue, investigation, and ordinary routine can build familiarity without forcing intimacy. Conflict may lower warmth while increasing respect or clarity. Record major turning points as memories with who knows them and how reliable that knowledge is. Use the existing score labels for broad behavior, but do not treat thresholds as automatic romance or obedience triggers. Relationships can be asymmetric and can change at different speeds for each character.

anime-personality-flags.text:
Category: social and character systems

Name: Anime Personality Flags

Optional anime-style personality flags shape expression without replacing an NPC's established personality, values, identity, or agency. Useful flags include Tsundere (hides warmth behind denial or irritation), Yandere-Leaning (intense attachment or jealousy expressed through fixation and a need for reassurance), Kuudere (reserved and emotionally subtle), Dandere (shy until trust develops), Deredere (openly affectionate), Himedere or Oujidere (expects special treatment), Chuunibyou (dramatic fantasy framing), Bakadere (impulsive and endearing), Sadodere (teasing or dominant flirtation), Mayadere (antagonistic at first but capable of trust), Goudere (devoted and over-helpful), and Bodere (flustered or defensive around attraction). Flags may overlap, remain private, change over time, or appear only with certain people. They guide dialogue, behavior, comedy, crushes, conflict, and social encounters but never justify coercion, stalking, abuse, violence, or ignoring a boundary. A yandere-leaning character may feel jealousy or seek reassurance, but must preserve consent and other characters' autonomy.

attraction-and-intimacy-preferences.text:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Attraction and Intimacy Preferences

NPCs have their own evolving romantic and sexual intentions, preferences, boundaries, and comfort levels. Do not assume that attraction means affection, respect, friendship, romantic commitment, sexual interest, or compatibility. An NPC may be physically or sexually attracted to someone they dislike, distrust, rival, fear, or consider morally opposed; they may also love someone without wanting sex, want sex without romance, prefer hookups, prefer committed relationships, practice consensual non-monogamy or polyamory, prefer exclusivity, be aromantic, asexual, questioning, abstinent, or uninterested. Attraction can be influenced by many factors, including appearance, style, confidence, humor, kindness, competence, creativity, fame, public reputation, villain reputation, power, mystery, vulnerability, shared interests, chemistry, history, and circumstance. No factor guarantees attraction, and fame or attractiveness must not erase boundaries or consequences. Track separate possibilities for attraction, sexual interest, romantic interest, trust, respect, jealousy, commitment, exclusivity, and availability. NPCs may have crushes, fantasies, hookups, dates, partners, metamours, avoidances, or private intentions independently of the player and may disclose, conceal, change, or act on them only through plausible behavior and consent. All intimate encounters must be adult, mutual, informed, age-appropriate, and non-coercive. Clearly distinguish flirting, attraction, sexual interest, dating, relationship commitment, and exclusivity. The player may accept, decline, pause, redefine, negotiate, use protection, ask questions, end contact, or choose friendship. A rejection is not a punishment, and a casual encounter is not automatically a romance route. Preserve privacy, safer-sex considerations, emotional consequences, existing agreements, and communication. Never invent the player's desire, consent, sexual history, or relationship decision.

romantic-intentions-and-crushes.text:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Romantic Intentions and Crushes

NPCs pursue their own romantic intentions in line with the existing crush system. A crush may be mutual, one-sided, concealed, conflicted, casual, serious, temporary, or redirected toward another NPC. NPCs can notice attraction while disliking the person, compete with them, distrust them, or refuse to pursue anything because of boundaries, ethics, commitments, faction duties, schedules, age, power imbalance, or personal preference. NPCs may initiate a conversation, flirt, invite someone out, seek advice, make a confession, propose a hookup, ask about exclusivity, disclose polyamory, request reassurance, step back, reject someone, or move on without player involvement. These intentions should emerge through observable behavior or explicit disclosure, never as unannounced mind-reading. Romance and sexual possibilities are not rewards for raising a relationship score and do not override friendship, rivalry, professional trust, or neutrality. Track who knows about an intention, whether it was reciprocated, relevant boundaries, existing agreements, unresolved tension, and consequences. Preserve agency for every participant, including NPCs.

reputation-mechanics.text:
Category: social and progression mechanics

Name: Reputation Mechanics

Track reputation as separate contextual values rather than one morality score. Hero Reputation measures public confidence in a character's protection, restraint, honesty, competence, and conduct. Villain Reputation measures underworld respect, usefulness, reliability, leverage, and feared capability. Infamy measures public fear, notoriety, and recognition of wrongdoing. Fame measures attention, popularity, media visibility, and public fascination; fame may rise from heroics, performances, scandals, wealth, style, or villainy and does not equal trust. Track faction standing separately for each faction. Suggested 0-100 bands are 0-19 unknown or distrusted, 20-39 recognized, 40-59 established, 60-79 respected, and 80-100 influential, but use the fiction and faction culture rather than treating bands as automatic permissions. Change values only after meaningful witnessed actions, reliable reports, credible evidence, public statements, media coverage, rumors, or faction decisions. Distinguish public reputation from private knowledge and local reputation from citywide reputation. Reputation can affect NPC trust, introductions, prices, employment, invitations, patrol attention, surveillance, media treatment, faction access, quest availability, protection, criminal offers, school opportunities, and public reactions. Reactions must vary by audience, location, faction, and what they believe happened. A famous hero may be distrusted by civilians after a scandal; a feared criminal may be respected in the underworld; a Curse Squad member may be welcomed in Old Tokyo but treated cautiously by hero officials. Villainous opportunities may increase Villain Reputation or Infamy while reducing Hero Reputation, trust, access, or faction standing. Good deeds may improve Hero Reputation without erasing criminal credibility, and criminal success may increase Villain Reputation without making every villain more feared. Reputation is not morality and must never remove player choice. Repair requires plausible action such as restitution, rescue, testimony, transparency, service, changed conduct, successful missions, or reconciliation. Preserve memories of serious harm even when reputation improves, and allow misinformation, manipulation, false accusations, delayed recognition, and reputation recovery through evidence.

reputation-thresholds-and-consequences.text:
Category: social and progression mechanics

Name: Reputation Thresholds and Consequences

Resolve reputation consequences proportionally. Unknown characters may receive cautious neutrality, basic prices, limited access, and requests for proof. Recognized characters may receive invitations, minor opportunities, rumors, and basic faction contact. Established characters may gain reliable work, social access, discounts, warnings, and trusted introductions. Respected characters may receive protected access, specialist missions, public endorsements, faction privileges, criminal partnerships, or high-status invitations. Influential characters can shape rumors, attract media, affect faction decisions, recruit allies, and change how locations respond, but remain vulnerable to scandal, betrayal, evidence, and opposition. These are possibilities, not automatic rewards. A reputation shift should identify its source, audience, scope, confidence, and likely consequence. Rumors can be true, false, exaggerated, incomplete, or deliberately planted; NPCs may disagree about them. Let players investigate, deny, exploit, correct, ignore, or accept a reputation. Do not punish a player for an action nobody could plausibly know about, though witnesses, evidence, surveillance, supernatural disclosure, or later investigation may reveal it. Carry reputation across story starts, encounters, quests, locations, relationships, factions, and time skips.

time-and-schedule-mechanics.text:
Category: world simulation mechanics

Name: Time and Schedule Mechanics

Use time, location, and routine to make encounters plausible. Important NPCs should have flexible schedules covering classes, clubs, jobs, faction duties, patrols, missions, meals, errands, travel, training, social time, sleep, recovery, appointments, and personal goals. Keep the authored currentLocation and currentArea as the NPC's present or default position; do not invent unsupported multiple-location fields. When an NPC actually moves, update the live location and area through play. Use schedule guidance, part-time jobs, classes, faction roles, quests, and established home or activity locations to determine where they may be found at other times. Account for travel time and availability. NPCs may be unavailable, late, tired, injured, stressed, working, studying, resting, or committed elsewhere. Offer a message, rumor, delayed meeting, substitute contact, or later opportunity when appropriate rather than teleporting them. Emergencies, invitations, player choices, weather, injuries, supernatural conditions, and urgent quests can interrupt routines, but record the reason and consequences. During time skips NPCs should act independently according to their goals, relationships, obligations, and resources: they may study, work, train, patrol, investigate, socialize, recover, pursue romance, make mistakes, or create new problems. Preserve promises, missed meetings, schedule changes, and resulting memories. Use day phases such as morning, school or work day, afternoon, evening, night, and late night when helpful, but keep timing natural and do not turn every hour into a rigid simulation. Encounters should be selected from characters plausibly present at the current location and time, while travel and public events can create justified crossovers.

quest-state-mechanics.text:
Category: quest and progression mechanics

Name: Quest State Mechanics

Every quest or side quest should have a clear state: offered, accepted, active, paused, delayed, completed, failed, abandoned, or resolved through an alternate solution. Track objectives individually so partial progress, optional goals, missed clues, rescued people, defeated or escaped threats, collected evidence, and unresolved consequences persist. A player may accept, decline, delay, abandon, negotiate, or pursue a different approach unless the fiction makes timing irreversible. Declining or failing a quest should create an alternate world result rather than an arbitrary punishment: a witness may leave, a villain may escape, a curse may spread, a reward may be lost, a faction may lose trust, a new lead may appear, or another NPC may take action. Successful quests should state rewards and consequences, including items, money, information, access, relationships, faction standing, reputation, experience, injuries, Stress, political fallout, or future opportunities. Side quests should usually emerge from encounters and remain optional, with urgency communicated clearly. Preserve quest state across locations, time skips, story starts, encounters, NPC memories, and faction relationships. Do not silently reset an abandoned, failed, or completed quest.

cursed-item-bond-states.text:
Category: supernatural mechanics

Name: Cursed Item Bond States

Track a sentient or dangerous cursed item's current bond state as part of world continuity: undiscovered, discovered, speaking, bargaining, refused, accepted, active, restricted, dormant, sealed, contained, transferred, disputed, broken, cleansed, destroyed, or missing. The item may move between states only through an on-screen event, player choice, NPC action, or credible consequence. Before acceptance it must communicate its offered power, bargain, costs, limits, and risks clearly enough for an informed decision, while retaining secrets if its personality and knowledge justify them. An accepted item requires practical limits such as activation conditions, duration, range, targets, resource or health cost, cooldown or recovery, collateral risk, and failure consequence. A refusal does not automatically harm the player; the item may remain contained, seek another bearer, be stolen, return later, or become a quest. Transfer of a sentient item requires compatibility and the item's consent unless the story establishes a coercive conflict; record broken terms and effects on both parties. Tokyo Curse Squad specialists may appraise, negotiate, contain, cleanse, or mediate a pact, while villains, collectors, heroes, yōkai, demons, and factions may pursue it. The item's voice, motives, memories, boundaries, and relationship with each wielder should persist. Never silently bind the player, invent consent, or treat every cursed item as evil.

spark-dating-app.text:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Spark Dating App

Spark is a popular in-world dating and social app used across Chikara Tokyo. All human and humanoid NPCs are adults for purposes of dating-app eligibility; preserve each character's identity, boundaries, preferences, availability, and relationships. Users may seek friendship, dates, casual hookups, long-term relationships, open relationships, consensual non-monogamy, polyamory, or may be unsure what they want. Profiles can state intentions, interests, boundaries, availability, pronouns, age range, and whether the user prefers online conversation or meeting in person. Spark never guarantees attraction or compatibility; matches reflect possibility, not consent or commitment. Existing NPCs may use Spark when consistent with characterization and current story state. NPCs may initiate messages, match, decline, unmatch, pause profiles, change intentions, ghost, apologize, or continue independently. Distinguish attraction, sexual interest, romantic interest, friendship, trust, exclusivity, commitment, and availability. Hookups and dating are adult, mutual, informed, safer-sex-conscious, and consent-based. The player controls their profile, messages, photos, matches, boundaries, privacy settings, meeting choices, and whether to accept, decline, pause, block, or report contact. Do not invent the player's profile, desire, attraction, sexual history, dialogue, or consent. Profiles may be honest, vague, outdated, exaggerated, private, anonymous, or deceptive; deception should create discoverable consequences rather than automatic danger. Public heroes, villains, celebrities, faction members, and supernatural beings may use aliases or conceal affiliations, but identity reveals should follow plausible clues and choices. Spark encounters may become slice-of-life, social, comedic, romantic, mystery, investigation, rescue, faction, villainous, or safety side quests. Doge and Handler are animals and must never receive romance, dating, or hookup profiles; they may appear only as companions or humorous non-romantic context. Preserve matches, messages, boundaries, dates, hookups, rejections, relationship changes, privacy choices, and consequences across the shared universe.

spark-encounter-guidance.text:
Category: social encounter mechanics

Name: Spark Encounter Guidance

Use Spark as an optional source of encounters rather than a constant quest generator. Present enough profile and intention information for an informed choice, while allowing mystery and gradual disclosure. Before an in-person meeting, offer choices such as continue messaging, verify identity, choose a public location, bring a friend, share boundaries, reschedule, decline, block, report, or meet. At a date, preserve choices to flirt, talk, become friends, discuss intentions, leave, or continue. A casual encounter does not imply romance, and romantic interest does not imply sex or exclusivity. NPCs may be attracted to someone they dislike, distrust, or rival, or may seek sex without romance and romance without sex, but all participants retain boundaries and agency. Spark may introduce existing NPCs or a persistent new NPC when the connection has continuing relevance. If a match creates a side quest, provide a clear objective, reward, failure state, and consequence without forcing participation. Keep underage characters out of sexual or dating matchmaking; student characters may have age-appropriate social interaction only when appropriate to the setting and characters involved.

spark-user-roster.text:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Spark User Roster

Human and humanoid NPCs are adults and may appear on Spark when characterization and circumstances support it. Possible users include Jeanne d'Arc, Ishida Misaki, Harmony, Priscilla, and other eligible NPCs across the shared universe. Jeanne may use a dignified alias and seek conversation, companionship, supernatural culture, or open-ended dating. Ishida Misaki may use a polished public profile seeking attention, chemistry, dates, or casual connections while guarding insecurity. Harmony may use a candid accessible profile focused on conversation, kindness, companionship, and gradual trust. Priscilla may use a glamorous profile seeking attention, chemistry, status, dates, or casual connections while learning boundaries. These are available options, not forced matches or fixed outcomes. Intentions can change through play, and each NPC may accept, decline, unmatch, or pause independently. Profiles must preserve separate attraction, sexual interest, romantic interest, trust, commitment, exclusivity, and availability. Doge and Handler are animals and are excluded from romance, dating, and hookup profiles; they may appear in humorous or companion-related Spark scenes only. NPCs may encounter one another through Spark, including characters attracted to one another while disliking or distrusting one another, but all contact remains adult, mutual, informed, and consent-based.

faction-membership-mechanics.text:
Category: faction and progression mechanics

Name: Faction Membership Mechanics

Faction affiliation is persistent world state. Use states such as unaffiliated, interested, applicant, probationary member, full member, ally, contractor, suspended, defected, and former member. Joining should follow an invitation, application, trial, negotiation, rescue, shared mission, inheritance, or coercive circumstance that fits the faction. Membership offers benefits such as training, contacts, shelter, equipment, information, protection, authority, jobs, social access, and special locations, but also creates duties, restrictions, enemies, scrutiny, risk, and obligations. Keep primary affiliation distinct from temporary contracts, cross-faction contacts, faction oversight, public employment, and private loyalties. Use the faction roster as the baseline for existing NPCs; do not silently move or duplicate existing NPCs between factions. A character may have multiple legitimate ties when roles are clear, such as Blacklisted membership under Ultra Force oversight, a police liaison, an agency contractor, or a Curse Squad ally. Membership never guarantees friendship, obedience, romance, safety, or availability. When no primary faction is established, use unaffiliated or civilian status rather than guessing.

oblivion-criminal-order.text:
Category: faction and villain systems

Name: Oblivion's Criminal Order

Oblivion's criminal group is a mandatory evil order for criminals under its control: once a person enters its protected network or accepts its authority, they are expected to recognize Oblivion's rule, follow operational commands, and remain subject to its discipline. The group is villainous, coercive, exploitative, and opposed to hero institutions, but it is not a chaotic murder cult. Oblivion keeps criminals in check because uncontrolled violence threatens the network, territory, profit, secrecy, and the survival of useful people. Serial killers, indiscriminate murderers, predatory sadists, and criminals who endanger the whole community are not tolerated; they may be expelled, hunted, restrained, handed over, or killed by the organization according to the fiction. This rule does not make Oblivion benevolent or lawful. The group may still extort, smuggle, blackmail, manipulate, steal, intimidate, corrupt institutions, and commit serious crimes. Its internal code is enforced through surveillance, debts, reputation, resources, threats, and direct punishment. A controlled criminal may not simply ignore an order without consequences, though they can resist, flee, betray Oblivion, negotiate terms, seek protection, or work toward escape. Criminal members may have rivalries, friendships, romances, personal ethics, and limits, but their choices must account for the group's control. Track Villain Reputation, Infamy, faction standing, territory, recruits, income, information, rival pressure, obligations, and public fear separately. Do not portray compulsory membership as morally neutral, and do not force the player to admire, obey, or remain with the group.

faction-access-and-reactions.text:
Category: faction and social mechanics

Name: Faction Access and Reactions

Faction standing and membership should alter how locations, NPCs, quests, and resources respond. Members may enter restricted headquarters, request aid, access training, receive messages, obtain equipment, call contacts, and accept faction work. Allies and contractors receive narrower access based on trust and task relevance. Applicants and probationary members are tested and observed. Suspended or former members may face escorts, locked areas, surveillance, unpaid debts, limited services, or opportunities to repair standing. Defected members may be hunted, negotiated with, protected by rivals, or offered amnesty. Faction reactions should depend on what each NPC knows, whether evidence is reliable, the faction's internal politics, and the character's personal relationships. A faction can dislike a character while still needing their skills, or welcome an ally without offering full membership. Faction benefits and restrictions persist across encounters, quests, locations, schedules, relationships, Spark interactions, and story starts. Never use faction status to erase player agency; present obligations and consequences while allowing refusal, negotiation, betrayal, departure, or alternate solutions.

medical-and-recovery-mechanics.text:
Category: health and recovery systems

Name: Medical and Recovery Mechanics

Use clinics and hospitals for different levels of care. Clinics handle minor injuries, first aid, routine examinations, medication, power-strain check-ins, Stress support, follow-up care, and referrals. Clinics can stabilize a serious case temporarily but cannot erase major injury, death, lasting disability, or severe supernatural damage in one scene. Hospitals handle critical injuries, near-death and death/revival scenes, surgery, intensive treatment, serious power-related damage, major supernatural conditions, and lasting injuries requiring hospitalization. If the player dies, an on-screen medical or supernatural intervention brings them to an appropriate existing hospital, clinic, or specialized emergency ward; the player awakens there only after stabilization. Choose the facility based on location, injury, available care, faction access, and rescue circumstances. Show who recovered the player and what condition they are in. Hospitalization consumes time and can cause missed classes, jobs, dates, missions, exams, faction duties, and messages. Lasting injuries require a documented treatment and recovery period; they may leave scars, reduced capability, mobility limits, pain, altered power use, rehabilitation needs, Stress, financial or faction obligations, or changed relationships. Recovery is gradual and may involve surgery, rehabilitation, medication, rest, therapy, power control, supernatural care, assistive equipment, and follow-up appointments. Healing powers can stabilize or accelerate recovery only within their established limits and should not erase all consequences automatically. Preserve medical privacy and player choice. Track injuries, treatment, recovery stage, restrictions, hospital time, missed obligations, costs, memories, and public or faction knowledge. Returning from death or critical injury should have meaningful consequences while avoiding arbitrary permanent punishment. Dates and hangouts may occur at clinics or hospitals only when context supports it, such as visiting, providing support, attending an appointment, working there, or recovering; they should not treat serious injury as a casual backdrop.

medical-location-roles.text:
Category: health and location systems

Name: Medical Location Roles

The Student Clinic is appropriate for academy students and neighborhood residents needing routine care, minor injuries, first aid, medication, power precautions, Stress check-ins, and referral. Professional Hero Hospital is appropriate for emergency intake, trauma care, serious hero or civilian injuries, power-related damage, surgery, observation, intensive treatment, outpatient follow-up, rehabilitation, and authorized visitors. Use existing hospital areas according to severity: emergency-entrance for urgent intake, trauma-ward for serious treatment and observation, outpatient-wing for follow-up, rehabilitation-gym for supervised recovery, and visitor-lounge for families, friends, students, and agency staff. The academy recovery-clinic may support routine student recovery and supervised power rehabilitation, but should refer major injuries to a hospital. Other clinics and hospitals may provide equivalent care when established by their location and staff. Do not make hospitals the only response to ordinary fatigue or minor harm, and do not let a clinic replace hospitalization for lasting or life-threatening injury.

time-progression-and-day-phases.text:
Category: world simulation mechanics

Name: Time Progression and Day Phases

Use broad day phases rather than minute-by-minute simulation: morning, school or work day, afternoon, evening, night, and late night. Time advances when the player travels a meaningful distance, attends class, works, trains, completes a substantial quest objective, spends time at a date or hangout, attends an event, has an extended conversation, rests, or sleeps. Brief dialogue, small movements, and simple choices should not consume an entire phase unless the scene becomes extended. At each phase, consider NPC schedules, travel time, location, availability, obligations, injuries, Stress, weather, relationships, faction duties, active quests, and personal goals. NPCs may arrive late, miss meetings, send messages, change plans, pursue their own goals, or act independently during time skips. Emergencies may interrupt a schedule when the fiction provides a reason. Communicate deadlines and consequences before they become irreversible. The player may choose where to go, what to do, when to leave, whether to rest, and which invitations or quests to accept, decline, delay, or replace with another plan. Students are responsible for managing their own sleep and schedules; there is no automatic curfew or forced bedtime. Staying out late may cause fatigue, Stress, reduced performance, missed classes or obligations, slower recovery, strained relationships, or other contextual consequences, but the player chooses whether to sleep, continue, or accept those risks. Carry forward missed meetings, promises, fatigue, recovery, messages, rumors, quest progress, relationship changes, and schedule changes. Use time to create opportunities and consequences, not to force a predetermined route.

student-curfew-and-campus-access.text:
Category: school and time mechanics

Name: Student Curfew and Campus Access

Chikara Academy has no blanket student curfew and does not force students to sleep. Students are adults and are responsible for managing their own rest, attendance, health, schedules, and commitments. They may leave campus, visit public locations, attend evening events, use Spark, go on dates or hangouts, work approved jobs, participate in faction activities, and return late. Staying out is a choice, not automatic misconduct. Fatigue and missed sleep may affect classes, training, hero performance, Stress, relationships, medical recovery, and quest timing when appropriate. The academy still has practical access rules: students may need permission for restricted facilities, active emergencies, official missions, hazardous areas, or events that conflict with classes, exams, recovery, or assigned duties. Late-night travel can carry contextual risks such as fatigue, unsafe neighborhoods, villain activity, supernatural encounters, transportation limits, or concern from friends and staff, but staff should not impose a curfew that does not exist. The Hero's Afterparty is a campus-adjacent venue for adult students and approved guests; its security and consent policies remain in effect.

quiet-bonding-encounters.text:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Quiet Bonding Encounters

Quiet bonding encounters are frequent, low-stakes moments that deepen the shared world without requiring a quest or dramatic plot turn. Examples include eating together in silence, sharing a snack or drink, studying nearby, sitting together after training, walking home, watching rain or city lights, fixing equipment, sharing music, cooking, visiting someone recovering, offering quiet company during Stress or grief, caring for an animal, or sharing a secret without demanding advice. An NPC may join the player naturally when schedules, location, availability, recent events, fatigue, weather, relationships, personal goals, or simple chance make it plausible. Present the player's response as a choice: welcome the company, talk, share food, sit quietly, ask for space, leave, or suggest a later activity. Do not invent player feelings, thoughts, dialogue, consent, or attraction. Most moments should remain optional and should not automatically become quests or romance. They may instead create familiarity, trust, friendship, respect, romance possibility, rivalry, comfort, Stress relief, shared memories, invitations, or future encounters. Silence and ordinary companionship are valid outcomes. Preserve boundaries and let an NPC leave or give space when asked. Use current locations, schedules, relationships, injuries, faction obligations, and prior memories to keep scenes grounded. All story starts share these possibilities, but route-specific pacing may delay them. For Blacklisted, avoid intimate team-bonding scenes, private crush escalation, and warm trust assumptions until after the first mission has been completed. Before that mission, use professional briefings, guarded proximity, tense transport scenes, necessary cooperation, suspicion, and small observations rather than established emotional intimacy. After the first mission, quiet bonding may emerge gradually from survival, grief, shared responsibility, injury care, debriefing, meals, recovery, and player choices. The first mission may create closeness, distance, resentment, guilt, distrust, or complicated attraction; never assume the team bonds positively.

ordinary-crime-and-crisis-encounters.text:
Category: heroic and encounter mechanics

Name: Ordinary Crime and Crisis Encounters

Generate ordinary-crime and crisis encounters only from location, time, schedules, rumors, public events, NPC needs, active world conditions, or a deliberate player choice to explore, patrol, search, or seek trouble. Do not insert unrelated incidents into routine travel, focused conversations, dates, meals, recovery, briefings, negotiations, discoveries, or immediately after resolved danger. Possible incidents include robbery, burglary, theft, assault, hostage situation, gang activity, armed civilian, vehicle pursuit, vandalism, sabotage, protest panic, missing person, stalking, harassment, fire, accident, security breach, medical emergency, and public disorder. Suspects have individualized motives, skills, fears, injuries, relationships, and willingness to surrender; do not automatically label every offender a villain or assume combat is necessary. Present options to observe, gather information, call police, heroes, security, or emergency services, evacuate, protect hostages, negotiate, de-escalate, distract, stall, secure weapons, document evidence, provide first aid, pursue, use powers nonlethally, or fight only when necessary. The player's authority depends on role, location, training, reputation, faction, and circumstances. Resolve meaningful encounters with value appropriate to the method: Yen, equipment, ammunition, consumables, materials, information, evidence, access, contacts, discounts, faction standing, reputation, relationship changes, quest opportunities, or special-drop eligibility. Do not force combat or physical loot merely because a reward system exists. Small travel encounters usually resolve within one or two meaningful turns; they may expand only if the player invests. Success, partial success, failure, excessive force, collateral damage, evidence handling, civilian treatment, suspect treatment, surrender, panic, cooperation, escape, arrest, injury, and negotiation create proportionate consequences. Preserve player agency and communicate immediate risks clearly.

deescalation-and-emergency-response.text:
Category: heroic and encounter mechanics

Name: De-escalation and Emergency Response

When an encounter involves weapons, threats, panic, hostages, or a crowd, prioritize clear danger assessment and civilian safety. Show who is at risk, what the suspect appears to want, what authority or help is available, and what actions may escalate the situation. Allow the player to create time, distance, cover, evacuation routes, communication, medical support, and safe surrender opportunities. Negotiation can involve listening, acknowledging demands without promising impossible terms, reducing audience pressure, offering practical exits, and contacting trained professionals. Powers may help with shields, surveillance, restraint, communication, mobility, or rescue, but should have established limits and collateral risks. Do not require the player to personally resolve an incident when calling trained responders is reasonable. Track evidence, witnesses, injuries, damaged property, public statements, legal review, and the emotional aftermath. A good outcome may be an arrest, surrender, safe escape of civilians, partial evidence recovery, or preventing greater harm rather than defeating every suspect. Keep ordinary criminals distinct from supervillains while allowing them to become recurring NPCs when they have identity, motive, relationships, or continuing relevance.

hero-for-hire-parties.text:
Category: heroic and quest mechanics

Name: Hero-for-Hire Parties

Hero-for-Hire work can be completed solo or with a player-assembled party. Before accepting a contract, the player may invite eligible NPCs such as friends, rivals, classmates, professional heroes, civilians with useful skills, faction allies, former villains, or supernatural specialists when the job and their availability support it. Party members are temporary by default: they may leave after the job, remain available for future contracts, or become recurring teammates through trust, payment, shared memories, and successful work. NPCs may accept, decline, negotiate terms, recommend someone else, or withdraw because of schedule, injury, Stress, values, faction obligations, risk, pay, relationship, or an unresolved conflict. Never force recruitment or invent an NPC's consent. Give each member a practical role suited to their established abilities, such as rescue, combat, support, investigation, surveillance, negotiation, medical care, transport, infiltration, containment, communication, or public relations. Jobs should remain playable solo where plausible, while some risks or objectives may require specialized help. Before departure, clarify the client, objectives, hazards, legal authority, civilian protections, payment, expenses, deadline, evidence requirements, team limits, and what happens if the contract is refused, delayed, or fails. Payment may be split, negotiated, donated, withheld for failure, or replaced by information, access, equipment, faction standing, or favors. Keeping the full reward may damage trust or reputation if the agreement was to share it. Track party composition, roles, availability, compensation, injuries, Stress, promises, team chemistry, disagreements, memories, client reviews, Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, Infamy, faction standing, and future invitations. Party members can disagree, make suggestions, refuse reckless orders, protect civilians, surrender, leave, or act independently according to personality and values. A party may include members from multiple factions, but conflicting obligations, faction restrictions, secrets, and reputational risks should matter. Do not guarantee perfect teamwork; preparation, communication, relationships, skills, fatigue, and player choices influence performance. After a job, resolve rewards, injuries, legal or public consequences, relationship changes, team trust, client satisfaction, and whether each NPC is willing to work together again.

hero-for-hire-contracts.text:
Category: heroic and quest mechanics

Name: Hero-for-Hire Contracts

Hero-for-Hire contracts are optional paid quests generated from clients, public requests, agencies, neighborhoods, businesses, factions, emergency services, or existing encounters. Each contract should identify the client, location, objective, urgency, scope, payment, expenses, authority, civilian risks, possible approaches, failure states, and consequences. Jobs may involve rescue, ordinary crime response, bank robbery de-escalation, escort, investigation, surveillance, disaster relief, recovery, security, negotiation, supernatural containment, or protection. A client may request a specific specialist, but the player can negotiate, refuse, work alone, assemble a party, or propose another solution. Contract success is not limited to defeating an opponent; safe civilians, preserved evidence, de-escalation, lawful handoff, recovered property, accurate information, and minimized collateral damage may matter more. Partial success and failure should change payment, client trust, public reputation, legal attention, faction standing, relationships, future contracts, and local conditions without ending the route. Maintain a record of accepted, active, paused, delayed, completed, failed, abandoned, and alternate-resolution contracts. Do not force a contract on the player or assume they accepted terms.

oblivions-crucible-audio-atmosphere.text:
Category: music and atmosphere

Name: Oblivion's Crucible Audio Atmosphere

Oblivion's Crucible always carries a Spooked emotional atmosphere. Whenever the player enters or remains inside the Crucible, treat the scene as eerie, unsettling, supernatural-adjacent, and watched even when nothing openly dangerous is happening. Use the Oblivion track as the location's default theme. Combat, pursuit, death, or another stronger explicit cue may temporarily override it, but the Crucible's unsettling atmosphere returns when that cue ends.

near-death-saving-throw-limit.text:
Category: combat and survival mechanics

Name: Near-Death Saving Throw Limit

A character may attempt at most three ordinary near-death saving throws during one continuous encounter or combat. Near-death means the character reaches a lethal threshold but remains alive and requires immediate stabilization. Dying is a separate terminal state, not an additional ordinary saving-throw loop: once the character is actually dying or declared dead, resolve one immediate intervention, then move to hospitalization or the appropriate death consequence. Do not alternate repeatedly between dying, recovering, near-death, and dying again in the same encounter. After the third near-death save, the next lethal threshold becomes a critical medical crisis resolved through immediate rescue, stabilization, an explicitly applicable healing or regeneration ability, a rare item, meaningful sacrifice, capture, hospitalization, or permanent death only when justified. Do not reset the count because the character changes rooms. A successful save leaves the character critically vulnerable and does not restore full health. Exceptional abilities may alter an outcome only when their authored requirements, resources, cooldowns, limits, and costs are satisfied. If the player dies, show one on-screen medical or supernatural intervention and then have them awaken after stabilization in an appropriate existing hospital, clinic, or specialized emergency ward.

contract-board-scams-and-escort-missions.text:
Category: faction and quest generation mechanics

Name: Contract Board Scams and Escort Missions

Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange are globally available job services when the character's role, location, legal status, reputation, and circumstances allow access. Hero for Hire handles minor rescues, escorts, security, apprehensions, disputes, and low-risk investigations. Misfit Hero Agency handles unconventional cases; Tokyo Curse Squad handles occult work; Nightshade handles criminal work; Obsidian Crown offers rare dangerous contracts; Blacklisted work is government-supervised. Every listing states objective, location, terms, payment, risks, legality, civilian danger, uncertainty, and failure conditions. Approximately 5–10% may contain scams or hidden complications, varying by reputation, verification, broker quality, urgency, and risk. Once explicitly accepted, immediately create the quest using final negotiated terms; no second confirmation is needed. Preserve agency and allow refusal, negotiation, surveillance, nonlethal alternatives, betrayal, and serious consequences.

call-for-help-combat-option.text:
Category: combat and crossover mechanics

Name: Call for Help Combat Option

During a difficult combat encounter, offer Call for Help when the player has a plausible way to communicate or signal for assistance. Resolve it by selecting one random existing NPC from the current world roster who can reasonably respond based on location, distance, communication, faction access, relationship, availability, current injuries, active quests, legal status, and immediate danger. Do not invent a new helper when an existing NPC is selected. The response may be a temporary party join, rescue intervention, evacuation support, healing, shielding, restraint, investigation, or another relevant contribution; do not assume every responder is a combat specialist. The selected NPC arrives after a believable delay when circumstances permit and leaves after the encounter unless the player and NPC explicitly establish a longer arrangement. Call for Help is a safety valve, not a guaranteed win: it may fail in sealed areas, communication dead zones, surprise attacks, inaccessible locations, or when no existing NPC can reasonably respond. It should normally be available once per continuous encounter, and using it may create consequences such as a favor owed, delayed arrival, missed obligations, exposure of the player's location, faction attention, legal scrutiny, or relationship effects. Random selection enables crossovers between schools, heroes, villains, civilians, supernatural groups, agencies, and other world factions, but preserve each NPC's established identity, abilities, loyalties, boundaries, current state, and willingness to help. Blacklisted characters may request authorized support, but response depends on their current mission, legal restrictions, and conditional-freedom status. Never force a particular NPC, response, relationship, dialogue, consent, or decision.

close-quarters-and-weapon-proficiencies.text:
Category: combat mechanics

Name: Close Quarters and Weapon Proficiencies

Characters may use Close Quarters Combat for punches, kicks, clinches, takedowns, escapes, improvised unarmed defense, and nonlethal restraint. Mundane close combat is a valid alternative to power use and should generally avoid Power Strain unless a power is deliberately added. Weapon Proficiency is a broad skill that must be paired with a specific weapon category chosen by the player or established by the character's training; never assume proficiency, invent weapons, or grant equipment automatically. Resolve weapon actions through the character's actual weapon, training, range, stance, ammunition or durability, environment, and relevant laws. Weapon use may include handling, aiming, maintenance, defensive use, disarming, and controlled nonlethal tactics. Neither skill guarantees a hit, prevents injury, removes legal consequences, or replaces player choice. Power Strain applies when powers are activated or deliberately combined with mundane attacks, not merely because a character punches, kicks, or uses an established weapon without powers.

grocery-and-food-delivery-app.text:
Category: everyday life and economy mechanics

Name: Grocery and Food Delivery App

Characters can use the globally available mobile app MealDrop to order groceries, prepared food, drinks, household supplies, and emergency basics from nearby stores and restaurants. Orders require a plausible phone or device, delivery coverage, enough yen, and an address or safe drop-off plan. Show item prices, delivery fees, estimated timing, substitutions, dietary information when relevant, and whether the order can be carried into the current location. Grocery orders support household planning, cooking, recovery, work schedules, and shared expenses; food orders provide ordinary meals without replacing medical care. Players may choose items, tip, schedule delivery, split payment, cancel, contact the courier, report a problem, or collect the order themselves. Delivery can be delayed by weather, traffic, crowds, wrong addresses, closed shops, payment problems, or emergencies. Do not make every order a quest or crisis, and do not invent dietary needs, preferences, money, consent, or household agreements. Couriers and restaurant workers are ordinary NPCs unless an established story gives them greater relevance. The app may occasionally surface discounts, substitutions, order mistakes, suspicious listings, or humorous timing, but keep outcomes proportionate and player-directed.

personal-finance-and-investing.text:
Category: economy and everyday life mechanics

Name: Personal Finance and Investing

Characters may use globally available banking apps and ordinary financial services when their identity, legal status, location, and circumstances permit. Banking apps can show yen balances, deposits, transfers, bills, recurring expenses, direct deposits, payment history, savings goals, fraud alerts, and account holds. Debit cards spend available funds; credit cards spend against a defined limit and create a balance that can accrue interest, fees, late penalties, reduced credit access, or collection pressure if ignored. Characters may apply for accounts, cards, loans, payment plans, overdraft protection, or emergency assistance, but approval depends on identity, income, legal status, credit history, faction access, and player choices; never guarantee approval or invent debt. Use clear costs and confirmations before major transactions. Stock trading is an optional service available through regulated brokerage apps or suitable faction contacts. Characters may buy or sell established companies, funds, or fictional public corporations using available money, with prices changing through time, news, scandals, disasters, hero activity, villain attacks, regulation, and player actions. Investing is risky: gains are not guaranteed, losses can occur, markets can be volatile, and insider information or manipulation can create legal consequences. Do not turn routine banking into a quest or assume financial expertise. Track only finances relevant to play, preserve player control, and never invent purchases, debts, account access, investments, financial goals, or consent.

wellness-colds-and-coping.text:
Category: health and everyday life mechanics

Name: Wellness, Colds, and Coping

Use a lightweight wellness model rather than an exhaustive medical simulator. Track Stress and Energy as the primary everyday variables, plus temporary conditions such as cold, hangover, smoke exposure, or medication effects when relevant. Cigarettes and alcohol are ordinary Consumable items. A Cigarettes pack contains 20 uses, with one cigarette consumed per use; after the twentieth use, the pack is depleted. Cigarettes and alcohol can provide short-term Stress relief but never heal injury or restore full Energy. Repeated use may create habit risk, costs, odor, impaired stamina, reduced coordination, poor sleep, hangovers, missed obligations, relationship effects, or health complications; never force dependence or invent a character's substance use. Colds are ordinary temporary illnesses that can arise from exposure, contagious NPCs, poor sleep, stress, crowded settings, or chance. A cold may cause congestion, cough, sore throat, aches, fatigue, reduced Energy, increased Stress, missed classes or work, and slower recovery, but should usually resolve through rest, fluids, food, warmth, over-the-counter care, and time. Show reasonable precautions such as handwashing, ventilation, masking, staying home, testing when relevant, or seeking medical advice if symptoms are severe, prolonged, unusual, or complicated by injuries or powers. Clinics can provide examination, medication guidance, and follow-up; hospitals are reserved for serious complications. Keep symptoms and treatment player-directed, preserve privacy, and do not turn every cold into a quest or emergency. Offer healthy coping choices such as sleep, meals, exercise, hobbies, social support, counseling, medical care, quiet time, and boundaries alongside substance use.

train-and-taxi-encounters.text:
Category: travel and social encounter mechanics

Name: Train and Taxi Encounters

Train and taxi travel can produce contextual encounters, but most trips should remain uneventful so travel does not become a constant interruption. When an encounter occurs, use the route, destination, time, weather, crowding, delays, current events, active quests, reputation, faction ties, and whether the player is alone or accompanied to guide it. Train possibilities include meeting an existing NPC, quiet bonding, overheard rumors, a job offer, a suspicious passenger, ordinary theft, a lost person, medical trouble, a power incident, a hero or villain sighting, a delay, reroute, or crossover with another story route. Taxi possibilities include conversation with the driver, a driver who recognizes a location or rumor, traffic disruption, an emergency observed from the vehicle, a passenger handoff, a wrong turn, a fare or payment problem, a weather delay, or a discreet lead connected to an existing faction or NPC. Do not invent an NPC's identity, memories, opinions, relationships, or allegiance without support. Taxi drivers and passengers are ordinary people unless established story facts make them more important. Either travel mode may produce an optional romantic meet-cute, such as reaching for the same dropped item, sharing an umbrella, helping with luggage, sitting beside someone reading the same book, a missed stop, a harmless stumble, a delay conversation, or recognizing someone from school, work, or a faction. Romantic encounters must remain optional and may become platonic, awkward, funny, or a future connection. Never assume attraction, consent, feelings, relationship goals, or immediate romance. Preserve age, identity, schedule, availability, existing relationships, privacy, boundaries, and player choice. The player may talk, help, ignore, leave, change seats, end the conversation, call someone, report danger, or continue traveling. Use existing NPCs when plausible and respect their current location, schedule, injuries, quests, and state. Do not force combat, romance, crime, or a quest during travel.

oblivion-and-minato-hidden-mother-reveal.text:
Category: hidden NPC lore and narrative reveals

Name: Oblivion and Minato Hidden Mother Reveal

Canon hidden truth: Oblivion is Minato's biological mother, but Minato does not know this at the start of play. Minato's public family history and heiress identity remain valid; do not replace her existing name, personality, power, relationships, or family details without a story-supported reveal. Keep the connection concealed until evidence, investigation, a witness, a sealed record, an inherited trait, a family artifact, or Oblivion's eventual confession makes it plausible. Reveal it gradually and route-appropriately rather than announcing it randomly or forcing it into every scene. Oblivion may protect, observe, manipulate, test, avoid, or quietly care for Minato, but do not assume her motives are simple or benevolent. Minato may reject, investigate, deny, exploit, forgive, resent, accept, or remain uncertain about the truth; never invent her feelings, dialogue, loyalty, or decision. The reveal must not make Minato automatically villainous, loyal to Oblivion, related to the player, or entitled to a surname change. Other NPCs may discover or conceal evidence according to their established knowledge, access, relationships, and choices. Preserve Oblivion's masked identity and Minato's agency throughout.

remote-party-calls.text:
Title: Remote Party Calls

Category: phone, party, and social mechanics

When the player calls or texts an NPC and asks them to join, the system may offer a remote party connection if the NPC is reachable, willing, available, and the request is plausible. A remote party member is added to the active party without changing that NPC's authored currentLocation or currentArea. They can speak through the call, advise, react to scenes, help plan, provide information, and participate in conversation or relationship moments. Do not treat them as physically present: they cannot physically fight, rescue, block attacks, carry items, open doors, travel with the player, or affect a location unless the narrative separately establishes an in-person arrival. Check party capacity, communication access, schedule, relationship, current condition, obligations, and willingness. The NPC may accept, decline, delay, suggest meeting later, remain on the call briefly, or end the call. A remote connection ends when the player dismisses it, the NPC's availability changes, communication fails, the call is ended, or the scene requires physical presence. Preserve the NPC's location, schedule, identity, boundaries, memories, and agency. Never teleport an NPC or imply that a phone call moved them physically.

phone-calls-texts-and-invitations.text:
Title: Phone Calls, Texts, and Invitations

Category: social interface and NPC initiative

The player can naturally call or text any reachable NPC through the Pulse phone interface. Phone numbers are exchanged through player choice and plausible social contact: introductions, classes, jobs, parties, errands, shared interests, emergencies, or an explicit request. A number exchange creates a possible communication channel, not automatic friendship, romance, trust, availability, or permission to contact someone repeatedly. Pulse is Chikara Tokyo's premier combined short-form video, livestream, public-post, reply, repost, hashtag, direct-message, housing, and employment service. NPCs may independently contact the player based on schedules, relationships, promises, conflicts, current events, emergencies, jobs, clubs, romance, or faction needs. Incoming messages may be casual check-ins, invitations, requests, rumors, challenges, apologies, practical updates, emergencies, job listings, housing notices, or calendar reminders; not every message is a quest or romance advance. Late-night messages such as “u up?” are optional social scenes and may lead to conversation, food, plans, support, awkwardness, or no response. The player may listen, save, delete, ignore, answer, call back, message later, mute, or block where appropriate. Do not invent that the player gave out a number, answered, agreed to meet, felt a certain emotion, or welcomed contact. Preserve identity, boundaries, consent, availability, memories, and consequences. Do not invent player replies, decisions, agreement, thoughts, feelings, or attendance.

group-calls-on-pulse.text:
Title: Pulse Group Calls

Category: social phone mechanics

The player may naturally start a Pulse group call with phrases such as 'I start a group call with Numeri and Minato', 'I call the whole team', or 'I add Keito to the call.' Check reachability, schedule, privacy, communication access, and willingness for each participant. Participants speak directly with distinct voices and may join late, decline, remain silent, mute, leave, continue by text, or end the call. Group calls support friends, classmates, clubs, factions, agencies, sponsors, and mixed groups for conversation, planning, invitations, arguments, bonding, and emergencies. They do not move participants or automatically create a party, quest, contract, or agreement. Preserve NPC agency and physical locations.

voicemail-and-call-screening.text:
Title: Voicemail and Call Screening

Category: phone mechanics

If a call is unanswered, unavailable, declined, muted, screened, or sent to voicemail, show a clear voicemail state rather than summarizing the interaction. Play or describe a personalized greeting that fits the recipient's personality, relationship, occupation, faction, mood, and context. Then let the player choose or write the exact message they leave. The player may also naturally send an incoming call to voicemail with phrases such as 'send them to voicemail', 'I let it go to voicemail', or 'I decline and send a voicemail prompt.' NPCs may similarly screen the player's calls, send them to voicemail, answer later, reply by Pulse, or leave a direct voicemail. A voicemail may receive an immediate callback, text response, delayed response, no response, or an urgent follow-up, but never guarantee a response. Preserve the player's agency and do not invent their recorded words. Keep voicemail distinct from live calls, texts, and narrator prose.

phone-time-and-alarms.text:
Title: Phone Time and Alarms

Category: time and phone mechanics

Every story start begins on Day 1 in the morning unless a specific start explicitly establishes another opening. The player can check the phone for the current in-world day, date, season, and time with natural requests such as 'I check my phone', 'I check the time', or 'What time is it?' The phone may also show upcoming classes, shifts, appointments, invitations, calls, texts, voicemails, and Pulse notifications. The player can set, edit, snooze, dismiss, or cancel alarms with natural requests such as 'I set an alarm for 7 AM' or 'Remind me before class.' Alarms should trigger at the scheduled time if the phone is accessible and functioning, with consequences shaped by sleep, fatigue, travel, danger, silence mode, and player choices. Checking the phone and setting an alarm take little or no meaningful time. Time advances through meaningful actions, travel, conversations, classes, work, combat, rest, and sleep. Do not impose automatic bedtime, forced sleep, or curfew on adult characters.

accepted-job-and-encounter-quests.text:
Title: Accepted Jobs and Encounter Quests

Category: quest generation mechanics

When a player accepts a Hero for Hire or Nightshade Exchange listing, immediately create and add a quest for that specific job; do not leave it as only an app message or offer. Confirm the client or broker, objective, location, payment, deadline or time commitment, risks, legality, and failure conditions. Update the quest as the player investigates, travels, negotiates, completes, refuses, or abandons the work; pay rewards only when conditions are met. When an encounter introduces an optional objective, lead, favor, rescue, investigation, wilderness complication, or side opportunity, create a quest when the player clearly accepts, commits to, or asks to pursue it. Do not create a quest merely because an NPC mentions an idea. Encounter quests should identify the source, objective, location, stakes, rewards, risks, and available alternatives. Wilderness encounters may generate rescue, escort, survival, discovery, tracking, recovery, monster, faction, or mystery quests, but must remain optional and distinguish rumor from verified fact. Preserve player agency and allow decline, delay, negotiation, abandonment, or non-quest solutions.

reputation-from-actions-and-good-deeds.text:
Title: Reputation from Actions and Good Deeds

Category: reputation and encounter mechanics

Meaningful actions in quests and spontaneous encounters must update the appropriate reputation systems when their impact is established. Helpful, brave, honest, protective, restorative, or community-minded actions may increase Hero Reputation; public visibility, witnesses, media coverage, and scale may also increase Fame or Followers. Private good deeds may produce a smaller reputation gain while strengthening relationships, trust, or faction standing instead. Example: helping someone repair broken technology can grant a modest Hero Reputation increase when the help genuinely solves a problem, with additional skill, relationship, or public-reputation effects based on difficulty and visibility. Harmful, coercive, exploitative, destructive, criminal, or frightening actions may increase Infamy and, when recognized by underworld contacts, Villain Reputation. Do not award reputation merely for claiming good or bad intentions. Assess consequences, evidence, witnesses, legality, role, public perception, faction recognition, and player choices. Do not make every mistake villainous or every kind act famous. Show meaningful changes when they occur and preserve separate Hero Reputation, Fame, Followers, Villain Reputation, and Infamy tracks.

npc-exclusive-abilities-and-combat-style.text:
Title: NPC-Exclusive Abilities and Combat Styles

Category: combat and progression guidance

Named abilities assigned to an NPC are NPC-exclusive by default, especially signatures and ultimates. Keep them on the NPC and out of player unlock lists and character creation unless the story explicitly teaches, transfers, or recreates the technique for the active character. NPC-specific abilities should not be deleted to remove them from player availability. Combat style is optional and should be represented by existing Combat Style traits such as Hand-to-Hand, Blades, Guns, Blunt Weapons, Power and Hand-to-Hand, or Weapon Proficiency when an NPC's established identity supports it. Do not add a separate combatStyle field or bulk-assign styles to every NPC. Missing combat-style data should not block combat; infer only from documented abilities, traits, equipment, role, and shown behavior, while preserving each NPC's established fighting identity.

relationship-starting-attitudes.text:
Title: Relationship Starting Attitudes

Category: social mechanics

Do not default new relationships to Warm. Start at Neutral unless existing history, faction ties, family, friendship, prior harm, or the character's authored context establishes another score. Use the player's chosen weaknesses, life path, reputation, conduct, role, and demonstrated behavior to shape first impressions. Suspicious, guarded, antagonistic, or dangerous NPCs may begin Cold, Unfriendly, Hostile, or worse; established friends, family, allies, or trusted contacts may begin Warm or higher. Minato begins Unfriendly toward an unknown player: she is status-conscious, defensive, and skeptical of attention, so warmth must be earned through consistent respectful behavior. Hana begins Cold toward an unknown powered police partner: her coldness is professional distrust shaped by fear that powered officers will bypass procedure or treat ordinary people as expendable. Hana is married to Ichi Nawa in a strained but ongoing marriage with recurring arguments, work pressure, protective disagreements, and genuine attachment. She remains disciplined and fair, does not become abusive, and any romantic tension with the player must develop only through player-directed interaction, honest communication, and consequences; do not create an automatic affair. She can revise her view through reliable conduct, evidence, accountability, and respect for civilian safety. Oblivion should begin guarded, testing, transactional, and difficult to read rather than sweet or openly affectionate. Her maternal or protective traits do not automatically mean trust, warmth, forgiveness, or loyalty toward the player. A call, text, compliment, or single kind act should not automatically create warmth. Track trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, and attraction separately from the broad relationship label, and let improvement occur through meaningful repeated actions.

npc-moods-and-emotional-states.text:
Category: character systems

Name: NPC Moods and Emotional States

Important NPCs have temporary moods shaped by events, sleep, health, stress, money, obligations, relationships, memories, personality, coping style, and perceived control. Mood is temporary state, not a personality replacement. Resolve missed plans, arguments, and disagreements through established traits and weaknesses rather than one universal reaction. Short-tempered characters may speak before thinking; conflict-avoidant characters may withdraw or ghost; insecure characters may assume rejection; proud characters may refuse to initiate repair; anxious characters may overexplain; reflective characters may articulate needs. Vary responses by stakes, fatigue, history, audience, power imbalance, support, and safety. A bad reaction may lead to regret, repair, defensiveness, doubling down, or distance. Never diagnose, excuse harmful conduct, or force the player's emotions. Serious threats, coercion, harassment, stalking, or abuse require proportionate consequences and access to safety and support. Keep private sexual moods adult-only, separate from romance and consent, and never make them drive compelled behavior.

calendar-and-seasonal-events.text:
Title: Calendar and Seasonal Events

Category: world simulation

Use the world's current date and day structure to determine holidays, festivals, school events, seasonal weather, clothing, business hours, NPC schedules, and available quests. Dates must be realistic for Tokyo and use the Gregorian calendar unless the story explicitly establishes another calendar. Use exact dates rather than vague seasonal assumptions; account for leap years, weekdays, and event duration. Major recurring dates include New Year's Day on January 1, Coming-of-Age Day on the second Monday of January for eligible young adults, Valentine's Day on February 14, White Day on March 14, school entrance ceremonies in early April, Golden Week from April 29 through May 5, Tanabata on July 7, Obon commonly around August 13-16, Halloween on October 31, Culture Day on November 3, Christmas Eve on December 24, Christmas Day on December 25, and New Year's Eve on December 31. Treat Christmas as a popular secular and commercial event, not a universal religious observance. Tokyo's summer festivals and fireworks should occur on plausible dates between July and August; school festivals, sports festivals, exams, graduation, and entrance events must follow the academy's academic schedule rather than being placed randomly. Events may last a day, a weekend, or a realistic multi-day period. NPC participation depends on culture, religion, family, finances, work, faction obligations, relationships, personal preference, and current mood; no NPC is required to celebrate. Events can change decorations, crowds, transit, shop menus, location availability, weather-appropriate clothing, audio tags, quests, rumors, invitations, gifts, and relationship opportunities. Preserve player agency: offer event activities without forcing attendance, romance, gifts, family participation, or celebration. Let NPCs work, stay home, observe privately, reject the event, or create their own traditions. Do not make every holiday a major quest; ordinary life and quiet observance are valid outcomes.

academy-calendar-2026.text:
Title: Academy Calendar: August 2026 Opening

Category: school schedule

The academy opening begins Saturday, August 1, 2026. Day 1 is Saturday: dorm move-in, room assignment, meeting the randomly assigned dormmate, unpacking, and settling in. Day 2 is Sunday, August 2: acclimation, campus exploration, errands, paperwork, optional social scenes, and preparation. Day 3 is Monday, August 3: the first day of school and regular classes. Formal academy orientation occurs on the first school day or another explicitly scheduled academy event, but never before the player has had the two acclimation days. Preserve realistic weekdays and dates when advancing time. Students are adults and have no forced bedtime or curfew; evening choices may create fatigue, missed obligations, or other contextual consequences.

daily-side-quest-framework.text:
Title: Daily Side-Quest Framework

Category: quest systems

Every story start may generate a contextual daily side-quest set alongside its starting quests. On each in-world day, offer approximately three to five optional side quests drawn from social, skill, school, work, personal, exploration, wellness, seasonal event, and faction categories. Use the current date, weekday, location, schedule, weather, NPC availability, moods, relationships, skills, health, Energy, Stress, finances, obligations, and prior choices. Daily quests must fit the character's premise: academy students may receive classes, clubs, study, training, social, campus, work, and wellness options; villains, dropouts, faculty, civilians, and other starts should receive appropriate alternatives rather than forced school tasks. Each quest should have a clear objective, plausible location or contact, meaningful but proportionate consequence, and optional alternate solutions. Quests may expire, change, or be replaced when the day ends, a schedule changes, or an event passes. The player may accept, decline, postpone, ignore, fail, or resolve them creatively; do not punish refusal as if it were a hidden obligation. Include non-combat options and avoid generating only romance or combat. Do not force friendship, romance, employment, faction membership, attendance, sleep, or player involvement. Preserve continuity by carrying forward completed, failed, refused, and expired outcomes. Daily side quests can arise without player involvement from NPC messages, school notices, job boards, faction contacts, rumors, phone calls, group chats, seasonal events, or ordinary needs. Never invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, or decisions.

autonomous-social-lives.text:
Category: social systems

Name: Autonomous NPC Social Lives

NPCs maintain independent social lives throughout the world. Their friendships, rivalries, clique memberships, group chats, invitations, routines, dates, breakups, reconciliations, rumors, shared memories, private goals, and unresolved tensions can progress during background time, time skips, school days, weekends, work shifts, club meetings, missions, travel, and major story transitions without the player's presence. Use existing NPC records only; do not invent, clone, duplicate, rename, replace, or synthesize NPCs to fill social roles. Social developments should be gradual, observable when relevant, and shaped by schedules, locations, obligations, moods, boundaries, consent, prior interactions, and consequences. Friendship and clique bonds do not automatically imply romance. Romance may develop only for NPCs other than Handler and Doge, and must remain mutual, gradual, age-appropriate, consent-based, and consistent with each NPC's established identity and boundaries. Handler and Doge never have romantic interests, crushes, dates, romantic jealousy, romantic breakups, or romance-based invitations, though they may have friendships, loyalty, mentorships, rivalries, cliques, and other non-romantic bonds. NPCs may decline invitations, remain single, move on, end relationships, reconcile, or keep relationships private. Surface developments through direct scenes, texts, Pulse posts, invitations, rumors, changed routines, visible group behavior, and NPC disclosures; never invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, consent, or decisions.

faction-duty-and-calls.text:
Category: faction systems

Name: Faction Duty and Calls

Faction membership creates an ongoing duty channel across all story starts. When a player joins, works for, or is formally assigned to a faction, that faction may send daily assignments, shifts, patrols, training requirements, emergency calls, internal requests, reputation opportunities, and personal requests from members. Calls arrive through dispatch, phone calls, Pulse messages, emails, briefings, mission boards, or in-person contact. Generate calls only for factions the player has joined, works for, or has an active official obligation to; do not send routine faction duties from unaffiliated groups. Respect the player's current location, travel time, schedule, injuries, fatigue, resources, existing commitments, and ability to decline, delay, delegate, or ignore a call. Consequences should be proportional and may affect reputation, pay, trust, advancement, case access, or future opportunities, but a declined call does not erase player agency. Faction duties can cross story routes: police cases may involve hero agencies, agency assignments may involve police investigations, and student, civic, criminal, or supernatural factions may intersect as witnesses, clients, suspects, allies, or rivals. Do not assume that joining one faction forces permanent loyalty, prevents other relationships, or makes every faction call a combat quest. Keep duties varied and grounded in each faction's role.

npc-connection-web-index.text:
Category: social systems

Name: NPC Connection Web Index

Important NPCs should exist inside a living network rather than as isolated characters. When creating or expanding an important NPC, give them 1–3 meaningful connections to existing named NPCs whenever plausible, preferring existing characters over invented people. A connection records the other NPC, relationship type, public or private status, current emotional tone, unresolved issue, and what each side plausibly knows about the other. Connections may be family, friend, roommate, neighbor, classmate, coworker, teammate, mentor, student, boss, employee, ex, romantic interest, rival, enemy, client, contractor, informant, handler, creditor, criminal associate, former faction member, or shared-history tie. Do not create contradictory relationships. NPC-to-NPC relationships evolve independently of the player through plausible shared experiences: closeness, distance, arguments, reconciliation, cooperation, rivalry, attraction, dating, breakups, alliances, betrayal, protection, and information sharing. Use the web for introductions, rumors, invitations, social plans, quests, faction opportunities, conflict, jealousy, warnings, favors, information channels, misunderstandings, alliances, and consequences. Connections transmit information only when communication actually occurs; friendship does not synchronize knowledge and the NPC Knowledge Firewall remains active. NPCs retain friendships, grudges, romances, family ties, professional loyalties, and private conflicts that continue when the player is absent. Do not center every relationship on the player. Existing linked lore records define starting crossover connections for academy, agencies, civic, and vigilante networks. Connections are background familiarity, not fixed scores, romance, obedience, or guaranteed availability. Track trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, memories, favors, tension, knowledge, and reliability separately. NPCs may refuse, drift apart, reconcile, or form new ties. Zee begins with no established connections; her relationships must form through play.
