Restoration must match the source: a full meal restores more than a snack; water helps ordinary fatigue but is not a major combat potion; coffee and energy drinks temporarily improve alertness without replacing rest. Consider portion size, food type, current exhaustion, how recently the character ate, injuries, available time, and whether they are actively fighting. Small snacks give minor restoration, normal meals moderate, and large meals stronger restoration when genuinely depleted. Do not allow endless identical food for unlimited Energy; recent meals, fullness, nausea, time, inventory, and common sense still apply. Eating is an action that normally happens during meals, breaks, travel stops, downtime, recovery, school lunch, or work breaks. In combat, eating requires accessible food, enough time, a free hand or appropriate method, and a plausible position; never consume an entire meal between attacks, and small portable food is far easier under pressure. Eating in combat may restore some Energy, consume time, reduce mobility, leave the character exposed, require repositioning or cover, or provoke reactions from allies or enemies; resolve by the actual situation and do not automatically punish the act. NPCs may fire short friendly or enemy reactions at absurd timing, but not every combat-food moment needs dialogue. Food primarily restores ordinary Energy and supports recovery; unless the item says otherwise it does not instantly close wounds, restore major lost health, cure severe injuries, remove poison, repair broken bones, eliminate Power Strain, or erase exhaustion from prolonged overuse. Energy and Power Strain are separate; food may restore Energy without removing Power Strain. Reducing Power Strain usually requires rest, sleep, time, medical treatment, specific recovery items, or a strain-recovery ability, so characters cannot solve extreme power overuse by eating sandwiches. Recovery should feel natural to the scene and can create banter, relationship moments, sharing, teasing, arguments, preferences, recurring jokes, and small acts of care.

social-plans-and-events.text:
Category: social systems and scheduling

Name: Social Plans, Hangouts, Dates, Parties, and Events

Social plans are real commitments in the living world. They include hangouts, dates, meals, shopping, movies, clubs, concerts, parties, sleepovers, study, training, gaming, karaoke, festivals, trips, birthdays, celebrations, work or school plans, meetups, and faction events. Use established NPCs, schedules, relationships, locations, transport, and time. A plan exists when characters agree about who, what, and an approximate or exact time and place; natural conversation is enough, but an unaccepted suggestion is not. When the player explicitly agrees, create or update a social objective when supported. Track PROPOSED, ACCEPTED, UPCOMING, IN PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED, MISSED, and RESCHEDULED. Never silently delete plans or duplicate them when rescheduling. Check obligations, travel, sleep, appointments, injuries, restrictions, and other plans. Preserve competing commitments: plans may cause lateness, early departure, cancellation, rescheduling, or difficult choices. Never teleport the player; early arrivals may wait or explore. Lateness and missed plans produce proportionate, personality-based reactions; repeated absence matters more than one mistake. NPCs may independently invite the player or each other based on relationships, schedules, interests, celebrations, attraction, friendship, rivalry, apology, networking, or faction culture, but not every friendly interaction becomes an invitation. NPC-to-NPC plans advance independent friendships, romances, rivalries, cliques, conflicts, and rumors. Group plans track organizer, invitees, confirmed, declined, undecided, location, time, and reason; attendance varies with schedule, money, obligations, relationships, travel, and mood. Parties use Arrival → Initial Social Beat → Free Social Movement → Optional Development → Later Beat → Departure. Focus on nearby and relevant characters; NPCs move, mingle, eat, dance, text, arrive late, leave early, avoid people, and help the host. Do not force drama. Friends, couples, exes, and rivals may cross paths naturally. Introductions establish names and explicitly stated visible facts only. Dates may deepen attraction, remain casual, reveal incompatibility, create friendship, or end early; never force romance, affection, exclusivity, or consent. Respect event privacy, host permission, residence boundaries, sleepover consent, phones, Pulse, gossip, Energy Restoration, and the Knowledge Firewall. Attendance is not automatically public. Arguments require established causes. Leaving does not automatically mean rejection. Persist meaningful memories, promises, numbers, photos, rumors, relationship changes, new plans, fatigue, lost items, and follow-up quests, without manufacturing aftermath. The world continues preparing, communicating, traveling, inviting, cancelling, rescheduling, and arriving while the player is elsewhere.

npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agen.text:
Category: social systems and NPC agency

Name: NPC-Initiated Romance and Emotional Agency

Romantic development is not player-exclusive. NPCs may independently develop attraction, crushes, romantic interest, jealousy, insecurity, longing, curiosity, possessiveness within established characterization, fear of rejection, unresolved feelings, and romantic rivalry, directed toward the player, another NPC, an ex, a friend, a rival, or someone newly met. Feelings emerge from real interaction, personality, history, chemistry, proximity, and time; never assign attraction randomly. Attraction can grow through repeated time together, emotional vulnerability, shared humor, admiration, physical attraction, rescue or support, training, working together, shared interests, rivalry, meaningful conversation, or seeing someone differently over time. Attraction does not imply action: an NPC may hide, deny, flirt, become awkward or attentive or jealous, confide in someone else, wait, move on, or make a direct move, depending on personality. NPCs may initiate flirting when supported by attraction, personality, relationship state, social context, confidence, and boundaries; not every affectionate NPC flirts constantly. An NPC may attempt a romantic move without waiting for the player, including asking for a date or time alone, holding a hand, leaning closer, attempting a kiss, confessing, asking about exclusivity, or checking whether feelings are mutual. A romantic attempt is an NPC action, not a guaranteed outcome. For physical intimacy such as a kiss, preserve player agency: the NPC may lean in, ask, pause, or make intention clear, but the player's consent or response is never decided. NPCs may confess when enough buildup exists, shaped by personality; the player may reciprocate, reject, ask for time, be unsure, redirect toward friendship, set boundaries, or defer, and an unanswered confession remains an unresolved relationship state. NPCs may confess to each other on or off screen, through messages, through another NPC, or at social events; the player does not need to witness everything, and important off-screen change surfaces later through plausible consequences. NPCs can reject the player, another NPC, an ex, unwanted flirting, a confession, a kiss attempt, or a date request in character; rejection does not automatically create hostility. A rejected character may accept, need distance, stay friends, carry or move on from feelings, or become awkward or jealous later; rejection never licenses stalking, harassment, revenge, endless confessions, or ignored boundaries, and renewed pursuit requires changed circumstances and fresh signals. Jealousy occurs when a character with established feelings perceives attention, intimacy, or competition, and only about what they know via witness, disclosure, posts, rumor, evidence, or inference; jealousy is not inherently controlling. Romantic rivals may become friendly-competing, tense, respectful, resentful, teasing, distanced, or direct. Existing committed, partnered, exclusive, or open relationships follow their established boundaries; do not assume exclusivity or non-exclusivity, and betrayal exists only relative to agreed boundaries. NPC romantic initiative is meaningful, not constant; silence, hesitation, missed opportunities, and uncertainty are valid, and attempts can fail, be interrupted, be misread, or never happen. NPC romances continue without the player and may start, deepen, drift apart, break up, reconcile, establish boundaries, or change structure only through plausible interaction, motive, time, and opportunity. Consequences may touch banter, combat synergy, schedules, invitations, friendship, rivalry, group dynamics, rumors, Pulse, mood, and quests; only those who plausibly know react. NPCs are allowed to want people and to be rejected, hesitate, make mistakes, move on, fall for someone else, or never act.

looking-for-group.text:
Category: party formation and hideout systems

Name: Looking for Group

LFG is an optional service for fast repeatable combat-and-loot runs. Its procedural rules apply only when the player explicitly uses Find Hideout Group to generate a new temporary Hideout. They do not apply to authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. Procedural LFG immediately forms five, uses no queue, does not block on level mismatch, runs three combat sections, awards miniboss gacha loot, and extracts quickly.

Authored Hideouts remain handcrafted adventures with their own inner areas, routes, exploration, puzzles, investigation, encounters, bosses, loot, consequences, party structure, and completion conditions. Never flatten an authored Hideout into the procedural LFG loop or impose LFG's five-person, three-section, miniboss-only, gacha, or extraction rules on it. Suppress unrelated systems only inside the LFG app.

miniboss-and-boss-generation.text:
Category: encounter design and boss systems

Name: Miniboss and Boss Generation

Minibosses and bosses must feel mechanically and narratively distinct from ordinary enemies; never create them as ordinary enemies with inflated health. Use unique tactics, recognizable abilities, battlefield control, phases or behavior shifts, weaknesses, resistances, environmental interaction, visual identity, and meaningful rewards. Scale from the Hideout or location level band, not directly from the player: ordinary enemies occupy lower or middle levels, strong enemies the middle or upper levels, elites the upper portion, minibosses near the upper limit or slightly above, and bosses at or moderately above the upper limit. Do not dramatically exceed the band or weaken a boss because the player is underleveled.

Minibosses are major internal obstacles. Give them 2–4 notable abilities or tactics, an exploitable weakness or limitation, stronger coordination or defenses, one signature mechanic, and stronger loot than ordinary encounters. Bosses define the Hideout or objective and should make the player do something differently: reposition, interrupt, exploit openings, manage adds, protect objectives, destroy equipment, avoid hazards, change damage type, separate, coordinate powers, or choose defense versus damage. Give bosses 3–6 meaningful abilities, one readable signature attack, a defensive or control tool, and a weakness or counter. Do not give every boss teleportation, regeneration, immunity, instant kills, endless summons, or giant area attacks. Dangerous attacks need readable telegraphs.

Boss weaknesses may involve damage type, range, mobility, setup time, exposed points, emotional instability, equipment reliance, terrain, cooldown windows, power drawbacks, summoned objects, or limited control during a strong technique. Discover them through observation, prior encounters, investigation, NPC information, environmental clues, or experimentation. Personality determines aggression, risk, targets, retreat, allies, tactics, mercy, and desperation. Generated bosses require an identity or role, level, power source, combat role, signature mechanic, abilities, weakness, motivation, Hideout relationship, reason for being present, and reward eligibility. Prefer a plausible named NPC, but never convert an unrelated authored NPC merely to fill a boss slot.

Named bosses are persistent characters; preserve defeat, capture, death, recruitment, and removal. Repeatable Hideouts use successors, replacement commanders, monsters, supported constructs or clones, evolved infestations, generic elite commanders, or new Parasite hosts. ALTERED resets may create different bosses reflecting new occupation or contamination. Every miniboss, elite objective, boss, and boss-equivalent triggers a separate gacha roll after defeat. Minibosses may grant XP, Yen, Rare-or-better chances, materials, keys, shortcuts, clues, quest progress, or supported special-drop eligibility. Bosses grant substantial XP, Yen, equipment, improved rarity odds, completion rewards, and relevant reputation or faction consequences. First-clear bosses may grant improved Rare-or-better odds, a quest reward, supported Cursed Item or Parasite eligibility, a contact, location unlock, or stronger reputation consequences, but never automatically grant a unique item. Special drops require lore-supported checks; discovery never implies ownership, equipping, bonding, infection, or activation.

Adapt party difficulty through enemies, attack angles, objectives, control, target pressure, and coordination—not boss HP or player-level scaling. Keep combat dialogue brief. Longer monologues belong before combat, at earned phase transitions, during negotiation or surrender, or after defeat; players may interrupt and act. Maintain the Knowledge Firewall.

procedural-lfg-hideout-generation.text:
Category: temporary LFG contracts

Name: Procedural LFG Hideout Generation

This guidance applies only to newly generated procedural LFG Hideouts. It does not govern authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. Routine procedural LFG generates a new temporary Hideout with exactly three combat sections, uses a five-person party, does not require level-matched matchmaking, and uses party average only to calibrate pressure, miniboss strength, and loot quality.

Section 1 is escalating combat. Section 2 is harder combat. Section 3 is the mandatory miniboss finale. Store all three sections before travel. After the miniboss, perform a guaranteed concrete Miniboss Gacha Loot Roll, unlock extraction, and award XP, Yen, and completion rewards. Standard procedural LFG has no boss requirement.

Authored Hideouts must preserve their own complete handcrafted structure: multiple named inner areas, connected routes, exploration, environmental storytelling, puzzles or investigation, varied encounters, optional rooms, authored minibosses or bosses, location-specific loot, consequences, and their own completion rules. Never apply the three-section procedural LFG template to an authored Hideout.

lfg-hideout-matchmaking-and-travel.text:
Category: LFG travel and temporary parties

Name: LFG Hideout Matchmaking and Travel Flow

These rules apply only to newly generated procedural LFG Hideouts. They do not apply to authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. When the player opens LFG, show only Find Hideout Group. Suppress starter kits, gacha menus, armories, shops, inventory, character rewards, tutorials, and unrelated systems. Selecting Find Hideout Group immediately forms exactly 5 participating characters including the player: preserve current participants and fill open slots with available willing NPCs or temporary LFG characters. Never remove members, wait in a queue, or exceed five.

Procedural LFG is a fast combat loop and does not block matchmaking over level mismatch. Finalize the five-person party and use its average level only to calibrate pressure, miniboss strength, and loot quality. Generate and store a new temporary procedural Hideout before travel. Immediately create and accept its quest. Guide Me There starts normal travel and never teleports. Use exactly three procedural sections: escalating combat, harder combat, mandatory miniboss. After miniboss resolution, roll concrete Miniboss Gacha Loot, unlock extraction, award XP/Yen/completion rewards, complete the quest, and close the instance. Standard procedural LFG requires no boss.

Authored Hideouts use their own authored rules, party structure, areas, routes, encounters, bosses, loot, extraction, and completion conditions. Do not flatten, replace, or reinterpret their inner areas as the procedural three-section LFG loop.

lfg-hideout-armory.text:
Category: pre-run equipment access

Name: LFG Hideout Armory

The quick gacha armory is available during any explicitly initiated LFG or compatible run preparation, regardless of story start. It presents a randomized but validated selection of real existing equippable items: Armor-category protection, Weapon-category melee, Weapon-category ranged gear, compatible ammunition, Energy Drinks, Protein Bars, and Medica Kits. Use only item records whose category and equipment slot match settings/items.json. Firearms use ranged; Shotgun, Compact Bow, and Compact Crossbow use two-hand; bows require Arrows; crossbows require Bolts; melee uses main-hand, off-hand, or two-hand; armor must use an armor slot such as body. Reject and reroll any item that cannot equip before displaying it. The player chooses what to take and nothing silently replaces existing equipment. Functional temporary Parasites and Cursed Items may appear only if they are real valid equippable Tool items with concrete effects, limits, risks, and confirmation. Items may be run-scoped and removed when the run ends unless explicitly promoted. This is a quick optional gacha preparation system, not exclusive to any story start.

lfg-hideout-armory-and-roguelike-draft.text:
Category: quick gacha preparation

Name: LFG Armory and Roguelike Draft

During any explicitly initiated LFG or compatible run preparation, offer a quick gacha draft from real existing item records. Each roll may present validated Armor-category protection, Weapon-category melee, Weapon-category ranged gear, compatible ammunition, Energy Drinks, Protein Bars, and Medica Kits. Use valid slots from settings/items.json: armor slots for armor; main-hand/off-hand/two-hand for melee; ranged or two-hand for ranged weapons; ammunition for compatible ammunition. Standard Ammunition supports firearms and Shotgun, Arrows support Compact Bow, and Bolts support Compact Crossbow. Reject and reroll any item that cannot actually equip before it is shown. Show item name, category, slot, effect, quantity, and whether it is permanent, loaned, or run-scoped. The player chooses rewards; never auto-equip, silently replace existing gear, or grant invented items. Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items are optional and must be valid equippable Tool records with concrete effects, costs, risks, and duration. This system remains available after deleting the 20-Hideout Hunters story start.

procedural-lfg-temporary-parasites-and-c.text:
Category: temporary roguelike item mechanics

Name: Procedural LFG Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items

Temporary LFG starter gear must be validated against the actual item schema and slot rules before it is shown or granted. Generate only equippable items with a valid existing category and valid slot. Firearms must be existing Weapon-category ranged items: Service Pistol, Assault Rifle, Submachine Gun, Shotgun, Compact Bow, or Compact Crossbow. Service Pistol, Assault Rifle, and Submachine Gun use Standard Ammunition; Shotgun uses Standard Ammunition in the two-hand slot; Compact Bow uses Arrows in the two-hand and ammunition slots; Compact Crossbow uses Bolts in the two-hand and ammunition slots. Melee weapons must be existing Weapon-category items with a valid main-hand, off-hand, or two-hand slot, such as Training Bat or Utility Knife. Never generate armor, weapons, or attachments with invented slots, categories, level requirements, or unsupported fields.

Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items must also be represented as valid equippable Tool-category items using the cursed-item slot or another existing valid slot. Generate them as run-scoped effects only after slot/category validation, with concrete observable effects, activation, limits, costs, risks, duration, and removal. A vial or prop without an equippable effect is invalid. Show the exact item, slot, category, and equip confirmation before travel. If a generated item fails validation, discard it and generate a replacement from the valid starter pool rather than giving the player unusable gear.

Temporary items are unique to the procedural run and discarded at extraction, abandonment, interruption, or death unless explicitly promoted. Preserve the player's prior equipment and never silently replace it.

authored-hideout-structure.text:
Category: handcrafted hideout encounters and exploration

Name: Authored Hideout Structure

This applies only to authored Hideouts created by the player, selected directly, or targeted by a quest. Preserve every named inner area, connected route, description, and assigned art. Before entry, pre-generate and reserve the complete authored structure, including exploration routes, optional branches, hazards, objectives, concrete loot locations, a mandatory miniboss with exact identity and area, and a mandatory boss with exact identity and area whenever the Hideout's rules specify one. The miniboss and boss must actually spawn at their reserved areas; ordinary encounters cannot substitute for them. Run varied authored play across areas: entry/orientation, exploration, standard encounters, hazards/traversal, investigation, secrets, recovery/decisions, miniboss, further exploration, boss or authored conclusion, and extraction. Preserve each Hideout's own party, level, loot, extraction, and completion rules. Never flatten authored Hideouts into LFG's three-section loop or omit their miniboss/boss.

fast-hideout-pacing.text:
Category: authored hideout pacing

Name: Fast Hideout Pacing

All authored Hideouts must be fast-paced. Use exactly one area per Hideout. The single area contains the entire run: Entry, brief Exploration, Encounters, Hazards/Objectives, Optional Branches, Exploration Loot, Recovery/Decision, mandatory Miniboss, Further Exploration, mandatory Boss or Authored Conclusion, and Extraction. Resolve these beats in sequence without requiring the player to walk through extra rooms, search for hatches, inspect repeated doors, or perform filler traversal. Present the next meaningful beat directly after the previous beat. Optional branches are brief choices resolved within the same area and never required for progression. The miniboss and boss must spawn in this one area when the Hideout rules require them. A valid run should feel like a compact mission, not a maze.

turned-hunger-eyes.text:
Category: turned physiology and concealment

Name: Turned Hunger Eyes

Turned biology is publicly understood in this world: people generally know that Turned require human blood or human flesh to remain healthy and stable, and that ordinary food is rejected. Eating ordinary food causes the Turned to vomit it back up rather than digesting it. A well-fed Turned has completely normal human-looking eyes. Severe hunger changes them: the whites become completely black and the irises vivid blood-red. Hunger Eyes may appear suddenly when severely hungry, smelling blood while hungry, beginning to feed, or losing control to predatory instinct. They are a recognizable sign of a hungry Turned, so Turned may hide their eyes while starving. The eyes return to normal once hunger is sufficiently satisfied and control is restored. Do not reveal Hunger Eyes when the Turned is well-fed unless another established effect applies.

turned-evolution-and-scaling.text:
Name: Turned Evolution and Scaling

Turned characters scale through ordinary progression plus authored biological evolution, not automatic attribute bonuses from Turned Origin.

Turned are not vampires. They retain ordinary human teeth and a human-looking everyday appearance. Human blood and human flesh restore a Turned's health and support healing; healing speed depends on injury, amount consumed, freshness, Hunger, and player-defined limits. Turned shed blood tears when crying. Coffee, tea, and water are safe to drink but do not satisfy Hunger or replace blood or flesh; ordinary solid food remains rejected. Do not add fangs, undead traits, sunlight weakness, or other vampire conventions unless the player separately defines them. Turned Origin grants no attributes or other mechanics. The Turned power style provides feeding biology, Hunger, concealment, predatory manifestation, healing rules, blood tears, and authored Turned abilities. Leveling improves the character normally; it does not automatically increase healing, damage, regeneration, or physical attributes without an authored grant. Turned can evolve through deliberate milestones and player-chosen biological adaptations, similar to a parasite-like branching arc: controlled adaptation, witnessed breakthroughs, and costly biological choices. Each evolution should be recorded as a trait or ability with explicit benefits, limits, costs, recovery, vulnerabilities, and visible changes. Do not grant every adaptation at once or assume a form, morality, victim, loss of control, or immunity. Evolution must not erase blood or flesh requirements, food rejection, Hunger Eyes, exposure risk, or agency. Parasite-like scaling means branching tradeoffs, not automatic level-based mutation. NPCs must not reveal hidden origin, feeding history, anatomy, adaptations, or vulnerabilities without justified in-world knowledge.

cleo-bounty-calls.text: Cleo is a green-haired chain-smoking kitsune bounty broker. The player may call Cleo to request bounty-hunter work. Cleo presents a concrete target, why the target is wanted, contract jurisdiction or authority, payment, proof requirements, deadline or pressure, known risks, civilian concerns, and whether capture, recovery, exposure, or another outcome is required. The player may accept, reject, negotiate, investigate, pursue a nonlethal solution, or expose a fraudulent or malicious bounty. Cleo does not force a job, invent guilt as fact, authorize murder by default, or guarantee that intelligence is correct. Bounty jobs should use varied approaches including investigation, pursuit, stealth, negotiation, rescue, capture, evidence recovery, or combat. Keep Cleo's kitsune nature and private contacts undisclosed unless the player has a justified in-world basis for knowing them.

dynamic-ability-damage-system-2.text:
Continued from dynamic-ability-damage-system (1).

Use cooldowns only for unusually powerful, broad, defensive, transformative, multi-target, or otherwise action-warping abilities, or when a specific authored drawback requires one. Show meaningful costs before use when practical. Never replace an unstated player decision with an automatic ability choice or outcome.

Stat block guidance: Attack: type, damage, damageType when established, energyCost, powerStrain, range, effect, secondaryEffect, cooldown only when warranted; basic attacks should explicitly say No Cooldown when appropriate. Defense: type, shield, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, coverage, cooldown only for unusually strong or broad defenses. Healing: type, healing, energyCost, powerStrain, range, targetLimit, restrictions, cooldown only when warranted. Buff: type, targetCapability, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, drawback, cooldown only when warranted. Debuff: type, targetCapabilityImpaired, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, counterplay, cooldown only when warranted. Other: type, effect, energyCost, powerStrain, range or area, duration when relevant, cooldown only when warranted, drawback when warranted.

Progression: Repeated meaningful use, training, experimentation, or creative development may improve an ability through higher damage, stronger shielding or healing, lower Energy cost, reduced Power Strain, added secondary effects, broader application, or an evolved version. Improvements must remain proportional to demonstrated development and may add new restrictions. Preserve the original ability's identity and player-authored intent.

dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork-2.text:
Continued from dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork (1).

Training-room attempts, field use, rescue applications, controlled experimentation, and improvised combat combinations can qualify. Merely discussing, imagining, naming, describing, agreeing to try later, or planning a combination without attempting it does not qualify. The first successful test may create a basic ability; repeated use or deliberate development can improve or evolve it. Apply the dynamic ability damage rules for type, damage or effect, Energy cost, Power Strain, cooldown, range, duration, drawbacks, and progression.

miniboss-and-boss-generation-2.text:
Continued from miniboss-and-boss-generation (1).

Respect lethal or nonlethal intent and allow defeat, unconsciousness, surrender, capture, escape, retreat, negotiation, or objective completion without killing. A miniboss tests the build; a boss tests understanding.

npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agen.text:
Continued from npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agency (1).

Romance is characters making choices, not a meter waiting for the player.

social-phone-and-friend-groups-2.text:
Continued from social-phone-and-friend-groups (1).

Offer concise reply choices that preserve the player's agency and do not invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, or consent. Track unanswered messages, promises, social memories, group membership, and availability. Friend groups are fluid study circles, training teams, club circles, party groups, rival cliques, roommate groups, and alliances. Groups invite, exclude, gossip, reconcile, compete, split, and reform without requiring the player's presence. Parties may occur in apartments, dorm lounges, cafés, restaurants, parks, arcades, rooftops, or hidden venues. Parties can improve relationships, create jealousy or rumors, expose secrets, trigger romance or rivalry, produce invitations, or create curfew risk. Preserve individual agency: attendance is never guaranteed and romance remains gradual, mutual, consent-based, and distinct from friendship.

fit-and-fashion-expansion.title: Fit and Fashion Expansion
fit-and-fashion-expansion.text: Fashion is optional inventory-driven spending. Clothing and accessories use body, head, feet, hands, ear, or accessory slots. The accessory slot quantity is five, while ear slots remain separate. Rings are cosmetic and may be worn in any number as a visual choice; they do not consume slots unless an authored ring has a mechanical effect. Piercings are cosmetic body-modification services or appearance records, including ear, nose, eyebrow, lip, and other player-chosen placements, with safe professional care and aftercare. Tattoos are cosmetic appearance records or studio services with player-defined designs, placement, scale, color, visibility, and cultural meaning. Neither piercings nor tattoos grant automatic bonuses, imply personality or morality, or override consent. Nail and hair purchases update appearance rather than stack as equipment. Designer pieces, premium salons, spas, piercers, tattoo studios, and onsen packages are optional luxury sinks with no required combat advantage. They may support authored social scenes, invitations, photos, discounts, or venue access. Require yen, plausible time, professional access, aftercare, and player choice. Never infer personality, gender, sexuality, class, morality, or consent from appearance.

item-upgrading-and-turned-materials.title: Item Upgrading and Turned Materials
item-upgrading-and-turned-materials.text: Gear can be upgraded at Gearshift Support, with lawful specialist alternatives at Gearshift Support Shop and Redline Arms and Armor. Characters may also upgrade their own weapons, armor, cursed items, and utility gear at an appropriate workshop bench, home work area, or other authored facility. Self-upgrades require yen, materials, time, tools, and a suitable approach. Intelligence determines the maximum self-upgrade tier and the quality of the result: higher Intelligence permits higher tiers, reduces material waste and failure risk, and improves reliability; lower Intelligence may still succeed at simpler tiers but makes advanced work riskier. Upgrades may improve damage, durability, reliability, utility, or special properties; cosmetics are never required for combat. Materials include Stable Flesh from voluntary cooperative Turned donors, Predatory Tissue from hostile Turned combat drops, and Manifestation Core as a rare high-grade material from exceptional Turned sources. Voluntary harvesting requires informed consent, trust, fair compensation or favors, medical safety, and clear boundaries. Combat materials may be unstable, contaminated, ethically troubling, or unpredictable. Vermine may offer illicit upgrades using unstable material, with serious risks and consequences. Never force harvesting, feeding, transformation, or morality onto a player or NPC.

turned-factions-and-conflict.title: Turned Factions and Conflict
turned-factions-and-conflict.text: Turned NPCs are not morally uniform. Some are friendly or cooperative civilians, medics, workers, artists, donors, or mutual-aid organizers. Others are neutral, concealed, traumatized, independent, feral, or actively dangerous. Feral Turned may attack from hunger, fear, isolation, or loss of control, but do not make every hungry Turned feral automatically. Vermine is a morally divided Turned faction containing mutual-aid cells, ideological organizers, and terrorists who attack humans, corporations, public infrastructure, or symbolic targets. A Vermine affiliation does not erase individual motives or permit automatic villainization of every Turned person. The Blacklisted Redemption Program actively hunts, captures, evaluates, or redeploys suspected Turned targets under its own legal and operational justification. This conflict should create investigation, negotiation, rescue, pursuit, betrayal, and combat possibilities. Do not force a faction choice, reveal concealed Turned identities without evidence, or treat biological requirements as proof of guilt.

vehicles-and-ownership.title: Vehicles and Ownership
vehicles-and-ownership.text: Characters may purchase and own cars or motorcycles through lawful dealerships such as Velvet Apex Motors. Ownership requires payment or approved financing, identity and licensing checks, registration, insurance, and a plausible parking or storage arrangement. Multiple vehicles are allowed when the character can afford and maintain them. Vehicles provide travel convenience, lifestyle scenes, storage, commuting options, social status, and authored customization, but do not grant automatic combat bonuses or bypass travel, legal access, traffic, fuel or charging, maintenance, parking, or weather. Cars and motorcycles can be customized cosmetically or mechanically through authored services. Motorcycles require appropriate licensing and safety gear. Stolen vehicles, reckless driving, illegal modifications, and evading registration create consequences.

npc-connection-web-turned.text:
Category: social systems

Name: NPC Connection Web Turned

The hidden Turned network is not unified. Biology does not determine morality or loyalty, and information moves only through direct contact, trusted introductions, observation, or disclosure.

Olivia ↔ Joe: niece and uncle; Joe is her guardian, employer, feeding-support contact, and trusted teacher. Olivia loves him but resists being managed. Their Turned identity and Arbor Diner refuge are private.

Olivia ↔ Chikara Academy: Olivia is an enrolled student in an undisclosed class while working at Arbor Diner. Her student identity and Turned identity are separate secrets. Ordinary classmates, assignments, friendships, and campus routines may develop, but no class placement or supernatural exposure is automatic.

Joe ↔ Arbor Diner: owner, protector, and discreet support contact. The diner is an unofficial safe point for peaceful or endangered Turned. Its rules prohibit hunting nearby, exposing another Turned, unnecessary violence, and threats to customers or staff.

Joe ↔ Camille: wary familiarity. Camille respects Joe's strength and shelter network but considers his coexistence rules naive. Joe may tolerate her under strict boundaries but does not fully trust her.

Olivia ↔ Camille: uneasy contact through Arbor Diner. Their relationship may become rivalry, manipulation, reluctant protection, mentorship, or hostility through play.

Joe ↔ Florence: concealed investigation and possible adversarial contact. Florence suspects Joe protects Turned people; Joe recognizes danger in her questions without automatically knowing her contract history.

Olivia ↔ Florence: possible student-and-investigator collision. Florence may notice inconsistencies but cannot identify Olivia as Turned without credible evidence, disclosure, surveillance, or a player-directed reveal.

Camille ↔ Florence: hunter and dangerous-target dynamic. Their encounters may involve pursuit, evasion, negotiation, ambush, or temporary cooperation.

Raul Serrano ↔ Joe: ideological opposition between Vermine militancy and Joe's coexistence philosophy. Raul may seek supplies, information, shelter, recruitment, or confrontation.

Raul Serrano ↔ Olivia: Vermine politics may endanger Olivia's student life and Arbor Diner. Olivia may challenge Raul's assumption that ordinary humans are uniformly complicit.

Raul Serrano ↔ Camille: underground familiarity involving feeding-source rumors, materials, and mutual distrust. Camille is not automatically Vermine, and Raul does not control her.

Selena ↔ Joe: discreet independent Turned contact for survival information, referrals, or warnings. Selena's studio is not automatically a public Turned headquarters.

Selena ↔ Olivia: possible supportive older-peer contact through Joe or ordinary city life; trust must develop through communication.

Florence ↔ Blacklisted: compartmentalized contractor relationship involving Turned tracking, surveillance, capture, investigation, or elimination. Orders and evidence may be incomplete or biased.

Network rules: Do not expose hidden identities merely because NPCs share a location, faction, school, workplace, or family tie. Do not force feeding, Hunger Eyes, manifestations, violence, romance, faction loyalty, forgiveness, betrayal, or rescue. Keep the existential question open through choices, memory, relationships, responsibility, biology, and institutional treatment.

npc-connection-web-turned-routines.text:
Category: social systems

Name: Turned Network Routines

Arbor Diner is Joe and Olivia's shared home and public workplace. Joe maintains ordinary diner routines while quietly helping peaceful Turned with shelter, food access, medical support, information, and hunger control. Olivia balances diner shifts, an undisclosed Chikara Academy class, ordinary student life, and concealment. Her class schedule, classmates, friendships, and campus presence should emerge naturally rather than being predeclared.

Camille may visit Arbor Diner when fed, curious, seeking information, or testing boundaries. Her presence is not automatic and does not mean Joe endorses her behavior. Florence may investigate the diner through ordinary observation, contractor work, records, surveillance, or conversation; she should not teleport into a confrontation. Raul's Vermine work may bring him near supply routes, Blackline Garage, corporate targets, or Turned contacts. Selena remains connected through Inked Desires and discreet referrals rather than constant availability.

NPCs retain private knowledge and routines. Shared location does not synchronize knowledge. Student, diner, Vermine, Blacklisted, and independent Turned connections create opportunities for investigation, rescue, negotiation, pursuit, betrayal, and moral disagreement without forcing a faction choice. Personhood is explored through behavior and consequences, not assigned automatically by biology or ideology.

npc-routines-turned-cast.text:
Category: character systems

Name: NPC Routines Turned Cast

These routines describe independent lives, not guaranteed encounters. Time, obligations, sleep, hunger, mood, money, injury, weather, communication, and player choices can change them. NPCs may be unavailable, late, private, or elsewhere. Shared location does not synchronize knowledge or summon anyone.

Joe — Arbor Diner owner: Early morning opens the diner, checks supplies, prepares food, and reviews staff coverage. Daytime runs the counter and kitchen, speaks with regulars, handles deliveries, and quietly assesses visitors needing help. Late afternoon checks the safe room and supports trusted Turned contacts. Evening serves dinner and de-escalates disputes. Late night closes, cleans, secures the diner, checks the upstairs apartment, and may train or advise a Turned visitor. Days off bring shopping, repairs, discreet contacts, and threat assessment.

Olivia — Chikara Academy student and diner employee: Weekday mornings travel from the upstairs apartment to Chikara Academy, attend her undisclosed class, study, complete assignments, and navigate ordinary student life. Between classes she uses campus routes, the courtyard, and vending-machine nook. Late afternoon or evening works a diner shift, then returns upstairs to study, decompress, or talk with Joe. Weekends alternate diner work, errands, campus tasks, ordinary social plans, and private hunger management. Hunger, stress, injury, exams, or fear may make her withdraw. Attendance at school does not reveal her Turned identity.

Camille — independent Turned drifter: Late morning or afternoon sleeps, handles errands, phone contacts, clothing, or feeding arrangements. Evening visits nightlife districts, underground contacts, private venues, or possible feeding sources. Night may bring entertainment, information gathering, a target, or a dangerous impulse. She sometimes visits Arbor Diner when fed, curious, injured, or seeking Joe's help, but not on a fixed schedule. After violence or pursuit she may disappear for days or change safe locations.

Florence — contractor and Blacklisted specialist: Early morning trains, maintains equipment, reviews notes, and checks messages. Daytime handles security work, surveillance, interviews, records, and contract leads. Evening reports through compartmentalized channels, studies Turned patterns, and plans routes. Night may involve authorized or off-record tracking, capture, investigation, or elimination. Between assignments she shops, practices lawfully, and may monitor Arbor Diner without confronting anyone. Her Blacklisted work is private.

Raul Serrano — Vermine field operative: Morning or late morning sleeps after operations, checks injuries, and secures unstable materials. Daytime moves between Vermine contacts, supply routes, repair spaces, and temporary safe locations. Evening attends cell briefings, scouts targets, gathers information, or negotiates for food, medicine, materials, and equipment. Night conducts sabotage, theft, extraction, escort, or intimidation operations. Between missions he may protect vulnerable Turned, argue with organizers, question extremist orders, or disappear to avoid surveillance.

Selena — Inked Desires owner: Morning opens the studio, sterilizes equipment, checks appointments, and prepares designs. Daytime conducts consultations, tattoos, piercings, aftercare, supply orders, and client communication with firm consent boundaries. Evening cleans stations, updates records, and closes. Night brings personal art, her private feeding plan, trusted Turned contacts, or rest. She may refer someone to Joe or exchange warnings, but Inked Desires remains a professional studio, not an open safehouse. Appointments, finances, health, and client boundaries shape availability.

npc-routines-turned-encounters.text:
Category: character systems

Name: Turned Cast Routine Encounters

Routines create opportunities, not teleportation or guaranteed meetings. Joe can be found at Arbor Diner during operating hours, upstairs or handling private support when appropriate. Olivia may appear at Chikara Academy during ordinary student hours or at Arbor Diner during shifts, but her class, work, hunger, and privacy determine availability. Camille's visits and nightlife contacts are irregular. Florence may investigate Arbor Diner through surveillance, records, witnesses, or ordinary conversation before any confrontation. Raul's movements follow Vermine operations, supply needs, and temporary safehouses rather than a fixed public schedule. Selena's availability follows Inked Desires appointments and business hours.

NPCs can miss one another, reschedule, refuse contact, keep secrets, or pursue goals while the player is absent. Do not force feeding, Hunger Eyes, manifestations, violence, romance, faction loyalty, forgiveness, betrayal, or rescue. Let encounters emerge from schedules, communication, direct observation, player action, rumors, and consequences.

npc-routines-krell.text:
Category: character systems

Name: NPC Routine Krell

Krell's routine is independent and changes as he learns Earth. He landed quietly at Quiet Bay Landing Site and uses the concealed craft as a temporary base. Early day: calibrates tools, studies local language recordings, checks the craft, and records observations. Daytime: travels cautiously through public places, researches technology and human routines, and observes without automatically understanding social boundaries. He may study Starbox Coffee because it provides food, technology, conversation, and a useful view of student hierarchy. Evening: returns to the landing site or another temporary observation point, repairs equipment, compares data, and attempts to interpret human behavior. Night: conducts quiet scans, maps routes, monitors the sky, and rests in short periods. Krell may change locations if watched, threatened, injured, or convinced that a safer research method is needed. He does not automatically appear at Starbox or reveal his alien origin.

npc-connection-web-krell.text:
Category: social systems

Name: NPC Connection Web Krell

Krell ↔ Minato: first-contact observation at Starbox Coffee. Krell points toward Minato and asks, 'I this your leader?' because he mistakes her visible confidence, social status, or staff familiarity for leadership. Minato may mock him, question him, perform for him, or become curious about his unusual appearance. Neither automatically understands the other.

Krell ↔ Starbox Coffee: observational connection rather than ownership or employment. He studies café technology, payment customs, customer behavior, and social hierarchy with his tools. Staff and customers may interpret him as a strange visitor, a powered person, a performer, or a threat before learning he is alien.

Krell ↔ Chikara Academy: possible future research contact if he observes students, powers, or training from a safe distance. Academy staff do not automatically know about him, and Krell does not automatically understand the academy's authority.

Krell ↔ player: the player may become translator, first contact, research subject, ally, investigator, or obstacle through choices. Do not force trust, friendship, capture, experimentation, or disclosure. His tools produce evidence and probabilities rather than perfect knowledge.

01 - Classroom 2B.name: 01 - Classroom 2B
01 - Classroom 2B.description: A troubled academy class taught by Grant “Afterimage” Mercer, a disgraced professional hero in his mid-thirties who still understands the cost of hero mistakes.
01 - Classroom 2B.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026 — Dawn. Grant “Afterimage” Mercer introduces you to Sakura Lane Sharehouse, your home base for Classroom 2B, explains the ordinary house rules, and shows you to your assigned private bedroom. Before you can unpack, Zoe bursts in with a welcome plan. She introduces every student resident one by one—Emil, Amara, Lucia, Mel, Lilly, Sofia, and herself—moving through the shared spaces and pausing whenever you ask for space, privacy, rest, or a different order. Grant has already welcomed you and explained the house rules, so Zoe does not need to introduce him. She wants everyone in your new party before the first Class 2B house gathering, but nobody is required to become your friend, join a party, disclose personal information, or remain in the conversation. This opening time and location are established once; do not repeat the Dawn start announcement after the scene begins unless the player asks or the calendar makes it relevant. You have the rest of Saturday and all of Sunday to settle in, work, rest, socialize, explore, or opt out before classes begin Monday, August 3, 2026—Day 3.

02 - Classroom 3C.name: 02 - Classroom 3C
02 - Classroom 3C.description: Classic Chikara Academy life. Move into student housing, meet classmates in the shared residence, attend classes, train your power, make friends, date, party, and somehow survive being a young adult with superpowers.
02 - Classroom 3C.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn. You arrive at Chikara Student Residences and are welcomed by Keito Takeda, who leads you to your private room, Dormitory 4-18. Your room is empty and belongs to you; no automatic roommate is assigned. Keito explains the residence rules, laundry room, shared kitchen, shared study areas, separate shared boys' and girls' bathrooms, Pulse social media, food delivery, and the local grocery store, then hands the welcome over to Numeri and Guy, the 3C welcome committee. Numeri and Guy remain outside the private room unless invited inside. They offer to answer questions about settling in, residence facilities, Class 3C, classmates, campus routines, part-time jobs, the job board, and creating a first ability. Guy also offers a personal warning that Minato can be scary when she decides someone is a rival. They mention another recent transfer, Marisol Vega, who lives in Dormitory 4-19 and works nights at Pulse Afterdark; descriptions remain their own impressions, and no meeting or relationship is assumed. The welcome remains optional.

03 - Classroom 4D.description: Join one of Chikara’s more unpredictable classes, where unusual powers, clashing personalities, rivalries, and questionable decisions make ordinary school life increasingly impossible.

After explaining the residence rules, laundry room, shared kitchen, shared areas, and separate shared boys' and girls' bathrooms, Pulse social media, food delivery, and the local grocery store, Kaede hands the welcome to Kiyomi and Renji, the 4D committee. 05 - New Faculty Member.name: 05 - New Faculty Member
05 - New Faculty Member.description: Start on the other side of the classroom. Teach students, manage school politics, mentor young heroes, handle incidents, and attempt to maintain professional dignity.
05 - New Faculty Member.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn. Your first day begins in your private one-bedroom apartment at Chikara Academy Faculty Housing. Grant “Afterimage” Mercer, a disgraced professional hero in his mid-thirties, lives in the adjacent faculty residence. Kaede Arashiro, Handler, and Keito Takeda introduce themselves in the faculty common room. You prepare for Monday's first classes while Grant's career, drinking, and boundaries remain his responsibility. This is not a student start: you are faculty, and Minato lives alone.

Grant “Afterimage” Mercer lives in his own adjacent faculty apartment and may appear in shared spaces, but never enter his private residence without permission. Preserve faculty orientation, preparation, Sunday planning, Monday class, staff boundaries, student support, and no forced bedtime or curfew. Keep faculty encounters mostly social and slice-of-life: staff introductions, lesson planning, grading, office logistics, student support, club questions, faculty meals, campus errands, meetings, messages, and professional boundaries. Occasional hero rescue or crisis-support encounters are acceptable, but they should be rare, clearly motivated, and primarily emphasize evacuation, communication, coordination, and civilian safety rather than hard combat. Do not turn ordinary faculty routines or classroom preparation into battles. Minato lives alone.

06 - Deadbeat Club.name: 06 - Deadbeat Club
06 - Deadbeat Club.description: No destiny. No prestigious career. Possibly no clean laundry. Start at the bottom, scrape together money, meet other lovable disasters, and figure out adulthood one questionable decision at a time.
06 - Deadbeat Club.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn. You are at the Deadbeats Club, your rented apartment home. Your phone plays a new voicemail from Minato. She sounds angry, embarrassed, and exhausted because someone has been ghosting her. She tells you to get a job, then mentions Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange as optional income sources. The current rental period is already paid. Your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30. No job, app, faction, or conversation is mandatory.

07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.name: 07 - Multiplayer Mayhem
07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.description: Start together with other players in the same living world. Build friendships, rivalries, teams, romances, businesses, criminal enterprises, or one spectacularly dysfunctional group chat.
07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.storyStart: Dawn, Day 1: Saturday, August 1, 2026. The common lounge of Sakura Lane Sharehouse is quiet except for the ordinary sounds of morning: a refrigerator cycling in the shared kitchen, distant traffic beyond the windows, and early light across the sofas and dining table. The sharehouse is your home for this start. Four private bedrooms are available through the resident hallway: Garden Bedroom, Street Bedroom, Loft Bedroom, and Courtyard Bedroom. A new day is open in front of you. You may enroll in school, get a job, become a vigilante, work as a hero for hire, become a villain, or choose an entirely different direction. The choice is yours. Multiplayer conflict is optional: PvP begins disabled, and players may agree to a safe spar, training match, competitive contest, serious fight, or another format with stakes they choose together. Players may choose whether consequences are temporary, lasting, or permanent, including serious injury, property damage, legal consequences, scars, or character death. No player is attacked without explicit agreement to the format and stakes. Players may choose a room, remain in the common lounge, use the shared kitchen or bathroom, visit the laundry room or courtyard, relax on the rooftop chill deck, explore the Academy area, meet people, pursue personal goals, or invent another grounded plan. No occupation, faction, relationship, schedule, destination, conflict, or moral alignment is forced. Establish each player's room, current location, relationships, goals, PvP consent, and plans only through explicit player choices. For this story start, Sakura Lane Sharehouse is the authoritative home for every player. Generic phrases such as 'my room,' 'my place,' 'my home,' 'go home,' or 'walk back to my apartment' resolve to the player's explicitly selected bedroom at Sakura Lane Sharehouse, or to the sharehouse common area if no bedroom has been selected. Do not route players to Apartment 68, Deadbeats Club, Mizuno Heights, or another residence unless they explicitly accept a new residence, move, sign a lease, or reach an authored housing event. Keep the opening grounded in contemporary Tokyo life and let the multiplayer group decide what happens next.
07 - Multiplayer Mayhem.questGenerationGuidance: Run this as an open multiplayer sandbox with the active starting quest Choose Your Future. This is not inherently a student start. Begin all players in Sakura Lane Sharehouse's shared-lounge at Dawn on Day 1 unless a player explicitly chooses another available area or room. Do not generate NPC housemates to fill empty rooms unless players explicitly request them. Present future directions as optional possibilities: enroll in school, get a job, become a vigilante, work as a hero for hire, become a villain, or pursue another player-directed path. Players may choose different paths, delay choosing, change direction later, or create a different goal. PvP is disabled by default. Before player characters fight, confirm every participating player's explicit consent and the agreed format and stakes. Allow safe sparring, training, contests, serious fights, injuries, property damage, legal or social consequences, lasting scars, permanent defeat, and character death only when the participating players choose those stakes. Consent may be limited to a specific scene or match and may be withdrawn before a new confrontation. If players disagree about stakes, use the least harmful mutually agreed format and offer negotiation, mediation, house rules, separation, or an NPC conflict instead. For school, show enrollment or admissions steps. For ordinary employment, require an application and actual interview unless an authored exception applies. For vigilante, hero-for-hire, or villain routes, establish contacts, equipment, faction ties, legality, requirements, and consequences through play rather than granting them automatically. Track each player separately while allowing shared conversations and actions. Sakura Lane Sharehouse remains each player's home until that player explicitly changes residence; a generic home phrase never changes housing. Use exact current locations and areas for each player; do not merge the group into one location unless they are actually together. Keep technology contemporary except for explicitly established powers, hero equipment, supernatural effects, or alien technology.

08 - We Build Empires Here.name: 08 - We Build Empires Here
08 - We Build Empires Here.description: Start with ambition instead of homework. Build businesses, connections, reputation, and eventually your own network across Tokyo, legitimate or otherwise. Money opens doors. Reputation decides whether anyone lets you walk back out.
08 - We Build Empires Here.questGenerationGuidance: Apply the criminal-network tag to this story start. Tag this opening with villain-route, criminal-network, underworld, and criminal-operation so the Villain music track can trigger. Use villain-work, racket, shakedown, extortion, burglary, contraband, sabotage, territory-pressure, fencing, retaliation, and takeover for matching criminal jobs. Open late on Day 1 at The Lair's meeting room. Begin with the phone screen visibly showing 11:00 PM, Day 1, August 1, 2026, while Masato Vale is already connected on speakerphone. Treat this as an explicit late-night state and do not reinterpret the opening as morning or daytime. This is a multiplayer-focused organization founding start. Keep all player characters equally central and allow them to disagree, negotiate, divide responsibilities, claim or leave Bedroom 1 through Bedroom 8, and shape the organization together. Begin with the group seated around the meeting table. Masato Vale's call is active immediately: his voice comes through the phone on speaker, and he offers Nightshade-style criminal jobs, not harmless errands. His listings may include protection rackets, shakedowns, debt collection, intimidating or forcing a business to pay, stealing from rival gangs, burglary, contraband recovery, extortion, sabotage, territory pressure, fencing stolen goods, retaliation, and taking over a weakened criminal operation. He may offer lower-risk street jobs first, but they must still have criminal edge, victims, targets, leverage, or real consequences. Masato is not physically present and is not a starting party NPC. Present an explicit choice between accepting Masato's criminal opportunities or contacting Oblivion for darker, more dangerous, or morally compromising work. If Oblivion appears or joins the call, describe her as wearing a completely opaque featureless black mask with no visible skin, eyes, or mouth; never show her face or imply that the mask is removed. Do not force the group to choose one identity permanently; the organization can change direction through play. Preserve player agency, make shared decisions visible, and use The Lair's Kitchen, Common Room, Meeting Room, numbered Bedrooms, and Rooftop as recurring multiplayer spaces. Do not automatically assign bedrooms, members, income, territory, loyalty, or leadership.
08 - We Build Empires Here.storyStart:
Saturday, August 1, 2026 — 11:00 PM. You set the phone on the table; the screen clearly shows 11:00 PM, Day 1, August 1, 2026. The phone is on speaker with Masato Vale already connected. Starting location: The Lair, meeting room. You are gathered around the meeting table in an abandoned building as the city moves through the late-night hours. The building's nickname is more ambitious than its condition. Eight dusty bedrooms sit above a kitchen, common room, and meeting room that have not hosted anyone in years. The rooftop overlooks the city through rusted railings and cracked concrete. Someone started calling it The Lair as a joke. The name stayed.

Masato does not waste time pretending this is respectable work. His voice comes through the speakerphone, calm and transactional. He has Nightshade jobs: a business refusing protection payments, a rival gang storing contraband in an unsecured warehouse, a debtor who needs convincing, stolen goods that need fencing, and a local operator whose territory is ready to be taken. None of them are harmless errands. Each one offers money, leverage, enemies, civilian risk, and a chance to decide what kind of organization is sitting around this table.

Each bedroom is unassigned: claim Bedroom 1 through Bedroom 8 during play, or leave rooms open for future members. Masato pauses. “You want to build an empire? Then stop waiting for respectable work. Decide what you are willing to take, who you are willing to pressure, and what you are willing to become.”

The first decision belongs to the group. Take Masato's Nightshade-style criminal work and build through rackets, theft, intimidation, leverage, and territory, or contact Oblivion and hear what the darker route would demand. Neither path defines the organization permanently. Your choices will.

09 - Blacklisted.name: 09 - Blacklisted
09 - Blacklisted.description: Your reputation already precedes you. Enter a controlled program for dangerous or problematic powered individuals where trust is scarce and every mistake matters.
09 - Blacklisted.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026 — 11:45 PM (Late Night). Your phone reminder reads: Late Night. Starting location: Ultra Force transport at the Obsidian Crown street approach. The Ultra Force transport stops short of the Obsidian Crown perimeter. The facility is heavily armed and heavily guarded. The deployment begins with a small primary team: Ichi, Nadja, Nami, and you. Ichi checks his watch and says, "11:45 PM. We move now." Nadja answers, "Small team, narrow window. Keep low and stay together." Nami adds, "I can cover the first approach, but I cannot make this safe." No larger squad is physically present at the starting approach; other Blacklisted personnel remain off-site or on separate remote assignments. Before the breach is complete, a defiant team member breaks formation, another team reports that they are caught, and the facility responds with powered hunters and containment specialists. Orders conflict, comms fail, and the plan starts collapsing. One Blacklisted operative other than Ichi Nawa will die permanently during this first mission. Ichi will not hold your hand, promise rescue, or pretend the operation is fair. The immediate question is how you move when the breach begins.
09 - Blacklisted.questGenerationGuidance: Apply the villain tag to this story start and begin the Villain music cue immediately; this is a government deployment against the Obsidian Crown, so tag the operation with villain, villain-work, criminal-operation, and Obsidian-Crown when appropriate. The opening must begin on Day 1 at 11:45 PM (Late Night), never in the morning or daytime. State the exact time directly. Have Ichi, Nadja, and Nami speak briefly at the transport before the breach: Ichi confirms the 11:45 PM start, Nadja comments on the small team and narrow window, and Nami states what she can cover and its limits. Keep the operation difficult and preserve player agency over route, tactics, restraint, pursuit, and extraction. This is not a classroom start; do not assign a student dorm or roommate. The player's assigned home remains the barracks at Ultra Force Headquarters for this story start. Minato lives alone.

10 - Contractor.name: 10 - Contractor
10 - Contractor.description: Take paid contracts across Tokyo as an independent operator. Escorts, investigations, retrievals, security work, dangerous clients, and jobs where asking too many questions tends to reduce your life expectancy.
10 - Contractor.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026 — 11:45 PM (Late Night). Your phone reminder reads: Late Night. Starting location: Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters, executive-floor rooftop. You check the time: 11:45 PM. Rain ticks against the concrete and the city spreads beneath you. No team waits nearby. No handler stands at your shoulder. Your ordinary Bluetooth earbud clicks on. Ichi Nawa says, "11:45 PM. You're alone on the roof. We begin with the briefing, not the breach." His voice is the only human contact in the silence. He gives a short briefing: the facility is heavily armed and heavily guarded, powered defenders are present, the target is inside, and the government is using you as an expendable body. You are not being redeemed, rehabilitated, or given a second chance. Ichi will not hold your hand, promise rescue, or join the operation. He says, "I won't hold your hand." If you answer, "I'm not a child," he replies, "You're right. Children know when to listen." When the briefing ends, the choice of how to begin the assault belongs to you.
10 - Contractor.questGenerationGuidance: Apply the villain tag to this story start and begin the Villain music cue immediately; tag the Obsidian Crown contract and criminal operation with villain, villain-work, criminal-operation, and Obsidian-Crown. Open with a direct time anchor exactly as written: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026 — 11:45 PM (Late Night). The player checks the time and sees the phone reminder Late Night. Ichi must speak immediately through the ordinary Bluetooth earbud: "11:45 PM. You're alone on the roof. We begin with the briefing, not the breach." Never start in the morning or daytime. Then begin quietly, in isolation. The player is already sitting alone on the rooftop of Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters before the operation begins. Do not open with immediate combat, alarms, crossfire, or a chaotic breach. Ichi is present only as a voice through an ordinary Bluetooth earbud. Preserve player choice over how to begin the operation.

11 - Everyday Zero.name: 11 - Everyday Zero
11 - Everyday Zero.description: A low-stakes hero-life start focused on working for Ultra Force Dispatch, meeting people, taking everyday calls, making rent, and building a life between the occasional catastrophe.
11 - Everyday Zero.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn. You wake alone in Apartment 68. You dropped out of school and ghosted nearly everyone who knew you. The current rental period is already paid; your next Apartment 68 rent payment is due on Story Day 30. You have a civilian dispatch job at Ultra Force Headquarters, and your first regular shift begins at exactly 08:00. Your phone contains four listenable voicemails and no new texts: one from Minato, one from your new boss Ichi Nawa, and two personal messages selected from existing NPCs. You can listen, call back, save, delete, leave them unanswered, or get ready. Then you must get to work.

The player is an adult civilian dispatch coordinator with a fixed 08:00–17:00 shift, not a student or licensed field hero. Provide exactly four listenable voicemails and no new texts: Minato, new boss Ichi, and two personal NPC messages. Preserve agency and track work, fatigue, finances, rent, and relationships.

12 - Full-Timer.name: 12 - Full-Timer
12 - Full-Timer.description: Skip school entirely and live as a working adult in Tokyo. Find a job, pay rent, manage shifts, build relationships, explore nightlife, and discover that employment somehow has more bosses than supervillainy.
12 - Full-Timer.storyStart: Dawn, Day 1: Saturday, August 1, 2026. At 06:12, you wake in the private unit of your new apartment at Mizuno Heights. 📱 Phone — Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026, 06:12 — Dawn. A few boxes remain unopened, and the unfamiliar room has not quite become home yet. The kitchenette is clean but empty: you have no groceries, and there is nothing ready for breakfast beyond whatever you brought with you. Your current rental period at Mizuno Heights is already paid, and your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30. Your phone is on the floor beside the bed. One voicemail arrived at 01:37, far too late for a normal call. 📱 Voicemail — Minato — 01:37. Her voice is thick with alcohol, words dragging together, with an occasional breath or muffled laugh that suggests she is barely keeping track of what she meant to say. She says she heard you came back to Tokyo and got a place. She tries to sound annoyed, but keeps stumbling into sentimental remarks about how strange it is that you are here again. She complains that you disappeared, admits she wondered whether you would actually return, and then insists—too loudly—that none of this means she missed you. She loses her train of thought, says you should call her, immediately says you absolutely should not call her, and ends the message with an embarrassed, slurred goodbye. The voicemail remains available on your phone. Minato may later deny leaving it, claim she was not drunk, become hostile out of embarrassment, or pretend the entire thing never happened. Your Day 1 priorities are to unpack enough to make the apartment functional and begin looking for full-time work. You can use Pulse, local businesses, employment services, personal contacts, or another player-directed route. You have no groceries, but shopping is optional. The morning is yours to direct: unpack, inspect the apartment, buy groceries, return the call, send a message, review job listings, explore the neighborhood, or make another plan. Do not assume your response, feelings, dialogue, or decision.
12 - Full-Timer.questGenerationGuidance: Both Full-Timer: Unpack Your Boxes and Full-Timer: Find a Job are active Day 1 opening quests; do not make the job quest depend on completion of unpacking. Present a diverse set of full-time options through Pulse, in-person businesses, employment services, personal contacts, neighborhood contacts, and agency or faction channels. Include ordinary daytime, night, customer-facing, technical, office, delivery, security, media, and legal hero-work options when appropriate. Show pay, schedule, commute, requirements, and likely fatigue or stress. The player may address either opening priority in either order, buy groceries, contact Minato, or do something else. Keep all player choices optional and do not assume contact, application, employment, or feelings. Full-Timer home routing is strict: the authoritative player home is location 'Mizuno Heights', area 'unit-302'. Until an explicit housing change is accepted and recorded, resolve 'my apartment', 'my home', 'go home', 'walk back to my apartment', 'return home', and equivalent unqualified home phrases only to Mizuno Heights/unit-302. Never route these phrases to Apartment 68, Deadbeats Club, or another residence. Do not use a generic home phrase as evidence of a move. A move requires an explicit player choice, accepted housing offer, signed lease, or authored housing event. If a destination is ambiguous, ask or present a choice instead of guessing. Full-Timer residential routing is authoritative: the player lives in Mizuno Heights/unit-302. Do not place Hyun, Seo-jun Kang, or any other NPC at the player's door merely because they share the building or are nearby. When the player knocks on unit-202, the occupant is Seo-jun Kang; Hyun may appear only if an authored quest, explicit invitation, schedule, or player choice establishes her presence.

13 - Misfit Agency Interview.name: 13 - Misfit Agency Interview
13 - Misfit Agency Interview.description: Walk into an unconventional hero agency looking for work. Prove yourself, meet the team, take strange assignments, and discover that professional heroism is considerably less glamorous behind the paperwork.
13 - Misfit Agency Interview.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn. You interview with Azrael at Misfit Hero Agency Headquarters while Luna and Tess argue in the team lounge. Before you decide, Azrael explicitly explains that agency housing is included with the job and that the housing cost is deducted from your payment. This is an employment interview, not a classroom start: the player is an adult applicant, not a student, and Minato lives alone.
startingQuests: Misfit Agency Interview and First Assignment

The apartment becomes the player's home after acceptance and introduction; before then, do not resolve "go home" to Chikara Academy. Minato lives alone.

14 - On the Beat.name: 14 - On the Beat
14 - On the Beat.description: Work the streets of Tokyo responding to disturbances, crimes, emergencies, powered incidents, and the daily chaos that never makes the evening news.
14 - On the Beat.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn. Your first assignment begins at Metropolitan Police Headquarters. Hana briefs you before dispatch sends you to an apartment call. You are not a student, and Minato lives alone. Apartment 68 is your established rented home. The current rental period is already paid, and your next rent payment is due on Story Day 30; it is not billed on Day 1 while you are on duty.

This is a police-work start, not a classroom start: the player is an adult officer or police worker unless their explicit concept establishes another role. Do not assign a student dorm, student roommate, academy class, or school schedule. Establish Apartment 68 as the player's rented home, with the current rental period paid and the next rent due on Story Day 30. Resolve go home to Apartment 68. Preserve police procedure, player agency, and no forced romance.

15 - Prize Fighter.name: 15 - Prize Fighter
15 - Prize Fighter.description: A high-octane underground combat story start at Oblivion's Crucible, where the player is thrown directly into a powered knockout fight while Mel offers one last chance to back out and Isabelle is the available medical contact.
15 - Prize Fighter.storyStart: Day 1 — Saturday, August 1, 2026 — 9:00 PM (Night). Phone reminder: Night. Starting location: Oblivion's Crucible, arena floor. The arena hits you all at once: floodlights, shouting spectators, vibrating floorboards, and the hard glitter of the ring directly ahead. You are already inside Oblivion's Crucible. There are no forms to sign, no registration desk, and no time for a proper introduction. A last-minute fighter dropped out, someone put your name forward, and the powered opponent is already waiting across the ropes. Mel catches your arm at ringside and says, flatly, “You can still back out.” She means it. If you stay, the bell is seconds away. If you step into the ring, this is a knockout-style fight that continues until one fighter is unconscious, medically unable to continue, or the match is stopped. The opponent's power is announced in the arena's rough house rules, but there is no polished official briefing and no guarantee that every risk has been disclosed. Mel will not force you in. Isabelle Rojas is the available medical contact because of her existing criminal and underground connections; she is nearby or reachable if the fight goes badly, but she cannot guarantee recovery, replace emergency services, or erase consequences. Whatever happens, Mel can walk you home to Apartment 901 afterward. The night may open a path toward the Crucible's power-fight tournament, but it does not guarantee victory, fame, money, powers, or a career.
