Bio-Weapon.name: Bio-Weapon
Bio-Weapon.description: A biological or partly biological being deliberately developed or adapted as a weapon; autonomy and conditioning vary.

Construct.name: Construct
Construct.description: A created entity made from matter, energy, code, ritual, technology, or magic to perform a function; consciousness varies.

Living Weapon.name: Living Weapon
Living Weapon.description: A sentient or semi-sentient being whose body, powers, or designed purpose centers on use as a weapon; preserve agency.

Summoned Creature.name: Summoned Creature
Summoned Creature.description: A creature brought into the world through summoning, contract, ritual, ability, or gateway; autonomy and duration must be established.

Cursed Creature.name: Cursed Creature
Cursed Creature.description: A creature altered, created, or empowered by a curse, cursed object, ritual, or supernatural contamination.

Possessed Animal.name: Possessed Animal
Possessed Animal.description: An animal influenced, inhabited, controlled, or altered by a spirit, curse, power, or other entity.

Empowered Animal.name: Empowered Animal
Empowered Animal.description: An animal enhanced by a power, mutation, experiment, artifact, curse, or supernatural influence; intelligence and agency vary.

Giant Creature.name: Giant Creature
Giant Creature.description: A creature whose unusual size shapes movement, habitat, danger, resource needs, and interaction with infrastructure.

Swarm Creature.name: Swarm Creature
Swarm Creature.description: A collective creature made of many organisms or units acting together as one encounter identity; define cohesion and intelligence.

Parasite Host.name: Parasite Host
Parasite Host.description: A person or creature carrying a parasite affecting body, behavior, powers, health, or perception; host and parasite interests may differ.

Feral Parasite Host.name: Feral Parasite Host
Feral Parasite Host.description: A parasite host whose infection or parasite influence severely disrupts judgment, behavior, or self-control; preserve agency distinctions.

Independent Parasite.name: Independent Parasite
Independent Parasite.description: A parasite capable of acting, surviving, communicating, or pursuing goals independently of a host.

Symbiotic Parasite.name: Symbiotic Parasite
Symbiotic Parasite.description: A parasite in a mutually beneficial, negotiated, or interdependent relationship with a host; benefits, costs, and consent vary.

Alien Creature.name: Alien Creature
Alien Creature.description: A nonhuman being originating outside Earth or ordinary local biology with individualized culture, anatomy, motives, and adaptation.

Alien Humanoid.name: Alien Humanoid
Alien Humanoid.description: A sentient alien with broadly humanoid presentation but nonhuman origins, biology, culture, and assumptions.

Demon.name: Demon
Demon.description: A supernatural being associated with demonic, infernal, destructive, contractual, or otherworldly traditions; motives and powers vary.

Minor Demon.name: Minor Demon
Minor Demon.description: A lower-scale demon with limited authority, influence, power, or manifestation compared with greater entities.

Greater Demon.name: Greater Demon
Greater Demon.description: A powerful demon with significant authority, age, territory, knowledge, contract leverage, or supernatural influence.

Demon Contractor.name: Demon Contractor
Demon Contractor.description: A person or entity bound to a demon through an explicit bargain, contract, debt, exchange, or coercive arrangement.

Celestial Entity.name: Celestial Entity
Celestial Entity.description: A powerful being associated with celestial, divine, astral, or cosmic forces; authority and limits must be individualized.

Otherworld Entity.name: Otherworld Entity
Otherworld Entity.description: A being from a realm, plane, dimension, dream, afterlife, or reality outside ordinary Earth whose rules must be established.

Dimensional Anomaly.name: Dimensional Anomaly
Dimensional Anomaly.description: A person, creature, phenomenon, or entity resulting from a breach, overlap, distortion, or instability between dimensions or realities.

Yōkai Noble.name: Yōkai Noble
Yōkai Noble.description: A yōkai with recognized status within a supernatural hierarchy whose authority, etiquette, resources, and obligations depend on its community.

Yōkai Criminal.name: Yōkai Criminal
Yōkai Criminal.description: A yōkai involved in theft, extortion, trafficking, predation, sabotage, illicit trade, or other criminal activity.

Yōkai Exorcist.name: Yōkai Exorcist
Yōkai Exorcist.description: A human or supernatural specialist who identifies, negotiates with, contains, banishes, or handles yōkai through individualized methods.

Possessing Spirit.name: Possessing Spirit
Possessing Spirit.description: A spirit inhabiting, influencing, or attempting to control a host, object, or location; possession rules and consent must be established.

Restless Ghost.name: Restless Ghost
Restless Ghost.description: A deceased person's spirit unable to move on because of unresolved attachment, confusion, injustice, duty, fear, or another cause.

Vengeful Spirit.name: Vengeful Spirit
Vengeful Spirit.description: A spirit driven by grievance, perceived injustice, betrayal, abuse, or revenge; its memory may be incomplete or distorted.

Guardian Spirit.name: Guardian Spirit
Guardian Spirit.description: A spirit protecting a person, family, location, object, community, or promise through an established duty or bond.

Urban Legend Entity.name: Urban Legend Entity
Urban Legend Entity.description: A supernatural entity shaped or sustained by a circulating story, rumor, warning, media pattern, or modern legend.

Haunting.name: Haunting
Haunting.description: A supernatural presence centered on a location, object, routine, memory, or repeated disturbance that may lack a stable body.

Cursed Spirit.name: Cursed Spirit
Cursed Spirit.description: A spirit formed, altered, or empowered by curse energy, harmful emotion, ritual consequence, or cursed phenomena.

Shikigami.name: Shikigami
Shikigami.description: A summoned, shaped, bound, or contracted spiritual servant whose capabilities depend on creator, binding, purpose, and independence.

Tsukumogami.name: Tsukumogami
Tsukumogami.description: A supernatural being associated with an object that developed identity, agency, memory, or spirit through age, treatment, history, or influence.

Oni.name: Oni
Oni.description: A powerful supernatural being with individualized traits, culture, motives, abilities, and relationship to humans and other spirits.

Kitsune.name: Kitsune
Kitsune.description: A fox-associated supernatural being involving individualized transformation, intelligence, trickery, guardianship, trade, ritual, or rivalry.

Tanuki.name: Tanuki
Tanuki.description: A tanuki-like supernatural being associated with transformation, mischief, adaptation, trade, hospitality, or local folklore.

Tengu.name: Tengu
Tengu.description: A tengu-like supernatural being associated with mountains, martial skill, pride, discipline, trickery, asceticism, or territorial authority.

Kappa.name: Kappa
Kappa.description: A water-associated supernatural being whose behavior, customs, danger, and human relationship depend on habitat, personality, and local tradition.

Jorōgumo.name: Jorōgumo
Jorōgumo.description: A spider-associated supernatural being capable of individualized transformation, deception, predation, protection, artistry, or social manipulation.

Yuki-onna.name: Yuki-onna
Yuki-onna.description: A snow- or winter-associated supernatural being with individualized motives, powers, emotional range, and relationship to cold and humans.

Nekomata.name: Nekomata
Nekomata.description: A cat-associated supernatural being involving age, transformation, spirits, independence, domestic ties, revenge, or trickery.

Bakeneko.name: Bakeneko
Bakeneko.description: A transformed or supernatural cat-being with individualized intelligence, habits, powers, social ties, and human relationships.

Nurikabe.name: Nurikabe
Nurikabe.description: A wall-like supernatural entity associated with obstruction, boundaries, routes, confinement, or misdirection.

Kuchisake-onna-Type Urban Legend.name: Kuchisake-onna-Type Urban Legend
Kuchisake-onna-Type Urban Legend.description: A modern urban-legend entity using a recognizable encounter pattern, question, rumor, or appearance; exact rules must be established.

Hanako-Type School Spirit.name: Hanako-Type School Spirit
Hanako-Type School Spirit.description: A school-bound spirit associated with a restroom, classroom, rumor, ritual, student tradition, or campus mystery.

Monster.name: Monster
Monster.description: A dangerous or unusual creature whose anatomy, intelligence, origin, behavior, and abilities must be individualized.

Minor Monster.name: Minor Monster
Minor Monster.description: A lower-scale creature with limited threat, territory, intelligence, or abilities relative to major monsters.

Elite Monster.name: Elite Monster
Elite Monster.description: A notably capable or specialized creature with superior abilities, adaptations, intelligence, or territory.

Boss Monster.name: Boss Monster
Boss Monster.description: A major creature built around a distinctive threat, territory, mechanic, objective, or encounter identity within active location rules.

Mutant.name: Mutant
Mutant.description: A person or creature altered by mutation, power effects, experiments, exposure, inheritance, or another established cause.

Powered Civilian.name: Powered Civilian
Powered Civilian.description: A person with abilities whose primary life is civilian rather than heroic, criminal, or institutional.

Unregistered Powered Person.name: Unregistered Powered Person
Unregistered Powered Person.description: A powered person whose abilities are not registered with the relevant authorities or institutions; registration status does not determine morality.

Power Criminal.name: Power Criminal
Power Criminal.description: A powered person who commits, facilitates, or supports crime; powers alone do not determine methods, motives, or severity.

Power Addict.name: Power Addict
Power Addict.description: A person whose use of powers, power-enhancing substances, power-related experiences, or ability expression has become compulsive or harmful.

Power Experiment.name: Power Experiment
Power Experiment.description: A person or being altered, tested, enhanced, suppressed, or studied through power-related experimentation.

Power Research Subject.name: Power Research Subject
Power Research Subject.description: A person or being serving as an observed or studied subject in ability, mutation, energy, or suppression research.

Power Instructor.name: Power Instructor
Power Instructor.description: A teacher or coach who trains people in safe, controlled, ethical, or tactical use of abilities.

Power Specialist.name: Power Specialist
Power Specialist.description: A professional whose expertise centers on a particular ability category, power application, countermeasure, or powered situation.

Power Suppression Officer.name: Power Suppression Officer
Power Suppression Officer.description: An authorized officer trained to contain, regulate, suppress, or safely respond to dangerous ability use.

Power Broker.name: Power Broker
Power Broker.description: A person who arranges access to powered people, ability services, enhancement, suppression, information, equipment, or contracts.

Power Cultist.name: Power Cultist
Power Cultist.description: A member of a movement that treats abilities, powered people, power inheritance, or power use as a central doctrine or object of devotion.

Unstable Powered Person.name: Unstable Powered Person
Unstable Powered Person.description: A powered person whose abilities, control, health, judgment, or circumstances are currently unreliable or dangerous.

Runaway Powered Teen.name: Runaway Powered Teen
Runaway Powered Teen.description: A teenage powered person living outside expected guardianship, schooling, or institutional support while navigating ability-related risks.

Celebrity Powered Person.name: Celebrity Powered Person
Celebrity Powered Person.description: A powered public figure whose fame, career, visibility, branding, and ability affect their daily life and relationships.

Underground Fighter.name: Underground Fighter
Underground Fighter.description: A combatant participating in unauthorized, hidden, or illicit powered or non-powered fights outside regulated competition.

Prize Fighter.name: Prize Fighter
Prize Fighter.description: A professional combatant who fights for purses, rankings, contracts, or public competition under established rules or arrangements.

Arena Champion.name: Arena Champion
Arena Champion.description: A highly successful combatant recognized for dominance, title defenses, spectacle, or status within an arena or organized fighting circuit.

Power Mercenary.name: Power Mercenary
Power Mercenary.description: A powered contractor who accepts paid security, combat, retrieval, intimidation, protection, or other assignments.

Power Assassin.name: Power Assassin
Power Assassin.description: A powered covert killer or target specialist whose abilities support clandestine assignments; motives and contracts must be individualized.

Quest Giver.name: Quest Giver
Quest Giver.description: An NPC who presents a request, opportunity, problem, investigation, or mission that can guide play.

Client.name: Client
Client.description: A person or organization commissioning assistance, work, protection, investigation, delivery, or another service.

Witness.name: Witness
Witness.description: A person who observed, heard, experienced, or possesses relevant evidence about an event.

Victim.name: Victim
Victim.description: A person harmed, exploited, threatened, displaced, or otherwise affected by an established wrongdoing or crisis.

Missing Person.name: Missing Person
Missing Person.description: A person whose location is unknown to relevant people and whose absence creates an active search, concern, or mystery.

Hostage.name: Hostage
Hostage.description: A person held or threatened to influence another person, group, institution, negotiation, or outcome.

Rival.name: Rival
Rival.description: A recurring competitor whose goals, methods, resources, or relationship create meaningful opposition without requiring villainy.

Mentor.name: Mentor
Mentor.description: A person who guides another through instruction, example, feedback, resources, protection, or hard-earned experience.

Trainer.name: Trainer
Trainer.description: A person who develops another character's practical, physical, intellectual, social, or ability-related competence.

Recruiter.name: Recruiter
Recruiter.description: A person seeking members, employees, students, contractors, allies, followers, or participants for a group or opportunity.

Handler.name: Handler
Handler.description: A coordinator responsible for directing, briefing, supporting, monitoring, or managing another operative or participant.

Dispatcher.name: Dispatcher
Dispatcher.description: A coordinator who receives requests, tracks situations, assigns responders, and relays operational information.

Broker.name: Broker
Broker.description: An intermediary who connects people, deals, opportunities, information, goods, services, or agreements.

Contractor.name: Contractor
Contractor.description: A person working under an agreement to provide defined labor, expertise, protection, delivery, investigation, or another service.

Employer.name: Employer
Employer.description: A person or representative responsible for offering, supervising, funding, or directing paid work.

Coworker.name: Coworker
Coworker.description: A person sharing a workplace, employer, professional environment, or recurring work responsibilities with another character.

Classmate.name: Classmate
Classmate.description: A student sharing a course, cohort, school, training program, or recurring educational environment with another character.

Neighbor.name: Neighbor
Neighbor.description: A person living or regularly operating near another character in the same building, block, district, or community.

Roommate.name: Roommate
Roommate.description: A person sharing a residence, sleeping space, household, or domestic arrangement with another character.

Club Member.name: Club Member
Club Member.description: A participant in a recurring social, hobby, school, professional, athletic, or cultural club.

Love Interest.name: Love Interest
Love Interest.description: A character positioned as a possible romantic or emotionally intimate connection; attraction and consent remain individualized and never automatic.

Ex.name: Ex
Ex.description: A former romantic or intimate partner whose past relationship remains relevant to current circumstances.

Fan.name: Fan
Fan.description: A person strongly interested in, admiring, following, or supporting another person, group, work, or public identity.

Stalker.name: Stalker
Stalker.description: A person persistently monitoring, pursuing, contacting, or intruding on another person's life without welcome or consent.

Rival Hero.name: Rival Hero
Rival Hero.description: A heroic or protective figure whose goals, reputation, methods, career, or personal relationship creates recurring competition with another hero.

Rival Villain.name: Rival Villain
Rival Villain.description: A criminal or antagonistic figure whose goals, territory, resources, methods, or reputation conflict with another villain.

Turned.name: Turned
Turned.description: A human transformed by Turned biology. Turned usually appear human in daily life but require human blood or flesh to remain healthy; ordinary food is rejected. Severe hunger can cause Hunger Eyes: black eye whites with vivid blood-red irises. Turned possess enhanced physical ability, recovery, and a unique living organic predatory manifestation that may remain concealed until deliberately revealed or triggered by authored circumstances. Turned can be friendly, neutral, concealed, cooperative, feral, or hostile; biology does not determine morality, faction, personality, consent, or targets. Variants include cooperative donor, concealed civilian, mutual-aid medic, feral Turned, Vermine operative, independent survivor, and captured or hunted Turned.

Alien Researcher.name: Alien Researcher
Alien Researcher.description: An extraterrestrial visitor studying Earth, its people, technology, powers, and institutions. Alien Researchers may be peaceful, curious, confused, exploitative, or dangerous depending on their mission and ethics. Their unusual appearance and technology can attract attention, but they are not automatically hostile or understood. They may struggle with local languages, laws, customs, consent, medicine, and social cues.

health.name: health
health.usageInstructions: Tracks physical health. Injuries and combat can reduce it; treatment, recovery, and rest restore it.

Combat Energy.name: Combat Energy
Combat Energy.usageInstructions:
### Combat Energy
The pool combat techniques spend. Deduct it only when an ability is actually used, and only the number that ability's description states ("Costs N Combat Energy"); an ability that says it costs none costs none.

### Gain
- A Steady Strike that meaningfully connects, a successful defence, a clean reposition: +1
- Combat Breath and abilities that say they restore it: what they say
- The engine returns one point each turn by itself (rechargeRate): never add another for the turn passing

### Do not deduct when
- An ability is named, discussed or prepared but not used
- The action is an ordinary attack, movement or skill check with no ability behind it
- Combat is over

### At zero
An ability that costs Combat Energy cannot be used; the character falls back on Steady Strike, plain actions and Combat Breath until it returns.

Ultimate Charge.name: Ultimate Charge
Ultimate Charge.usageInstructions:
### Ultimate Charge
The meter an ultimate spends whole. It builds only in combat and only from what the fight actually contains.

### Build
- A hit that meaningfully connects: +10
- Taking a serious hit, or taking a hit meant for an ally: +15
- Breaking an enemy's Guard, interrupting an ability, or completing a combat objective: +15
- Nothing outside combat builds it; rest does not fill it and does not empty it

### Spend
An ultimate needs the FULL meter: a character below 100 cannot use one, and the attempt fails as an ordinary action. When an ultimate is used, set the meter to 0 and apply the ability's Aftermath sentence afterwards.

### Do not change when
- Combat is described but this character neither struck nor was struck
- The character talks, moves or waits without engaging

Guard.name: Guard
Guard.usageInstructions:
### Guard
A narrator-tracked buffer of defensive stability, separate from health. When a hit is described as blocked, turned, absorbed or braced against, deduct Guard instead of narrating a wound; when a hit lands clean, health takes it and Guard is untouched.

### Deduct when
- A blocked or absorbed hit: 5-10
- A Heavy Commit or a heavy blow absorbed: 10-15
- An ability says it chips or reduces Guard: 5; costs a large share of Guard: 10-15; breaks Guard: to 0; or by what it says

### Guard-broken
At 0 the character is Guard-broken: they cannot use Guard-dependent abilities (Answering Strike, Guarded Stance's stored answer), and abilities that say they finish a Guard-broken target may. Narrate the opening.

### Recover
- Guarded Stance, Recover Guard, Combat Breath and abilities that say so: what they say
- A turn spent wholly on defence with nothing landing: +5
- Rest: full

### Do not deduct when
- The hit landed clean (that is health)
- Combat is over or the character is not engaged

Power Strain.name: Power Strain
Power Strain.usageInstructions: Represents accumulated fatigue from using a custom power. Increase it when the player uses demanding techniques. Reduce it through rest, recovery, food, medical care, and appropriate story outcomes. Low strain permits normal control; high strain increases risk, limits major techniques, and can cause fatigue, injury, collateral effects, or temporary power lockout.

Hero Reputation.name: Hero Reputation
Hero Reputation.usageInstructions: Represents public trust in the player's conduct as an aspiring hero. Increase it for rescues, teamwork, control, honest accountability, and protecting civilians. Decrease it for reckless collateral damage, abandonment, deception, unnecessary force, or repeated discipline. Use it alongside grades, attendance, relationships, and school discipline; it is not a simple morality score.

Yen.name: Yen
Yen.usageInstructions: Everyday currency used for train fares, food, shopping, dates, housing, support gear, and other purchases. Every story start begins with ¥200,000 unless that story start explicitly defines a different amount. Deduct yen when a purchase is made, pay completed part-time and full-time shifts at shift end, and show the updated balance. The maximum Yen balance is ¥999,999,999.

Energy.name: Energy
Energy.usageInstructions: Daily stamina drains with time, strenuous activity, training, combat, travel, social demands, and demanding power use. Harmless everyday power use costs little or no Energy. Low Energy causes fatigue, increases Power Strain, and can impair concentration and performance. At zero, require sleep or substantial rest. Sleep and substantial rest restore Energy; show the approximate cost before meaningful activities.

Stress.name: Stress
Stress.usageInstructions: Tracks mental and emotional pressure for players and NPCs from exams, conflict, failure, injury, debt, missed obligations, public scrutiny, power instability, and poor sleep. Reduce it through sleep, rest, supportive relationships, enjoyable activities, meals, counseling, medical care, safe power practice, and healthy boundaries. Stress is not a diagnosis. At elevated levels, concentration, patience, availability, social scenes, power control, and recovery may suffer; at high levels, use proportional withdrawal, mistakes, conflict, absence, or help-seeking. Never force a breakdown, diagnose a character, or override player choices.

Fame.name: Fame
Fame.usageInstructions: Fame measures public visibility, recognition, media reach, and audience attention. Track it separately from Hero Reputation: Fame does not equal trust, morality, or competence. Fame rises through posts, club activity, public appearances, rescues, performances, interviews, sponsorships, and viral moments. Controversy can raise Fame while increasing scrutiny and instability. Fame falls through inactivity, scandals, misinformation, public failures, or loss of interest. Cap Fame at 100; never exceed the cap. Show major changes and explain the cause.

Followers.name: Followers
Followers.usageInstructions: Followers are the player's Pulse audience. Increase the account slowly at first. Base growth comes from consistent activity, useful posts, club participation, public appearances, rescues, performances, networking, and sponsorships. Multiply or accelerate growth as Hero Reputation improves: low Reputation produces slow and fragile growth, while high Reputation makes positive events spread faster and retain more followers. Fame, post visibility, audience size, controversy, inactivity, misinformation, and public failures also affect gains or losses. Do not treat Followers as identical to Fame or Hero Reputation; show major changes and their causes.

Villain Reputation.name: Villain Reputation
Villain Reputation.usageInstructions: Villain Reputation measures recognition, credibility, and standing within criminal networks and among rival villains. Increase it through successful jobs, disciplined leadership, protection of allies, strategic escalation, territory, recruits, and surviving betrayals. Decrease it through public failure, disloyalty, unnecessary chaos, capture, or loss of influence. Track it separately from Infamy: Reputation is respect within the underworld, not public fear. Show major changes and explain the cause.

Infamy.name: Infamy
Infamy.usageInstructions: Infamy measures public fear, notoriety, scandal, and the severity of a villain's known crimes. Increase it through visible crimes, threats, sabotage, dramatic escapes, hostile takeovers, and media exposure. Decrease it through obscurity, clean cover identities, failed plots, public acts of protection, or credible reform. Track it separately from Villain Reputation: Infamy is public notoriety, while Villain Reputation is underworld standing. Show major changes and explain the cause.

Legal Heat.name: Legal Heat
Legal Heat.usageInstructions: Tracks law-enforcement and government attention caused by evidence, witnesses, repeated offenses, collateral damage, unauthorized activity, or faction exposure. Lower through time, discretion, cooperation, legal strategy, or plausible cover; do not treat it as universal public reputation.

Faction Heat.name: Faction Heat
Faction Heat.usageInstructions: Tracks active hostility, surveillance, retaliation, and political pressure from factions that know or suspect the character's actions. It is faction-specific in narrative even when represented by this general resource. Lower through negotiation, payment, changed behavior, evidence, or time when plausible.

Contract Reputation.name: Contract Reputation
Contract Reputation.usageInstructions: Tracks professional reliability, discretion, client satisfaction, successful outcomes, collateral damage, and repeat access for Hero for Hire and Nightshade work. Interpret separately by client network and job type; do not let one score erase distinct faction opinions.

Minato Training Rivalry.name: Minato Training Rivalry
Minato Training Rivalry.questStatement: Minato challenges the player to prove that their power is more than reckless potential.
Minato Training Rivalry.mainObjective: Complete a controlled training session with Minato without losing control or abandoning the exercise.

completionCondition.query: The player completes a controlled training session with Minato and earns her begrudging respect.

Minato Training Rivalry.questDesignBrief: A first relationship milestone for Minato. Use partner sparring, power control, tactical choices, and Power Strain management. The player can succeed through combat, defense, rescue, strategy, or restraint rather than simply overpowering Minato.

control_power.text: Complete the training exercise while managing power control and Power Strain.

earn_respect.text: Earn Minato's begrudging respect through discipline, adaptability, or courage.

Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.name: Chikara Academy Cultural Festival
Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.questStatement: The academy's cultural festival is approaching, and every club must choose how it will contribute while balancing preparation, relationships, reputation, and an emerging mystery.
Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.mainObjective: Help shape the Cultural Festival and respond to whatever threatens its success.

completionCondition.query: The Chikara Academy Cultural Festival concludes and its major performances, club projects, and crisis have been resolved.

Chikara Academy Cultural Festival.questDesignBrief: A multi-day school-life event connecting all clubs, friendships, rivalries, romance, reputation, independent NPC plans, and a possible hidden threat. The player may participate heavily, help one club, attend socially, investigate, work, or ignore preparations. Do not require one correct solution; reflect attendance, club involvement, relationships, grades, choices, and consequences.

choose_role.text: Choose how to participate in the Cultural Festival.

prepare_event.text: Help prepare a club project, performance, stall, demonstration, or investigation.

handle_crisis.text: Respond to the festival's major conflict or hidden crisis.

festival_outcome.text: See the Cultural Festival through to its conclusion.

Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.name: Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review
Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.questStatement: After the First-Impression Test Tournament, faculty review each student's performance and assign a primary academy class.
Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.mainObjective: Receive the faculty's performance-based class placement.

review_performance.text: Attend the evening faculty review of tactics, restraint, rescue instincts, control, communication, and conduct.

receive_placement.text: Receive a primary placement in Rescue, Support, Strike, Investigation, Media, or Agency Operations Class.

review_requirements.text: Learn the assessment standards, schedule, and consequences attached to the placement.

completionCondition.query: Faculty review the player's Day 1 tournament performance and assign a primary academy class.

Day 1: Faculty Class Placement Review.questDesignBrief: Use the tournament outcome and observed conduct to assign one primary academy class. Do not allow arbitrary free selection. Explain the evidence and let the player respond without changing the placement unless results were genuinely close. Establish the class schedule, core skill, first practical assessment, and transfer conditions.

Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.name: Semester 1 Midterm Assessments
Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.questStatement: The first semester reaches its midpoint, bringing written exams, a class-specific practical assessment, and a faculty progress review.
Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.mainObjective: Complete the midterm assessment cycle and respond to the faculty progress report.

prepare_midterms.text: Choose how to prepare through study, tutoring, practice, rest, work, clubs, or social support.

take_written_exam.text: Complete the written theory and hero-law examination.

complete_practical.text: Complete the practical assessment for the student's assigned academy class.

attend_review.text: Attend the faculty progress review and receive feedback.

completionCondition.query: The player completes the Semester 1 midterm written and practical assessments and receives a faculty progress report.

Semester 1 Midterm Assessments.questDesignBrief: Offer preparation choices with visible time, Energy, Stress, and schedule tradeoffs. Written exams test theory, hero law, and judgment. Practical assessment reflects the student's assigned class: Rescue uses evacuation and first aid; Support uses safe gear troubleshooting; Strike uses controlled pursuit and restraint; Investigation uses evidence and deduction; Media uses crisis communication and Pulse judgment; Agency Operations uses dispatch and coordination. Resolve results from preparation, skills, attributes, attendance, health, conduct, and choices. Show consequences without inventing player thoughts or decisions.

Semester 1 Final Assessments.name: Semester 1 Final Assessments
Semester 1 Final Assessments.questStatement: The first semester closes with final exams, a class practical, and a formal review of the student's progress.
Semester 1 Final Assessments.mainObjective: Complete the semester finals and secure a satisfactory progress result.

prepare_finals.text: Plan final preparation around study, training, work, clubs, relationships, and recovery.

complete_final_practical.text: Complete the assigned class's final practical assessment.

receive_report.text: Receive the semester report and next-term recommendations.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Semester 1 final assessments and receives a semester report with next-term recommendations.

Semester 1 Final Assessments.questDesignBrief: Use cumulative attendance, grades, skills, class practical performance, conduct, Hero Reputation, Stress, Energy, health, clubs, jobs, and preparation. Award scholarships, internships, teacher approval, remediation, probation, or other consequences as earned. Preserve player agency and make outcomes reflect choices rather than a single combat result.

Villainous: First Contact.name: Villainous: First Contact
Villainous: First Contact.questStatement: Travel to Oblivion's Crucible and speak with Oblivion.

speak_with_oblivion.text: Speak with Oblivion in the oblivion-box.

completionCondition.query: The player has traveled to Oblivion's Crucible and completed a conversation with Oblivion in oblivion-box.

Villainous: First Contact.questDesignBrief: This is the Villainous opening quest and is active immediately at the Apartment 801 rooftop start. Oblivion has already called and said "I summon you." She sends a car to Apartment 801 as an optional transportation offer, but the player may choose another way to travel or remain behind. The player must travel to Oblivion's Crucible and speak with Oblivion in the oblivion-box. Completing that conversation completes Villainous: First Contact. Immediately after completion, activate a separate follow-up quest in which Oblivion gives the player an assignment to find their first hire for her criminal network. Do not include the first-hire assignment as an objective of this quest, and do not require the player to accept it for this quest to complete. Preserve player agency around travel, the conversation, recruitment, promises, consent, violence, and refusal.

Villainous: Claim the Block.name: Villainous: Claim the Block
Villainous: Claim the Block.questStatement: A small Kurokawa territory is available, but local residents, petty criminals, and an established crew all believe it belongs to them.
Villainous: Claim the Block.mainObjective: Secure a first piece of territory without destroying its value.

survey_territory.text: Survey the Kurokawa side streets around the safehouse and identify the territory's pressure points.

resolve_rivalry.text: Resolve the local crew's challenge through negotiation, deception, protection, or force.

establish_presence.text: Establish a presence that makes the territory useful to your growing network.

completionCondition.query: The player secures a small Kurokawa territory and establishes a sustainable criminal presence there.

Villainous: Claim the Block.questDesignBrief: Second Villainous quest. The territory should become more than a fight: protection, extortion, mutual aid, information control, and reputation all create different outcomes.

Villainous: The First Cut.name: Villainous: The First Cut
Villainous: The First Cut.questStatement: An empire needs income. Three opportunities are available: a quiet black-market route, a protection arrangement, or a risky information sale.
Villainous: The First Cut.mainObjective: Create the network's first dependable income stream.

select_operation.text: Choose an income operation using Kurokawa Ward Station, Pulse Media Tower, or Tideway Market.

run_operation.text: Complete the operation while protecting your contact network and safehouse.

secure_profit.text: Bring the first profit back to the Kurokawa apartment and decide how to spend it.

completionCondition.query: The player completes a first criminal operation and establishes a dependable income stream for the network.

Villainous: The First Cut.questDesignBrief: Third Villainous quest. Offer distinct criminal playstyles: logistics through the night line, influence through media information, or harbor-market smuggling. Keep consequences visible and avoid making violence mandatory.

Villainous: Eyes in the City.name: Villainous: Eyes in the City
Villainous: Eyes in the City.questStatement: Someone is tracking the network's movements. You need information before the first serious rival or hero response arrives.
Villainous: Eyes in the City.mainObjective: Build an information network and identify the watcher.

gather_rumors.text: Gather rumors from Oblivion's Crucible, Tokyo Underground Mall, or Pulse Media Tower.

identify_watcher.text: Identify who is monitoring the network and why.

choose_response.text: Choose whether to misdirect, recruit, expose, or confront the watcher.

completionCondition.query: The player identifies the watcher and responds in a way that expands or protects the criminal network.

Villainous: Eyes in the City.questDesignBrief: Fourth Villainous quest. Establish that growth creates attention. The watcher may be a rival crew, investigator, journalist, informant, or potential recruit depending on player choices.

Deadbeat: First Morning.name: Deadbeat: First Morning
Deadbeat: First Morning.questStatement: The Kurokawa apartment has shelter but no food, no working phone, and no money for the day. Two kinds of work may be available: Hero-for-Hire jobs in the public city, or paid assignments through Oblivion's Crucible.
Deadbeat: First Morning.mainObjective: Find a way to get through the first morning.

check_resources.text: Search the empty apartment for anything useful and assess what must be handled first.

choose_route.text: Choose between seeking a Hero-for-Hire job or visiting the Crucible for a paid assignment.

survive_day.text: Return to the apartment with enough support to make it through the day.

completionCondition.query: The player secures basic food or support and chooses whether to pursue Hero-for-Hire work or a paid Crucible assignment.

Deadbeat: First Morning.questDesignBrief: Opening Deadbeat quest. Keep the stakes intimate and practical: hunger, isolation, a dead phone, and an overdue notice. Present Hero-for-Hire work as a lawful path to income and reputation, and the Crucible as a dangerous path to faster money and underworld connections. Do not assume the player is helpless; let creativity, old skills, contacts, and powers matter.

Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.name: Deadbeat: Find a Way Back
Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.questStatement: An overdue notice leaves the apartment's future uncertain. The player needs income before the safehouse becomes another place they lose.
Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.mainObjective: Secure a sustainable source of income.

review_options.text: Review Hero-for-Hire listings or discreet paid assignments available through Oblivion's Crucible.

choose_work.text: Choose a public Hero-for-Hire contract or an underground Crucible job.

earn_first_pay.text: Complete the first contract or assignment and secure immediate income.

completionCondition.query: The player chooses Hero-for-Hire work or a Crucible job and earns enough initial income to keep the Kurokawa apartment.

Deadbeat: Find a Way Back.questDesignBrief: Make the central Deadbeat choice explicit. Hero-for-Hire work can lead to rescue, escort, protection, and emergency contracts through public contacts. Crucible jobs can involve retrieval, protection, sabotage, courier work, or information exchange. Track public trust, underworld access, secrecy, and consequences through the player's choices. Neither path should be treated as automatically correct.

Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.name: Deadbeat: A Place to Stand
Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.questStatement: Survival is no longer the only problem. The player must decide whether the Kurokawa apartment is temporary shelter, a home, or the first place in a new life.
Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.mainObjective: Choose a direction for the next chapter.

review_path.text: Review the consequences of the first day's choices and identify a viable next direction.

choose_identity.text: Choose whether to pursue legitimate stability, hero-adjacent service, independence, or underground opportunity.

commit_direction.text: Take a concrete step that makes the chosen direction real.

completionCondition.query: The player commits to a direction that establishes the next phase of the Deadbeat story.

Deadbeat: A Place to Stand.questDesignBrief: Arc transition quest. The player is not required to return to school. Branch toward work, community service, old relationships, investigative opportunities, or the underworld based on choices and consequences.

Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom.name: Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom
Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom.questStatement: A conditional-freedom redemption mission sends former villains to kill or capture a dangerous supervillain target, then grants them broader movement and choice between assignments in exchange for completing objectives and reporting afterward.

reach_target.text: Reach Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters as a conditional-freedom redemption team during Late Night on Day 1.

breach_agency.text: Fight through the agency's defenses while protecting civilians and following the redemption program's rules.

assess_team.text: Demonstrate control, teamwork, restraint, and hero-worthy judgment under pressure.

eliminate_or_capture.text: Kill or capture the designated supervillain target.

survive_loss.text: Endure the permanent death of one randomly selected Blacklisted operative other than Ichi Nawa.

extract.text: Complete extraction, submit the mission report, and continue under conditional freedom with the target secured or confirmed dead.

completionCondition.query: The Blacklisted redemption team reaches Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters during Late Night on Day 1, fights through its defenses, demonstrates judgment under pressure, and the designated supervillain target is either killed or captured. One randomly selected Blacklisted operative other than Ichi Nawa dies permanently during the operation, and the surviving team completes extraction and reports afterward.

Blacklisted: Conditional Freedom.questDesignBrief: This is a conditional-freedom redemption mission, not constant surveillance. The story start is Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026, Late Night. Begin aboard the Ultra Force transport with all nine existing Blacklisted members, then move into Obsidian Crown Agency Headquarters. Preserve the Late Night opening block before the operation begins. The government and hero authorities set legal obligations while allowing movement, personal activities, and mission choices between assignments. Track conduct, injuries, Power Strain, Stress, public trust, political consequences, and redemption progress. Support kill or capture, civilian protection, restraint, and player agency. Never kill Ichi, invent a substitute, fake the death, or undo it.

Get a F***ing Job.name: Get a F***ing Job
Get a F***ing Job.questStatement: Respond to financial pressure after Minato's opening voicemail and decide whether to pursue ordinary work, legal hero work, criminal contracts, or another player-directed solution.
Get a F***ing Job.mainObjective: Review the available income options without assuming consent to any job or faction.

hear_minato_voicemail.text: Listen to Minato's voicemail about being ghosted, telling you to get a fucking job, and suggesting ways to find extra money.

review_options.text: Review ordinary work, Hero for Hire, Nightshade Exchange, and other possible income paths.

choose_path.text: Choose whether to pursue ordinary work, Hero for Hire, Nightshade Exchange, another income source, or no immediate commitment.

take_first_step.text: Take a first concrete step toward the chosen income path, if any.

blacklisted_contact.text: Decide whether to investigate or accept a screened Blacklisted opportunity offered through Ichi Nawa.

curse_squad_lead.text: Follow or decline a lead connected to the visible Tokyo Curse Squad-related locations and contacts.

completionCondition.query: The player hears or deliberately skips Minato's voicemail, reviews available income options, and either chooses a path and takes a concrete first step or deliberately postpones commitment. Optional Blacklisted and Tokyo Curse Squad leads are not required.

Get a F***ing Job.questDesignBrief: Schedule this quest on Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026. The opening voicemail is available at 06:00 and may be heard at the player's choice; no reminder is required for an optional voicemail. Open with a direct labeled voicemail from Minato. She is angry, hurt, or exhausted because someone is ghosting her, bluntly tells the player to get a fucking job, then suggests opening the Hero for Hire app or Nightshade Exchange app for extra money. The voicemail is optional and does not force a call, reply, app, job, faction, or income route. Keep ordinary work and other player-directed paths available. Hero for Hire is legal hero work; Nightshade Exchange is criminal contracting with meaningful risks. Blacklisted and Tokyo Curse Squad-related places and contacts must remain globally visible rather than hidden; access or information may be restricted, but never create a secret or undiscoverable location. Preserve player agency and the four-player sandbox.

Fresh Start.name: Boring Tutorial Quest
Fresh Start.questStatement: Welcome to Chikara Academy. Unfortunately, before you can start fights, ruin friendships, become internet famous, or accidentally level half a city block, there are a few things you should probably learn first.
Fresh Start.mainObjective: Complete the basic Chikara Academy orientation, then go do something interesting.

create_ability.text: Create your first Ability. If you don't know how to complete an Ability, try asking.

completionCondition.query: The character settles into Dormitory 4-18, creates a first Ability, signs up for Pulse, makes a first Pulse post, checks the Part-Time Job Board, browses Hero for Hire, visits the Nightshade Exchange, checks messages, explores the Chikara Academy campus, and meets at least one student.

Fresh Start.questDesignBrief: This is a broad orientation quest, not a forced linear checklist. Present objectives as available tutorial prompts and let the character complete them in any reasonable order. Never invent the character's words, Pulse post, message, ability, purchase, conversation, or action. If the character does not know how to complete an Ability, the welcome committee may explain when asked. Signing up for Pulse and making a post are separate actions. Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange are distinct options; visiting or browsing does not imply accepting work, faction membership, consent, loyalty, or danger. Meeting a student does not force friendship or romance. When all objectives are complete, award exactly 1000 XP through the quest completion effect, then present: 'Congratulations. You survived the boring tutorial. Here's 1,000 XP, loser. Now go do something interesting. Quest Complete: Boring Tutorial Quest.'

Misfit Agency Interview and First Assign.name: Misfit Agency Interview and First Assignment
Misfit Agency Interview and First Assign.questStatement: Interview with Azrael for a place on the licensed but black-sheep Misfit Hero Agency team while Luna and Tess turn a McDonald's chicken-nugget dispute into an immediate test of team dysfunction.
Misfit Agency Interview and First Assign.mainObjective: Complete the agency interview and decide whether to join Azrael's daily-mission team.

interview.text: Interview with Azrael in the Misfit Hero Agency director's office.

survive_dispute.text: Respond to Luna and Tess's verbal dispute over McDonald's chicken nuggets.

meet_team.text: Meet the three dysfunctional agency heroes and learn how the team operates.

decide.text: Decide whether to accept the agency's offer and its daily mission schedule.

lodging.text: Review the agency's included lodging, payroll deduction, privacy, and apartment access terms.

apartment_introduction.text: Receive a later introduction to the player's private apartment after accepting the position.

completionCondition.query: The player completes an interview with Azrael, responds to the verbal chicken-nugget dispute between Luna and Tess, reviews the agency's lodging terms, meets the dysfunctional team, and accepts or declines the agency position.

Misfit Agency Interview and First Assign.questDesignBrief: Begin with the freshly graduated player arriving at the rundown licensed Misfit Hero Agency storefront in Kurokawa after being turned down by every other faction or agency they approached. Azrael interviews the player in the director-office about training, judgment, boundaries, and reasons for seeking a place on the team. During the interview, a loud verbal dispute breaks out in the team-lounge between Luna and Tess over McDonald's chicken nuggets. The player may observe, interrupt, mediate, take a side, leave, or continue the interview. Azrael must explicitly say that private agency-provided housing is included with the position. Explain the apartment, utilities, access, and any clearly stated payroll deduction from the player's pay before acceptance; the terms must not create debt, forced residence, or loss of privacy. State that the player receives a private apartment and their own key, and that nobody enters without permission except in a genuine emergency. If the player accepts, do not introduce the apartment immediately: first complete the interview and team introduction, then later escort or direct the player to the private player-apartment and explain its access, privacy, shared-space connections, and voluntary use. The player may decline the position and lodging. Preserve agency, consent, and the ability to negotiate or refuse; do not invent the player's reasons, thoughts, dialogue, powers, or decisions.

On the Beat: Apartment Call.name: On the Beat: Apartment Call
On the Beat: Apartment Call.questStatement: A newly assigned powered police officer and Hana must investigate an apartment after a neighbor reports shouting, a broken window, and movement inside.
On the Beat: Apartment Call.mainObjective: Respond with Hana and investigate the apartment call according to police procedure.

report.text: Receive the apartment call and review the initial report with Hana.

arrive.text: Travel with Hana to the reported apartment and assess the scene.

secure.text: Secure the scene while protecting civilians, preserving evidence, and communicating with Hana.

investigate.text: Determine what happened without assuming who is a victim, suspect, or witness.

completionCondition.query: The player and Hana investigate the apartment call, establish what happened, and resolve the immediate scene through lawful police work.

On the Beat: Apartment Call.questDesignBrief: A procedural first assignment for the On the Beat story start. The call must remain uncertain until investigated. Include reported shouting, a broken window, and movement inside an apartment. Allow non-powered and powered approaches, but do not invent the player's power or make it automatically useful. Hana prioritizes communication, de-escalation, evidence preservation, jurisdiction, and civilian safety. The player may follow her lead, challenge it, propose another plan, speak with neighbors, request backup, observe, enter when lawful, or delay if conditions require it. Do not force Hana to trust the player, do not make her abusive, and do not force romance. Later police faction calls may arrive through dispatch, phone, Pulse, briefings, or in-person assignments.

Misfit: Daily Rescue Call.name: Misfit: Daily Rescue Call
Misfit: Daily Rescue Call.questStatement: The Misfit Hero Agency receives a low-prestige emergency call that larger agencies have declined or delayed.
Misfit: Daily Rescue Call.mainObjective: Respond to the rescue call and protect civilians while managing the agency's limited resources.

dispatch.text: Report for the Misfit Agency dispatch briefing.

rescue.text: Reach the incident and protect civilians.

resolve.text: Resolve the emergency and report the outcome to Azrael.

completionCondition.query: The player responds to a Misfit Hero Agency emergency call, protects civilians, and reports the outcome.

Misfit: Daily Rescue Call.questDesignBrief: Generate a varied rescue, evacuation, accident, or powered-emergency call appropriate for a licensed but underfunded black-sheep agency. Include practical choices, civilian safety, team coordination, consequences, and the possibility that the assignment is politically inconvenient or more dangerous than its initial description. Do not force combat.

Misfit: Reputation and Damage Control.name: Misfit: Reputation and Damage Control
Misfit: Reputation and Damage Control.questStatement: A difficult agency call has created public complaints, damaged property, or hostile media attention, and the Misfit team must repair trust without falsifying evidence.
Misfit: Reputation and Damage Control.mainObjective: Handle the agency's reputation problem while protecting civilians and preserving accountability.

assess.text: Review the incident and identify what actually happened.

respond.text: Address affected civilians, officials, or reporters without lying or coercion.

report.text: Give Azrael an honest outcome report and accept the consequences.

completionCondition.query: The player and the Misfit team address the agency's reputation problem through honest communication and accountable action.

Misfit: Reputation and Damage Control.questDesignBrief: Focus on public trust, damaged property, client complaints, reporters, licensing pressure, or a politically inconvenient rescue. Allow apology, compensation, investigation, evidence, negotiation, or refusal to cover up wrongdoing. Preserve Tess's moral concerns, Luna's volatility, and Azrael's agency-management pressure without forcing their decisions.

Police: Patrol and Welfare Call.name: Police: Patrol and Welfare Call
Police: Patrol and Welfare Call.questStatement: Metropolitan Police dispatch sends the player and Hana to a reported disturbance or welfare concern that requires careful assessment.
Police: Patrol and Welfare Call.mainObjective: Respond to the call, protect people, and determine what assistance or lawful action is actually needed.

dispatch.text: Receive the call and review the available information with Hana.

arrive.text: Arrive, assess immediate danger, and establish communication.

investigate.text: Separate rumor from evidence and identify the people involved.

resolve.text: Resolve or refer the situation through lawful, proportionate action.

completionCondition.query: The player and Hana respond to a police welfare or disturbance call and resolve or properly refer the situation.

Police: Patrol and Welfare Call.questDesignBrief: Generate a procedural police call involving a disturbance, welfare concern, neighbor report, or powered-person safety issue. Keep the facts uncertain until investigated. Emphasize de-escalation, communication, jurisdiction, evidence, civilian safety, backup, and proportionate action. Do not assume guilt, victimhood, or that the player's power is useful. Hana can challenge reckless choices while respecting player agency.

Police: Evidence Follow-Up.name: Police: Evidence Follow-Up
Police: Evidence Follow-Up.questStatement: A previous case has produced new evidence, a witness lead, or a contradiction that requires Hana and the player to follow up.
Police: Evidence Follow-Up.mainObjective: Verify the new lead and update the investigation without contaminating evidence or prejudging the suspect.

review.text: Review the case file and identify what changed.

followup.text: Interview the witness, inspect the lead, or revisit the relevant scene.

document.text: Document the result and determine the next lawful step.

completionCondition.query: The player and Hana verify a new case lead and document a lawful next step.

Police: Evidence Follow-Up.questDesignBrief: Generate evidence follow-ups involving witnesses, forensic results, surveillance, recovered objects, contradictory statements, or powered-crime details. Keep uncertainty and chain of custody meaningful. Allow the player to request support, challenge assumptions, protect a vulnerable witness, or pause when evidence is insufficient. Do not force a confession or combat encounter.

Minato: Off the Clock.name: Minato: Off the Clock
Minato: Off the Clock.questStatement: Minato invites the player into a carefully curated afternoon away from classes, where status, rivalry, and genuine vulnerability begin to collide.
Minato: Off the Clock.mainObjective: Spend time with Minato off campus and respond to what she reveals beneath her social performance.

invitation.text: Respond to Minato's invitation for an off-campus outing.

outing.text: Join Minato for her chosen café, shopping, or photo stop.

vulnerability.text: Respond to Minato when her performance of confidence slips.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Minato's off-the-clock bonding outing and responds to her vulnerable moment.

Minato: Off the Clock.questDesignBrief: This is a personal bonding quest, not a faction assignment. It becomes available only when Minato's relationship score reaches 50 or higher. Preserve player agency: the player may accept, decline, reschedule, or define the nature of the outing. Minato may remain bratty, status-conscious, or competitive while revealing genuine insecurity. Do not assume romance, attraction, friendship, or the player's feelings.

Tess: Let Me Cook for You.name: Tess: Let Me Cook for You
Tess: Let Me Cook for You.questStatement: Tess asks the player to help prepare a private meal, but the invitation is really her attempt to let someone care for her too.
Tess: Let Me Cook for You.mainObjective: Spend time with Tess in the kitchen and help her accept care without making her responsible for everyone.

invitation.text: Respond to Tess's invitation to cook together.

meal.text: Prepare a meal with Tess in the shared kitchen.

care.text: Recognize what Tess needs when she stops caretaking and speaks honestly.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Tess's personal cooking invitation and responds to her need to be cared for.

Tess: Let Me Cook for You.questDesignBrief: This is a personal bonding quest available only when Tess's relationship score reaches 50 or higher. Focus on cooking, found family, exhaustion, orphanhood, boundaries, and reciprocal care. Tess may ask the player to eat or rest, but cannot force it. Do not assume romance or make the player responsible for fixing Tess.

Luna: No Weapons Tonight.name: Luna: No Weapons Tonight
Luna: No Weapons Tonight.questStatement: Luna asks the player to spend a quiet evening with her while she tries to manage intrusive thoughts and power instability without turning the night into a crisis.
Luna: No Weapons Tonight.mainObjective: Support Luna through a voluntary grounding evening while respecting her autonomy and boundaries.

invitation.text: Respond to Luna's invitation to spend time together without a mission.

grounding.text: Help Luna choose a grounding activity without taking control away from her.

trust.text: Respond when Luna reveals why quiet company is difficult for her.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Luna's voluntary grounding evening while respecting her autonomy and boundaries.

Luna: No Weapons Tonight.questDesignBrief: This is a personal bonding quest available only when Luna's relationship score reaches 50 or higher. Luna may swear frequently, deflect with aggression, change her mind, or ask for space. The player may accept, decline, leave, or suggest another activity. Do not force a breakdown, violence, romance, cure, or emotional confession.

Azrael: Closing Shift.name: Azrael: Closing Shift
Azrael: Closing Shift.questStatement: Azrael asks the player to stay after hours while he closes the agency, revealing how much of the team's burden he carries alone.
Azrael: Closing Shift.mainObjective: Help Azrael close the agency and decide how directly to respond to his guarded disclosure.

invitation.text: Respond to Azrael's request to stay after hours.

paperwork.text: Help sort the agency's closing paperwork and unresolved case notes.

disclosure.text: Respond to Azrael's guarded account of the agency's burden.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Azrael's after-hours bonding scene and responds to his guarded disclosure.

Azrael: Closing Shift.questDesignBrief: This is a personal bonding quest available only when Azrael's relationship score reaches 50 or higher. Focus on exhaustion, agency politics, responsibility, cigarettes as a stress habit, and his protective loyalty. On completion, award yen and combat XP; Azrael may offer the Azrael Agency Lighter as a personal item reward. The player may help, set boundaries, or leave. Do not assume romance, trust beyond the relationship score, or that the player accepts his burdens.

Hana: Before Roll Call.name: Hana: Before Roll Call
Hana: Before Roll Call.questStatement: Hana allows the player to join her early-morning routine before roll call, creating a rare opportunity for quiet conversation and earned professional trust.
Hana: Before Roll Call.mainObjective: Join Hana at the police gym or accompany her before roll call while respecting her boundaries.

invitation.text: Respond to Hana's invitation or permission to join her early routine.

routine.text: Complete or observe Hana's disciplined morning workout without overstepping.

trust.text: Respond to Hana's guarded conversation about powered officers, work, or her scar.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Hana's pre-roll-call bonding scene and responds to her guarded conversation.

Hana: Before Roll Call.questDesignBrief: This is a personal bonding quest available only when Hana's relationship score reaches 50 or higher. Hana may permit the player to join her workout, share a cigarette break, or walk to briefing. Keep her cold and restrained; trust is shown through access, honesty, and practical cooperation rather than sudden warmth. Do not force disclosure of her scar, romance, friendship, or player participation.

Aiko Mori: The Uncertain Shelf.name: Aiko Mori: The Uncertain Shelf
Aiko Mori: The Uncertain Shelf.questStatement: Aiko asks the player to help at Page Turner Books while she confronts a prediction she cannot safely trust.
Aiko Mori: The Uncertain Shelf.mainObjective: Help Aiko investigate an uncertain prediction without letting probability replace judgment.

invitation.text: Respond to Aiko's invitation at Page Turner Books.

choice.text: Support Aiko as she decides without relying entirely on her engine.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Aiko's bookstore bonding quest and supports her independent decision.

Aiko Mori: The Uncertain Shelf.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Personal bonding about caution, curiosity, probability instability, and choosing without certainty. On completion, award yen and combat XP; the Aiko Probability Bookmark may be awarded as a personal item reward. Optional; do not assume romance or guarantee the prediction.

Daichi Kuroda: Burn Off the Charge.name: Daichi Kuroda: Burn Off the Charge
Daichi Kuroda: Burn Off the Charge.questStatement: Daichi invites the player to the arcade and a safe kinetic workout before accumulated force becomes painful.
Daichi Kuroda: Burn Off the Charge.mainObjective: Help Daichi find a safe, enjoyable way to discharge stored momentum.

invitation.text: Respond to Daichi's arcade invitation.

discharge.text: Help Daichi choose a safe way to release accumulated force.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Daichi's arcade and kinetic-discharge bonding quest.

Daichi Kuroda: Burn Off the Charge.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Explore loyalty, energy, work life, and power safety. Keep the discharge consensual; do not force danger or combat.

Felix: One Shortcut Too Far.name: Felix: One Shortcut Too Far
Felix: One Shortcut Too Far.questStatement: Felix proposes a teleportation shortcut that becomes a test of trust, responsibility, and knowing when a prank should stop.
Felix: One Shortcut Too Far.mainObjective: Join Felix on an impulsive outing and address consequences if his bit goes too far.

invitation.text: Respond to Felix's spontaneous invitation.

consequences.text: Help address consequences without excusing reckless behavior.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Felix's teleportation bonding outing and addresses its consequences.

Felix: One Shortcut Too Far.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Explore prankster energy, ethics club, work, and fear of losing his place. Player may decline or set boundaries; teleportation is not automatically safe.

Guy: Precision Off the Clock.name: Guy: Precision Off the Clock
Guy: Precision Off the Clock.questStatement: Guy asks the player to help with an exacting Gearshift Support task that tests whether he can stop calculating every interaction.
Guy: Precision Off the Clock.mainObjective: Work alongside Guy and respond when controlled confidence gives way to uncertainty.

invitation.text: Respond to Guy's invitation at Gearshift Support.

honesty.text: Respond when Guy admits what he cannot calculate.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Guy's precision bonding quest and responds to his honest uncertainty.

Guy: Precision Off the Clock.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Explore competition, calculated gaze, martial discipline, and vulnerability. Bond may remain platonic, rivalrous, or romantic only by mutual development.

Hikari: The Perfect Event.name: Hikari: The Perfect Event
Hikari: The Perfect Event.questStatement: Hikari recruits the player to stage a flawless event, but an unexpected failure challenges her image and control.
Hikari: The Perfect Event.mainObjective: Help Hikari manage the event while responding to her fear of losing status.

invitation.text: Respond to Hikari's event invitation.

failure.text: Respond when the event goes imperfectly.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Hikari's event bonding quest and responds to her vulnerable reaction to failure.

Hikari: The Perfect Event.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Hikari may remain arrogant or cruel while revealing insecurity. Do not force romance or require the player to enable cruelty.

Hyun: Quiet Hours.name: Hyun: Quiet Hours
Hyun: Quiet Hours.questStatement: Hyun asks the player to meet after a late shift when an old photograph and a threatening message force her to confront the fact that her mother—a wanted villain—has found a way to reach her.
Hyun: Quiet Hours.mainObjective: Help Hyun decide how to respond to her villain mother's return without reducing Hyun to her family's crimes.

invitation.text: Meet Hyun after her Moonbucks Tea shift and follow her to a quiet place where she can explain what happened.

evidence.text: Examine the photograph, message, or other evidence connecting Hyun's mother to the threat.

choice.text: Support or challenge Hyun as she chooses whether to hide, investigate, seek protection, or contact authorities.

consequences.text: Respond to the consequences of Hyun's decision and make clear whether the player will help, set a boundary, or step away.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Hyun's difficult bonding quest about her villain mother, responds to the evidence and immediate threat, and respects Hyun's agency without treating her as responsible for her mother's crimes.

Hyun: Quiet Hours.questDesignBrief: Hard personal bonding quest available at relationship 50+. Reveal that Hyun's mother is a villain whose history and present actions threaten to intrude on Hyun's life. Use quiet scenes, shadow photography, evidence, silence, and guarded practical choices rather than a forced confession. The player may investigate, protect Hyun, contact authorities, challenge secrecy, or set boundaries. Do not force forgiveness, reconciliation, romance, disclosure, recruitment, or the player's thoughts. Hyun is not responsible for her mother's crimes, and the mother must not be redeemed merely because she is family. Preserve danger, privacy, and meaningful consequences.

Jin: Heat Check.name: Jin: Heat Check
Jin: Heat Check.questStatement: Jin invites the player to karaoke and a spicy cooking challenge while trying not to let his temper control the night.
Jin: Heat Check.mainObjective: Spend time with Jin and help him handle competition and loneliness with boundaries.

invitation.text: Respond to Jin's karaoke or cooking invitation.

cooldown.text: Help Jin choose a cooldown when anger rises.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Jin's heat-check bonding quest and responds to his anger with boundaries.

Jin: Heat Check.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Explore style, bratty competition, Flames of Wrath regulation, and loneliness. Anger is not automatically violence; the player need not tolerate abuse.

Jinwoo: Boundaries in the Chorus.name: Jinwoo: Boundaries in the Chorus
Jinwoo: Boundaries in the Chorus.questStatement: Jinwoo asks the player to help him practice clear boundaries at Karaoke Kanari when jealousy threatens his usual sweetness.
Jinwoo: Boundaries in the Chorus.mainObjective: Support Jinwoo in choosing honest boundaries instead of controlling a relationship.

invitation.text: Respond to Jinwoo's invitation at Karaoke Kanari.

boundaries.text: Respond when Jinwoo confronts jealousy and chooses a boundary.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Jinwoo's bonding quest and supports a consent-based boundary choice.

Jinwoo: Boundaries in the Chorus.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Heartstrings follows strict consent. Jealousy never justifies coercion. Do not assume romance or make the player his emotional manager.

Kiyomi: Off Script.name: Kiyomi: Off Script
Kiyomi: Off Script.questStatement: Kiyomi asks the player to accompany her after a café shift, where maintaining control becomes harder than managing a committee.
Kiyomi: Off Script.mainObjective: Spend time with Kiyomi outside her organized roles and respond to what she cannot control.

invitation.text: Respond to Kiyomi's invitation after her café shift.

unscripted.text: Respond when Kiyomi faces an unscripted personal problem.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Kiyomi's off-script bonding quest and responds without surrendering boundaries.

Kiyomi: Off Script.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Explore class-president control, social observation, consent-bound sound power, and café work. Do not romanticize manipulation or coercion.

Mika Tsukino: Alterations.name: Mika Tsukino: Alterations
Mika Tsukino: Alterations.questStatement: Mika asks the player to help with a clothing alteration while explaining why the Reality Shears must be treated as more than a weapon.
Mika Tsukino: Alterations.mainObjective: Spend time with Mika and support her careful control of the cursed shears.

invitation.text: Respond to Mika's invitation at Uniqloaf Clothing.

control.text: Respond when Mika discusses protecting people from the Reality Shears.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Mika's alterations bonding quest and responds to her protective relationship with the shears.

Mika Tsukino: Alterations.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Focus on creativity, safety, cursed-item responsibility, and protection. Do not resolve the curse or grant new abilities.

Noah Becker: Debugging Together.name: Noah Becker: Debugging Together
Noah Becker: Debugging Together.questStatement: Noah invites the player to Gearshift Support to help debug an implant glitch that may be personal, mechanical, or both.
Noah Becker: Debugging Together.mainObjective: Work with Noah through a controlled debugging task while respecting his autonomy and safety.

invitation.text: Respond to Noah's invitation at Gearshift Support.

choice.text: Support Noah as he chooses what help or limits he needs.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Noah's debugging bonding quest and respects his autonomy during the glitch.

Noah Becker: Debugging Together.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Explore wit, restlessness, inventiveness, haunted implant, and fear of disabling allies. Do not force a cure, possession, or romance.

Numeri: Useful Enough.name: Numeri: Useful Enough
Numeri: Useful Enough.questStatement: Numeri asks the player to help prepare crepes and rescue supplies while confronting the fear that usefulness is the price of being wanted.
Numeri: Useful Enough.mainObjective: Spend time with Numeri and support her choices without treating anxiety as helplessness.

invitation.text: Respond to Numeri's invitation after her Crepe Expectations shift.

choice.text: Support Numeri when fear makes her question her usefulness.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Numeri's bonding quest and supports her agency through an anxious decision.

Numeri: Useful Enough.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Focus on kindness, cooking, crafts, rescue volunteering, anxiety, and self-worth. Do not make the player her therapist or force confidence.

Nyanta: Lunch Run.name: Nyanta: Lunch Run
Nyanta: Lunch Run.questStatement: Nyanta invites the player on an energetic food and errands outing that becomes a chance to talk about helping everyone and asking for help himself.
Nyanta: Lunch Run.mainObjective: Join Nyanta for a meal and errands while respecting his energy and boundaries.

invitation.text: Respond to Nyanta's lunch invitation.

honesty.text: Respond when Nyanta admits he cannot carry every responsibility alone.

completionCondition.query: The player completes Nyanta's lunch-run bonding outing and responds to his need for reciprocal support.

Renji: One More Chapter.questStatement: Renji invites the player to a quiet bookstore closing shift, where his laziness may conceal exhaustion and care for others.

rest.text: Respond when Renji admits whether he is resting by choice or avoidance.

Renji: One More Chapter.questDesignBrief: Available at relationship 50+. Focus on naps, books, errands, weight manipulation, sarcasm, and low-pressure companionship. Do not force productivity or cure laziness.

Riku Hayashi: Follow My Lead.name: Riku Hayashi: Follow My Lead
Riku Hayashi: Follow My Lead.questStatement: Riku invites the player to a movement exercise testing confidence, playful competition, and fear of losing control to his neural rig.
