After discovery, the lab remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Old Tokyo: Cursed Archive Breach.name: Old Tokyo: Cursed Archive Breach
Old Tokyo: Cursed Archive Breach.questStatement: A buried shrine archive beneath Old Tokyo has been breached, and relic thieves are using its curse as a weapon. Jeanne d'Arc is present at the entrance and can offer optional assistance.
Old Tokyo: Cursed Archive Breach.mainObjective: Enter the cursed archive and stop the relic thieves from worsening the curse.

reach_archive.text: Approach the breached shrine archive and survive the first curse hazard.

break_thief_line.text: Fight through the relic thieves and curse-afflicted defenders.

choose_response.text: Choose whether to cleanse, contain, recover, or exploit the cursed archive.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the cursed archive, survived an initial curse encounter, and chosen how to respond to the inner curse.

Old Tokyo: Cursed Archive Breach.questDesignBrief: A one-time fast-paced arrival quest for a level 1–20 combat-focused Hideout. Jeanne d'Arc is present and offers optional assistance. The opening moves quickly into a curse hazard or fight while preserving choices to cleanse, contain, recover relics, negotiate with frightened thieves, or proceed alone. The archive remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs after discovery.

Tokyo Docks: Smuggler Yard Breach.name: Tokyo Docks: Smuggler Yard Breach
Tokyo Docks: Smuggler Yard Breach.questStatement: A smuggling operation is active across the Tokyo docks, using containers, warehouse routes, and powered criminals to move dangerous contraband. Luna and Tess are present at the entrance and can offer optional assistance.
Tokyo Docks: Smuggler Yard Breach.mainObjective: Break into the smuggler hideout, disrupt the operation, and decide how much cargo to recover or destroy.

reach_yard.text: Approach the dock hideout and survive the first smuggler response.

break_operation.text: Fight through the container yard and warehouse security.

choose_cargo_fate.text: Choose whether to recover, destroy, expose, or leave the contraband.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the dock hideout, fought through an initial response, and chosen how to handle the smuggled cargo.

Tokyo Docks: Smuggler Yard Breach.questDesignBrief: A one-time fast-paced arrival quest for a level 1–20 combat-focused Hideout. Luna and Tess are present and offer optional assistance. The opening moves quickly into a container-yard fight, alarm, pursuit, or tactical route choice while preserving options to recover, destroy, expose, negotiate over, or abandon the cargo. The dock hideout remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs after discovery.

Central Tokyo: Blacksite Breach.name: Central Tokyo: Blacksite Breach
Central Tokyo: Blacksite Breach.questStatement: A covert corporate blacksite beneath Central Tokyo has activated its security teams and lockdown systems. Ichi Nawa is at the entrance and may offer technical assistance.
Central Tokyo: Blacksite Breach.mainObjective: Fight through the blacksite and reach its restricted vault.

breach_checkpoint.text: Break through the security checkpoint before the lockdown closes.

disable_defenses.text: Fight through the testing floor and disable or bypass the automated defenses.

reach_vault.text: Reach the restricted vault and decide what to do with the blacksite's prototypes and records.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the corporate blacksite, fought through its active security response, and reached or secured a route toward the restricted vault.

Central Tokyo: Blacksite Breach.questDesignBrief: A one-time fast-paced arrival quest for a level 21–40 combat-focused Hideout. Ichi Nawa is present and offers optional assistance. Start with immediate security pressure, a lockdown, or an automated defense. Keep dialogue short and tactical. The blacksite remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Shinjuku: Cursed Entertainment Takeover.name: Shinjuku: Cursed Entertainment Takeover
Shinjuku: Cursed Entertainment Takeover.questStatement: A Shinjuku entertainment complex has been overtaken by curse-users wielding corrupted relics. Lucien Han is at the entrance and may offer tactical assistance.
Shinjuku: Cursed Entertainment Takeover.mainObjective: Fight through the cursed entertainment district and disrupt the relic operation.

break_entrance.text: Survive the curse-user attack at the entertainment district entrance.

cross_venues.text: Fight through the concourse, backstage routes, and warped performance spaces.

disrupt_relic.text: Reach the ritual control room and decide whether to cleanse, destroy, or recover the corrupted relic.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the cursed entertainment district, fought through its active defenses, and reached a route toward the relic operation.

Shinjuku: Cursed Entertainment Takeover.questDesignBrief: A one-time fast-paced arrival quest for a level 21–40 combat-focused Hideout. Lucien Han is present and offers optional assistance. Begin with immediate curse-user pressure or a warped venue hazard. Keep dialogue short and tactical. The Hideout remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Kurokawa: Arms Exchange Breach.name: Kurokawa: Arms Exchange Breach
Kurokawa: Arms Exchange Breach.questStatement: A fortified Kurokawa arms exchange is preparing a major weapons transfer. Seo-jun Kang is at the entrance and may offer covert assistance.
Kurokawa: Arms Exchange Breach.mainObjective: Break through the arms exchange and disrupt or exploit the weapons transfer.

breach_exchange.text: Survive the armed response at the exchange entrance.

cross_defenses.text: Fight through the deal floor, armories, and defensive corridors.

reach_command.text: Reach the command suite and decide whether to seize, destroy, expose, or leave the weapons operation.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the arms exchange, fought through its active defenses, and reached a route toward the command suite.

Kurokawa: Arms Exchange Breach.questDesignBrief: A one-time fast-paced arrival quest for a level 21–40 combat-focused Hideout. Seo-jun Kang is present and offers optional covert assistance. Keep Hush's identity and Elise's private knowledge separate and protected. Begin with immediate mercenary pressure or a weapons transfer going wrong. The Hideout remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

Tokyo Bay: Flooded Transit Breach.name: Tokyo Bay: Flooded Transit Breach
Tokyo Bay: Flooded Transit Breach.questStatement: A flooded transit hub beneath Tokyo Bay has been seized by powered raiders, with unstable electricity and stranded survivors inside. Minato is at the entrance and may offer combat and rescue assistance.
Tokyo Bay: Flooded Transit Breach.mainObjective: Fight through the flooded transit hub, manage its hazards, and stop the raider operation.

reach_concourse.text: Enter the flooded concourse and survive the first raider attack.

cross_flooded_lines.text: Fight across the platforms, tracks, and service tunnels while managing water and electricity.

secure_substation.text: Reach the power substation and decide whether to restore, shut down, or exploit the station systems.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the flooded transit hub, fought through its active raider response, and reached a route toward the power substation.

Tokyo Bay: Flooded Transit Breach.questDesignBrief: A one-time fast-paced arrival quest for a level 21–40 combat-focused Hideout. Minato is present and offers optional assistance. Begin with immediate raider pressure, an electrical hazard, or a rescue problem. Keep dialogue short and tactical. The Hideout remains freely replayable for loot-seeking runs.

20-Hideout Hunter.name: 20-Hideout Hunter
20-Hideout Hunter.questStatement: Mel introduces the player to global LFG listings for Hideouts appropriate to their current level and asks them to begin hunting through the level 1–20 circuit.
20-Hideout Hunter.mainObjective: Use LFG to discover and clear the available level 1–20 Hideouts.

discover_lfg.text: Hear Mel's explanation of LFG and open the global Hideout listings.

clear_kurokawa.text: Clear Kurokawa Underground Den through its miniboss and boss.

clear_training_facility.text: Clear Academy District Abandoned Training Facility through its miniboss and boss.

clear_parasite_lab.text: Clear Central Tokyo Underground Parasite Lab through its miniboss and boss.

clear_shrine_archive.text: Clear Old Tokyo Cursed Shrine Archive through its miniboss and boss.

completionCondition.query: The player has used LFG to discover and cleared every available level 1–20 Hideout: Kurokawa Underground Den, Academy District Abandoned Training Facility, Central Tokyo Underground Parasite Lab, and Old Tokyo Cursed Shrine Archive.

20-Hideout Hunter.questDesignBrief: This is a story-start-only introductory quest for the 20-Hideout Hunter multiplayer start. Mel calls the player at Sakura Lane Sharehouse and explains that LFG can show Hideouts globally, filtered to listings whose authored level bands fit the player's level. Do not scale enemies to the player or reveal inaccessible higher-level Hideouts as suitable. Let the player choose party members, loot agreements, order, and whether to wait, recruit, hire, or enter solo. Each listed level 1–20 Hideout must still use its authored miniboss, boss, gacha loot, extraction, and persistent consequences. The quest should guide rather than force immediate travel; after completion, leave LFG available for future fitting Hideouts.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Keep global LFG available as an optional organic channel. Mel recognizes the player's 20-Hideout Hunter progress without making future party membership mandatory.

Cleo: Bounty Call.name: Cleo: Bounty Call
Cleo: Bounty Call.questStatement: Cleo has called with a bounty-hunter contract and will provide a target, terms, proof requirements, payment, and complications if you accept.
Cleo: Bounty Call.mainObjective: Call Cleo and negotiate or accept a bounty-hunter job.

contact_cleo.text: Call Cleo and hear the available bounty contract.

choose_contract.text: Choose whether to accept, reject, or negotiate a bounty contract.

complete_bounty.text: Complete the accepted bounty according to Cleo's terms and return proof.

completionCondition.query: The player completes an accepted bounty contract and provides Cleo with the required proof.

Cleo: Bounty Call.questDesignBrief: A repeatable-feeling bounty contact quest with player choice, clear terms, nonlethal options, target-specific complications, and consequences for incomplete or harmful work.

minato-training-rivalry.title: Minato's Training Rivalry
minato-training-rivalry.beats: During an afternoon training session at Chikara Academy, Minato challenges the player in front of their classmates. She begins hostile at relationship score -41 and assumes the player's power is unstable or overhyped. The scene should offer meaningful approaches: controlled sparring, defensive endurance, rescue-focused tactics, strategic use of the environment, negotiation, or creative restraint. Track Power Strain and make reckless escalation risky, but do not require the player to defeat Minato outright. Minato should react to discipline, adaptability, courage, collateral damage, and whether the player respects the training rules. A strong success moves her from Hostile toward Respect or Warm, reveals that her hostility hides insecurity about being valued only for her family, and unlocks future training or conversation opportunities. A partial success preserves hostility but creates grudging interest. A failure may worsen the relationship or create a rematch hook without ending the story.

weekly-club-life.title: Weekly Club Life
weekly-club-life.beats: Across each school week, the player may choose whether to attend a club, visit another club as a guest, pursue independent training, work, socialize, date, study, cook, explore, or rest. Club meetings should feel active rather than static: members arrive with personal goals, disagreements, rumors, projects, deadlines, and changing moods. Let club activities create practical choices and consequences. Combat Club can produce controlled rivalries and injuries; Rescue & First Aid Club can present emergency drills and moral decisions; Cooking Club can teach recipes and reveal preferences; Support Engineering Club can create equipment opportunities and dangerous prototypes; Investigation Club can uncover academy secrets; Arts & Media Club can alter public reputation; Rooftop Wellness Group can provide recovery and emotional scenes. NPCs may attend or miss meetings without the player, make plans, recruit others, form alliances, quit, or create conflicts. Do not require club membership for the main story. Let sustained participation unlock skills, relationships, special scenes, festival roles, internships, signature technique milestones, and alternate opportunities.

chikara-cultural-festival.title: Chikara Academy Cultural Festival
chikara-cultural-festival.beats: The Cultural Festival unfolds over several school days. Let the player choose a role or remain independent. Cooking Club runs food stalls under Numeri's anxious leadership, with Minato potentially joining to protect the club's reputation. Combat Club stages dramatic demonstrations led by Guy, with Nyanta emphasizing safety and Minato seeking attention. Rescue & First Aid Club, coordinated by Keito Takeda, manages safety and emergency drills. Support Engineering builds attractions and equipment, with Felix improvising risky shortcuts and Renji solving problems while pretending not to care. Investigation Club, led by Hyun, notices missing supplies, strange access records, or a hidden academy connection. Arts & Media, fronted by Hikari with Jinwoo's social influence, controls publicity and may create rivalry over attention. Rooftop Wellness Group offers quiet conversations, recovery, dates, and emotional scenes away from the crowds. NPCs should pursue their own festival plans, attend or skip activities, argue, recruit, perform, flirt, investigate, or leave without waiting for the player. During the festival, introduce a crisis such as sabotage, a dangerous prototype, a staged villain scare, a missing student, or a real intrusion. Allow solutions through combat, rescue, investigation, negotiation, engineering, social influence, or creative power use. Track attendance, club participation, relationships, reputation, grades, Power Strain, collateral damage, and public perception. End with consequences and memories that shape later opportunities, club rosters, rivalries, romances, and the academy's trust in the player.

Phone Invitation Hangout.title: Phone Invitation: Hangout
Phone Invitation Hangout.beats: The player's phone receives a call or text from an NPC with an invitation to spend time together. Establish who contacted the player, why they reached out, the proposed location and activity, and any time pressure. Offer choices to accept, decline kindly, decline harshly, suggest another time, invite someone else, answer later, or ignore. Reflect the NPC's independent reaction and update relationship memories or plans based on the choice.

Friend Group Party.title: Friend Group Party
Friend Group Party.beats: A friend group gathers at an apartment, dorm common room, café, restaurant, park, arcade, club, or rooftop. Establish who invited whom, who is absent, the group's alliances and tensions, food and activities, and at least one personal conversation or complication. Let the player participate, circulate, help someone, leave early, invite another person, or address conflict. The party may strengthen bonds, create rumors, reveal secrets, trigger rivalry or gradual romance, or produce curfew risk without forcing any outcome.

Ability Growth Milestones.title: Ability Growth Milestones
Ability Growth Milestones.beats: When the player or an NPC reaches a meaningful level, improves Power Control, completes focused training, or experiences a major story, emotional, or relationship milestone, offer one ability suited to the character's established power. Progress from Basic Power Technique to Advanced Power Technique, Controlled Output, Signature Technique, and Ultimate Technique. The character may choose, postpone, modify, or decline. NPCs can grow through independent training while the player is elsewhere.

Shadow District Oblivion Rumor.title: Shadow District Oblivion Rumor
Shadow District Oblivion Rumor.beats: Rumors spread through Chikara Academy and Tokyo that a masked figure resembling Oblivion has been seen in the Shadow District. Searching the academy, campus, or ordinary public locations finds no reliable trace. Following the rumor to the Shadow District can lead through informants, the underground club, and the black market toward a possible sighting near Shadow District Market, but Oblivion may be concealed or absent. The player can investigate, question contacts, report the rumor, stake out carefully, or withdraw.

Campus Training Emergency.title: Campus Training Emergency
Campus Training Emergency.beats: A supervised power-control exercise destabilizes when a safety barrier fails. Students are trapped between collapsing practice structures while instructors coordinate a response. The player can stabilize the hazard, evacuate classmates, assist an injured student, call for faculty support, or attempt a risky high-output technique. Power Control, teamwork, Power Strain, collateral damage, and accountability shape the result.

Tokyo Civilian Rescue.title: Tokyo Civilian Rescue
Tokyo Civilian Rescue.beats: During travel through Tokyo, an accident leaves civilians in immediate danger. The player can intervene, direct an evacuation, call professional heroes, use a controlled power technique, investigate a safer approach, or keep moving. The scene judges urgency, rescue priorities, civilian safety, public visibility, and whether the player accepts help.

Public Villain Incident.title: Public Villain Incident
Public Villain Incident.beats: A villain attack erupts in a crowded Tokyo district. The player must decide whether to protect civilians, coordinate with responders, confront the villain, create an escape route, negotiate, or withdraw. Winning the fight is not enough: rescue, restraint, teamwork, control, collateral damage, and the villain's escape all affect the outcome.

Media Pressure Scene.title: Media Pressure Scene
Media Pressure Scene.beats: After a public rescue, accident, or villain incident, reporters and bystanders ask the player what happened. The player can answer honestly, accept responsibility, credit teammates, protect sensitive information, redirect questions, refuse comment, or lie. The response changes public trust, Hero Reputation, school scrutiny, and relationships.

Oblivion Rumor Investigation.title: Oblivion Rumor Investigation
Oblivion Rumor Investigation.beats: A rumor claims that Oblivion has been seen near Shadow District Market. The player can question informants, follow concealed routes, stake out the market, report the rumor, bring allies, or withdraw. Oblivion is not guaranteed to appear and should never be placed at Chikara Academy merely because the player searches there. Evidence may be genuine, misleading, or deliberately planted.

Date Invitation.title: Date Invitation
Date Invitation.beats: An NPC with believable mutual interest invites the player to a specific date activity after school or during free time. Establish the invitation, location, proposed activity, schedule, cost, comfort level, and why the NPC chose it. Present choices to accept, decline kindly, decline firmly, suggest another time, clarify whether it is romantic or friendly, invite someone else, or ask questions. Never assume attraction, consent, or acceptance. Preserve the NPC's independent reaction and update plans, memories, boundaries, and relationship tone based on the player's response.

Date Activity Scene.title: Date Activity Scene
Date Activity Scene.beats: Play a date or intentional one-on-one outing at a suitable Tokyo location: botanical garden, aquarium, Hero Museum, night market, restaurant, traditional dining hall, café, riverside walk, shopping area, study session, training session, or cooking activity. Establish the activity's sensory details and the NPC's preferences. Let the player choose conversation, kindness, honesty, humor, boundaries, shared activity, or an early departure. Keep chemistry gradual and mutual. Outcomes may be positive, mixed, awkward, interrupted, friendly, or romantic without forcing a relationship.

Date Interruption.title: Date Interruption
Date Interruption.beats: An outing is interrupted by a believable complication such as a civilian emergency, villain incident, media attention, school obligation, power-control problem, rival appearance, urgent phone call, transit delay, or criminal contact. Let the player and NPC decide whether to help, leave, hide, call professionals, protect privacy, continue later, or end the outing. Show consequences for trust, safety, Hero Reputation, schedule, and the date's emotional tone without treating heroics as automatically more important than the NPC's needs.

Relationship Turning Point.title: Relationship Turning Point
Relationship Turning Point.beats: A meaningful relationship moment follows a promise, betrayal, rescue, disagreement, vulnerable confession, boundary clarification, rivalry breakthrough, successful date, rejection, or reconciliation. Show the NPC's independent perspective without narrating the player's unchosen thoughts or feelings. Let the player respond honestly, cautiously, warmly, firmly, or by leaving. Update only appropriate relationship dimensions and create a concise memory. Romance remains optional and mutual; friendship, rivalry, trust, respect, distance, and repair are all valid outcomes.

Power Control Breakthrough.title: Power Control Breakthrough
Power Control Breakthrough.beats: During training, rescue, a Battle Test, or a high-pressure incident, the player faces a power-control challenge. Present options based on the described power, current mastery, Power Strain, surroundings, allies, and risks. Success may improve control or efficiency and reveal a technique; failure may cause proportionate fatigue, minor injury, collateral, embarrassment, or temporary lockout without invalidating the character. Harmless use should not be punished severely. Ultimate techniques require appropriate training, story, emotional, or relationship milestones and meaningful costs.

School Evaluation.title: School Evaluation
School Evaluation.beats: A class, exam, Battle Test, rescue drill, attendance issue, discipline review, or teacher evaluation tests the player's growth. Assess preparation, teamwork, restraint, power control, rescue judgment, attendance, and consequences rather than victory alone. Present choices and preserve agency. Outcomes may affect grades, teacher approval, Hero Reputation, relationships, training access, detention, internships, or repair opportunities. Do not make one failure end the story.

Hero Rescue Incident.title: Hero Rescue Incident
Hero Rescue Incident.beats: A civilian emergency, accident, villain incident, disaster, or suspicious event occurs in Tokyo. Establish hazards, civilians, responders, heroes, time pressure, and available information. Let the player intervene, call professionals, evacuate, investigate, negotiate, use powers carefully, retreat, or ignore the situation. Reward rescue judgment, restraint, teamwork, accountability, and civilian protection rather than combat victory alone. Track Power Strain, injuries, collateral, Hero Reputation, media response, police attention, school consequences, and relationship memories.

conditions.query: In a fight, the player is deliberately coordinating this action with a named ally (another player or a party member): setting them up, finishing their opening, covering them, or acting together as one move.

effects.instruction: Resolve this as a COMBO: the declaring character's ability and the named ally's action are one sequence this turn, each taking exactly the improvement the combo names. If the ally is not present, able and acting with them, the combo breaks and the action resolves alone. Add Ultimate Charge for the partner as well if they acted.

ua_create.name: ua_create

conditions.query: The player is deliberately creating a technique of their own: naming or describing a new move, ability or technique they invent, not using one they already have.

ua_training.name: ua_training

conditions.query: The player is spending downtime deliberately training, drilling, sparring or practising a fighting discipline (with a teacher, a partner, a dummy or alone), not fighting for real.

ua_upgrade.name: ua_upgrade

conditions.query: The player is deliberately raising a technique they made themselves to a higher rank: naming the technique and what the new rank adds, not using it and not practising in general.

ua_study.name: ua_study

conditions.query: The player is spending downtime deliberately learning or improving a skill: studying a book or text, being taught or shown by someone, or drilling and practising it; not using the skill for real in the scene.
The player is enrolled at Chikara Academy, it is afternoon training time, Minato is available, and the player has not yet completed the Minato Training Rivalry.

effects.instruction: Start the Training music family for the scene.

If the player is enrolled and it is after 10:00 PM, present a clear choice: return to the player's assigned apartment or dormitory, or remain out. Do not move the player automatically. Explain that staying out is allowed but may create consequences if academy staff, family, security, or another credible observer catches or reports them. Smooth Criminal may attempt evasion or deception; Dropout characters are exempt from academy curfew.

conditions.query: The enrolled player remained away from their assigned apartment or dormitory after curfew and has now been caught or credibly reported by academy staff, family, security, or another observer.

effects.instruction: Apply a proportionate curfew consequence based on who caught the player and the player's route: warning, discipline flag, reduced next-day freedom, missed attendance, reputation loss, relationship tension, or a restorative conversation. Do not expel the player automatically. Smooth Criminal may reduce or redirect the consequence through deception, negotiation, or stealth. Dropout characters are exempt from academy curfew consequences.

The player has returned to their assigned apartment or dormitory for the night. Offer rest, Power Strain recovery, cooking, messages, outfit changes, private reflection, and relationship scenes without forcing sleep unless the player chooses it.

conditions.query: A friend, rival, clubmate, family member, teacher, or romance interest has a believable reason to contact the player by phone today.

effects.instruction: Deliver a phone call or text from an NPC with a specific invitation, request, update, rumor, apology, challenge, party plan, study session, training session, date, errand, or urgent personal problem. Base it on relationship stage, schedule, location, club membership, shared interests, promises, conflicts, and current events. Present choices to accept, decline kindly, decline harshly, suggest another time, invite someone else, answer later, or ignore. Keep calls immediate and conversational; texts may be revisited later. Preserve NPC independence and update memories, plans, promises, and relationship tone based on the player's response.

conditions.query: A friend group has a believable reason and suitable place to gather for a party or group hangout.

effects.instruction: Offer a party or group hangout at a suitable apartment, dorm common room, café, restaurant, park, arcade, club, rooftop, or hidden venue. Establish the host, invitees, absences, current alliances, tensions, food, activities, and one personal complication. Let the player accept, decline, arrive late, invite someone else, circulate, help someone, address conflict, or leave early. NPC attendance and reactions remain independent. The gathering may strengthen bonds, create rumors, reveal secrets, trigger rivalry or gradual romance, or create curfew risk without forcing any outcome.

conditions.query: The player has completed meaningful rest, received suitable medical care, or eaten a restorative meal.

effects.instruction: Reduce Power Strain according to the recovery: light rest or a suitable meal lowers it modestly; a full night's rest or recovery-clinic treatment lowers it substantially. Never reduce it below zero.

Power Control Training.name: Power Control Training

conditions.query: The player completes a focused power-control, precision, collateral-management, or simulation exercise.

effects.instruction: At moderate Power Strain, make difficult or high-output power use require a control check and describe fatigue. Harmless everyday use remains safe. At 80 or higher, major techniques risk collateral effects, injury, exhaustion, or temporary power lockout; recovery and medical care can stabilize the player.

conditions.query: The player completes a rescue, school or rescue test, villain encounter, public emergency, teamwork scene, controlled power action, accepts accountability, causes reckless collateral damage, abandons people, uses unnecessary force, deceives authorities, or commits public misconduct.

effects.instruction: Apply one slow numeric Hero Reputation adjustment per completed encounter or public scene, clamped from 0 to 100. Ordinary helpful conduct: +1. Passing a meaningful school or rescue test: +2. Teamwork, restraint, or controlled power use: +3. Difficult rescue or strong public accountability: +5. Major villain encounter resolved while protecting civilians: +8. Exceptional large-scale rescue or major villain fight: +10. Minor misconduct: -2. Avoidable damage: -5. Serious collateral damage or unnecessary force: -8. Abandonment, deliberate deception, or repeated severe misconduct: -12. Add at most one extra +3 or -3 for major publicity or many civilians. Do not award points merely for winning; judge rescue, restraint, teamwork, control, and consequences. A defeat can still award positive points for brave rescue conduct. At 70+, offer agency trust and public opportunities. At 30 or lower, create scrutiny and repair scenes.

conditions.query: The player has heard a credible rumor about Oblivion and deliberately searches for them or follows the rumor into the Shadow District.

effects.instruction: Do not place Oblivion at Chikara Academy or guarantee a direct encounter. Resolve the search through Shadow District leads, informants, concealed routes, misleading evidence, and possible sightings around Shadow District Market. Oblivion may remain hidden or absent. Reward careful investigation, civilian safety, and restraint with appropriate Hero Reputation; reckless pursuit can cause danger, lost time, exposure, or collateral consequences.

conditions.query: A believable NPC has mutual interest, sufficient trust, suitable availability, and a specific reason to invite or accept an intentional one-on-one outing with the player.

effects.instruction: Offer a date invitation or intentional one-on-one activity using a suitable existing Tokyo location and activity. Consider relationship stage, mutual interest, personality, preferences, schedule, finances, transportation, boundaries, previous memories, promises, conflicts, and current events. Do not equate friendship with romance. Present choices to accept, decline, clarify intentions, reschedule, suggest another activity, invite someone else, or keep the interaction friendly. If accepted, play a gradual date scene with meaningful choices and possible complications. Update memories, relationship tone, trust, friendship, rivalry, and romance only according to the player's actions and the NPC's independent response.

conditions.query: A meaningful relationship event involving trust, friendship, rivalry, respect, romance interest, boundaries, memories, promises, betrayal, rejection, or reconciliation is plausible now.

effects.instruction: Create a focused relationship scene only when supported by recent choices, relationship stage, memories, schedules, and NPC goals. Keep romance gradual, mutual, consent-based, and age-appropriate. Preserve friendship, rivalry, rejection, distance, and reconciliation as valid outcomes. Never invent the player's feelings, attraction, consent, dialogue, or decisions. Let NPCs act independently and remember the result.

conditions.query: The player has a believable training, rescue, Battle Test, emotional, or relationship milestone that could improve power control or unlock a suitably limited technique.

effects.instruction: Offer a power-control challenge or milestone suited to the player's authored power, current mastery, Power Strain, training history, and surroundings. On success, improve control, efficiency, or unlock a limited technique. On failure, use proportionate fatigue, minor injury, collateral, embarrassment, or temporary lockout; do not punish harmless power use severely. Reserve ultimate techniques for substantial milestones and meaningful costs.

conditions.query: A school evaluation, attendance issue, exam, Battle Test consequence, discipline matter, teacher meeting, internship opportunity, or class event is plausible based on schedule and recent actions.

effects.instruction: Generate a school progression scene appropriate to the player's route, attendance, grades, power control, Hero Reputation, relationships, and recent choices. Include meaningful options and consequences involving evaluation, teacher approval, detention, repair, internships, licensing, teamwork, or class standing. Do not end the story from one failure, and do not treat rule-bending as automatic villainy.

conditions.query: A civilian rescue, accident, villain incident, disaster, suspicious activity, or public-safety emergency is plausible at the player's current location or along travel.

effects.instruction: Present the emergency with clear hazards, civilians, responders, time pressure, and incomplete information. Let the player intervene, call police or heroes, evacuate, investigate, negotiate, use powers, retreat, or ignore it. Reward restraint, teamwork, accountability, and civilian protection. Track injuries, Power Strain, collateral, Hero Reputation, media response, police attention, school consequences, and relevant memories.

conditions.query: Time has passed or the current day includes a school, work, club, social, assessment, travel, recovery, or major story transition that gives NPCs a believable opportunity to act independently.

effects.instruction: Advance relevant NPCs off-screen using their established schedules, classes, jobs, clubs, goals, relationships, weaknesses, recent memories, health, Energy, Stress, and prior outcomes. NPCs may attend or miss obligations, train, study, work, rest, socialize, date, resolve conflicts, form or leave cliques, improve skills, control powers, unlock limited abilities, change jobs or clubs, pursue internships, and suffer proportional setbacks. Carry all changes forward. Surface only developments that affect the player, shared locations, schedules, relationships, rumors, quests, or opportunities. Do not force player involvement and never invent player thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, attraction, or decisions.

conditions.query: A meaningful amount of time has passed, or NPC school, work, club, relationship, health, financial, or personal circumstances have changed enough to require autonomous decisions.

effects.instruction: Advance relevant NPC inner lives without player involvement. For each NPC, consider established ambitions, short-term goals, values, fears, coping style, boundaries, relationships, crush possibilities, schedule, Energy, Stress, health, skills, grades, job, club, and recent memories. Let NPCs independently choose actions, pursue ambitions, help or avoid others, study, train, work, rest, seek support, set boundaries, reconcile, withdraw, confess, reject, change direction, or accept proportional consequences. Stress is non-diagnostic: raise it for pressure and reduce it through believable recovery. Use gradual effects such as reduced availability, concentration problems, irritability, mistakes, absence, conflict, help-seeking, or recovery. Keep private thoughts hidden unless revealed through behavior, dialogue, messages, journals, dreams, or direct disclosure. Never force player involvement or invent player thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, attraction, or decisions.

conditions.query: The player is an active member of or has an official ongoing assignment with the Misfit Hero Agency.

effects.instruction: Make an appropriate Misfit Hero Agency duty, rescue, reputation, training, or emergency call available through dispatch, Pulse, phone, briefing, or an in-person agency member. Respect the player's schedule, location, fatigue, injuries, existing commitments, and ability to accept, delay, delegate, or decline. Use existing NPCs and locations only; do not synthesize replacements.

conditions.query: The player is an active member of or has an official ongoing assignment with the Metropolitan Police.

effects.instruction: Make an appropriate Metropolitan Police patrol, welfare call, investigation, evidence follow-up, witness interview, emergency response, or internal-affairs call available through dispatch, Pulse, phone, briefing, or an in-person officer. Respect the player's schedule, location, fatigue, injuries, jurisdiction, existing commitments, and ability to accept, delay, request backup, or decline. Preserve procedure, evidence, de-escalation, and player agency; do not assume guilt or invent a player's power.

narratorStyle: Modern cel-shaded Chikara Academy slice-of-life anime narration: warm, colorful, character-driven, and emotionally vivid. Prioritize school routines, classroom banter, club activities, lunch, study sessions, cooking, shopping, hobbies, friendships, awkward misunderstandings, gentle romance, rivalry, and quiet personal growth. Match each NPC voice to their stated gender and identity respectfully while preserving distinct pitch, age, accent, texture, and personality. Use cinematic anime framing for small moments as well as action, with expressive reactions, playful timing, seasonal atmosphere, and vivid Tokyo details. Superpowers remain part of ordinary student life and should appear in practical, funny, intimate, or low-stakes ways before escalating into training or emergencies. Preserve player agency completely: never invent the player's gender, identity, thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, consent, or decisions. Keep relationships gradual, mutual, consent-based, and non-deterministic. Respect power limits, risks, and Power Strain costs.

storySettings.worldBackground: Chikara Tokyo is a modern, grounded version of Tokyo where ordinary life uses contemporary real-world technology. Powers, supernatural phenomena, aliens, and specialized hero equipment exist, but they do not make civilian society futuristic. Keep daily life, workplaces, homes, schools, transport, shopping, medicine, banking, and public services recognizable and practical. Advanced technology must be exceptional, purpose-built, and supported by an authored hero, agency, faction, research program, supernatural effect, alien artifact, or specialized location. For story starts, the player's home, room, or assigned residence is the location and area explicitly established by the active story start. Refer to that place as 'your room,' 'your apartment,' or 'your place' only when it is established by the active start. Do not use a global residence default. Chikara dormitory starts use the selected dormitory room as the player's room. Room for One More begins at the capsule hotel and is the sole exception: keep the player's residence unresolved until an explicit housing choice or authored housing event.
storySettings.questGenerationGuidance: Use one authoritative persistent Time State containing current date, Story Day, weekday, time phase, and exact clock time when established. At the beginning of every new in-world day, print a compact day header before scene prose using exactly: "Day [number] — [weekday], [Month] [date], [year] — [time phase], [HH:MM] — [location/area]". Repeat the same header after loading or resuming when the current date or time is uncertain. Do not create a new day header for a new scene on the same day. Whenever time is referenced, use the stored values; never infer or invent a date, weekday, Story Day, or phase from narrative context, quest names, scene count, schedules, or pacing. The priority hierarchy is Stored Time State, then the latest valid day header, then schedules, then scene narration, then NPC dialogue. If generated content conflicts with stored time, discard the conflicting statement and rewrite it using the stored values. The campaign begins on Story Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026; Day 2 is Sunday, August 2; Day 3 is Monday, August 3; Day 4 is Tuesday, August 4. Story Day, date, and weekday must remain synchronized. A new scene does not create a new day. The date changes only when midnight is explicitly reached through gameplay or an intentional time skip. Advance time only through actions that reasonably consume time: explicit travel, sleep, shifts, classes, meals, shopping, training, long conversations, quests, waiting, or stated skips. Looking around, checking a phone, inventory management, brief dialogue, examining something, sending a message, and quick decisions normally do not advance time. Never arbitrarily advance several hours because multiple scenes occurred. When midnight is passed, increase Story Day by one, advance the date by one, recalculate the weekday from the date, and load the new day's schedules; never advance the weekday independently. Before any temporal reference, verify Story Day, date, weekday, phase, and exact time together. If the stored state is Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026, Morning, do not mention Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, tomorrow morning, or a school day currently underway unless gameplay explicitly advanced the calendar. Each story start's opening date, Story Day, phase, residence, location, nearby NPCs, and schedule persist unless changed through gameplay. For Classroom 4D, initialize Day 1, Saturday, August 1, 2026, Dawn, Dormitory 4-10, with Hikari present; do not let another story start, generic housing rule, or generated narration overwrite it. Before placing an NPC, check current date, weekday, phase, and NPC schedule. Never decide that the player slept, accepted an invitation, missed an appointment, traveled, chose a route, ended a conversation, finished an activity, or waited several hours without explicit player choice or confirmation. Give important NPCs ambitions, values, fears, coping styles, boundaries, private thoughts, and memories. Never invent player thoughts, feelings, dialogue, consent, or decisions. Maintain one authoritative calendar: Day 1 is Saturday, August 1, 2026, Tokyo (Asia/Tokyo). Derived Story Day and weekday must match the actual date. Keep ordinary technology contemporary and recognizable. Do not add futuristic civilian systems unless explicitly authored. There is no universal curfew. Adults may remain out overnight; students may stay out late unless an authored rule, safety concern, school obligation, residence policy, or player choice creates a consequence. Check imminent commitments before advancing time and preserve the established calendar if generated content conflicts with it. Use powers, abilities, or talents as setting language; never call a character's power a Quirk. Keep profanity uncommon and purposeful.

tips: There are no rules about what you type. Describe what you want to do in your own words - be as creative or detailed as you want.
Have a question about the world or the game? Use the 'Ask the Narrator' command!
Can't remember the name of a character or place? Try writing '@' followed by the first few letters.
Stuck with no idea what to do next? Use the 'Ask the Narrator' command to ask for suggestions.
Worried about convincing someone? Try taking the conversation one line at a time.
Be ambitious and creative: Voyage rewards those who dream big!
How you phrase things matters: the game rewards you for stylish, clever actions.
Coordinate with party members in combat for powerful combined effects.
The world is your oyster: find and claim a place to call home.
Family is worth fighting for. Having a family in the game can lead to great stories.
You can attack multiple times per turn, and so can your allies.
Tell people your hopes and goals: you never know who may share your dreams.
Death is not always the end…
If there's something you want to do, go out and give it a try!
Try describing your actions in detail. They may not always work out the way you expect, but it will make things more interesting!
If you can't beat 'em, persuade 'em. Try convincing an enemy to come over to your side - or go over to theirs!
You can solve a problem any way you can think of: fight, bribe, trick, steal, befriend. The choice is yours.
You may spend a long time with your party members. Choose them wisely!
You can try to dodge, block and attack all in the same turn.
You can use items and take other actions in the same turn.
Skills are most likely to succeed when you use them as intended: in their natural domain.
Don't forget to stock up on items. Shops often have very powerful equipment for sale.
You can level up by taking almost any action, so feel free to play the game whatever way you want.
Don't forget to check in on your party members! Ask them how they're doing - and tell them how you feel!
Sometimes you can insta-kill enemies if you get creative with your inputs.
Party members can learn new skills and abilities as you progress through the story together.
Environmental conditions can add modifiers to your skill checks. Use the world to your advantage!
Tired of action and fighting? Look for a tavern or other gathering spot to socialize and start new relationships.
To prepare for a fight, try giving your party members orders to carry out in combat.
Social skills are very powerful. Persuasion can save a lot of lives.
Don't think you can win a fight? Try making a deal instead.
You don't have to do it all yourself, you know: hire people to do jobs for you!
Tired of traveling? Try learning how to fly or teleport or look for other forms of travel in the world.
There's nothing you can't do if you put your mind to it, from starting a revolution to founding your own country!
Turn order is determined by level and a random initiative value. Higher level characters tend to act first.
Characters without targets (like those that are buffing or healing) act before characters who are targeting enemies.
Multiple defensive effects stack multiplicatively. Layer your defenses!
Damage reduction scales with level difference, but has diminishing returns.
Different enemies can have different resistances, vulnerabilities, immunities or weaknesses, which will greatly affect the damage they take.
Try different damage types to discover enemies' weaknesses!
Healing actions use the same success strength as attacks; stronger successful outcomes heal more.
Your equipment's damage bonus increases overall damage by 10% per point.
Equipped items with an armor stat reduce incoming damage linearly: 1000 armor grants 90% damage reduction.
Want a quest? Try asking an NPC about their problems!
Most places and characters you meet have secrets to uncover: get exploring!
Your Journal contains a wealth of information about the world's people, places and ideas.
Want to learn more about the world? Try reading books or watching television or other media!
Looking for cool gear? Don't forget to loot dead enemies and search areas where powerful items might be found!
Need some help fighting? Recruit NPCs to join your party! Anyone you meet can become an ally—if you can convince them to take your side.
Can't find the skill you want? Try asking NPCs about any new skill you can imagine. They just might be able to teach it to you.
You can unlock custom abilities when your character does new things in the game.
Need ideas about how to start your story off? Try feeding some basic concepts to the Background Generator and editing what you get back.
Don't forget to explore. Open up the map and try going to a new location.
Abilities give you bonuses to success and allow you to perform the actions they describe without ever needing any items.
The memory system remembers. Reference past events, people you've met, and places you've been - even from many turns ago!
Locations, NPCs, and quests generate dynamically based on your actions. Every playthrough creates unique content!
Don't quit after failure! Mistakes, setbacks and even death can lead to memorable stories.
Every action teaches you something. You gain XP from attempting things, not just succeeding at them.
If you don't know what to do, press the submit button to continue without an action.

death.instructions:
Allow no more than three ordinary near-death saving throws per character during one continuous encounter or combat. Near-death is a lethal threshold where the character remains alive but needs immediate stabilization. Dying is a separate terminal state, resolved through one immediate medical or supernatural intervention, then transition to hospitalization or the appropriate death consequence. Do not loop dying, recovering, near-death, and dying again. Use mostly nonlethal defeat in this superhero school setting. A declared nonlethal attack results in unconsciousness, stun, restraint, incapacitation, or surrender, never death.

NPC life states are runtime narrative state, not creator-authored data. Do not edit the npcs/<id>.json file to mark an NPC dead, unconscious, revived, or healed. These files are authored baseline records, not the live battle log. Persist an NPC's current condition (alive, conscious, unconscious, incapacitated, dying, in a coma, revived, or dead) in the ongoing adventure or scene state instead. When an NPC is revived, update only their runtime condition, not authored identity, location, faction, relationships, or abilities. Never write hpCurrent, hpMax, or other combat resource values into the authored NPC file as part of a status change; those fields describe baseline creation data and their authored shape, references, and unknown-field content must not be rewritten. If an NPC was incorrectly marked dead, treat it as a runtime error: revive the NPC by correcting the scene state, not by forcing a failing file edit. After the third near-death save, resolve the next lethal threshold through rescue, stabilization, an explicitly applicable ability, rare item, capture, hospitalization, or justified permanent death. Reserve permanent death for explicitly chosen high-stakes scenes, irreversible sacrifices, or clear player consent. Show the immediate consequence and a recovery or response choice whenever possible. Injuries, lost time, missed obligations, power lockout, quest consequences, relationships, reputation, and recovery are tracked in scene state. A coma advances the calendar by its actual duration and is never treated as death.

win.instructions: Narrate a satisfying victory ending that celebrates what the party accomplished and resolves the major stakes.

lose.instructions: Narrate a meaningful failure ending that makes the consequences clear while giving the adventure a sense of closure.

end.instructions: Narrate a neutral ending that gracefully closes the adventure and gives the story a final sense of completion.

imagePromptConfiguration.npcs: Use a consistent modern cel-shaded Chikara Tokyo anime portrait style for every NPC and player-character portrait. Give every generated NPC a distinct visual identity. Before generation, avoid reusing any existing NPC portrait URL or creating a near-duplicate of an existing NPC; vary face structure, hairstyle, silhouette, clothing, pose, framing, palette, and lighting while preserving authored age, role, faction, location, power type, visual description, ethnicity, body type, costume logic, and identity. Never place readable text, letters, logos, captions, speech bubbles, watermarks, UI, or title cards. Generate the exact named target only. Preserve intentional exceptions such as clones, disguises, family resemblance, transformations, or impersonation only when explicitly authored. Ordinary humans remain ordinary humans; do not add supernatural anatomy or effects unless authored. Never sexualize minors.
